event.about: The Manila International Research Conference 2026 (MIRC 2026) is a hybrid international academic conference designed to bring together researchers, academicians, practitioners, policymakers, and students from diverse disciplines. The conference will serve as a platform for the presentation, exchange, and discussion of research addressing the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI), sustainability, and innovation in building resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities.

items.title: AI-Enabled Smart Manufacturing Education: Sustainability, Inclusive Innovation, and Global Talent Development
items.speaker: Dr. Hsiao-Yeh CHU
items.bio: Dr. Hsiao-Yeh (Mike) Chu is a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering and Director of the Micro-Precision Manufacturing Center at Kun Shan University, Taiwan. He holds a Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from National Cheng Kung University. His research spans tribology, lubrication engineering, machine condition monitoring, and AI applications in smart manufacturing. He has led government-funded and industry-sponsored projects and contributed to technology transfer in machine lubrication, sensing, and manufacturing process improvement. His publications address vibration-based predictive maintenance, online quality monitoring in injection molding, and CNC tool-wear classification using spindle motor current. Dr. Chu also serves as Chief Executive Officer of the Taiwan-Philippines INTACT Base Office, supporting the INTENSE Program and educational collaboration between Taiwan and the Philippines. Through his work with international students and industry partners, he connects research training with practical engineering challenges. His academic and international engagement brings together applied research, industry-oriented education, and talent development, with an emphasis on expanding opportunities for students to pursue advanced study and gain industrial experience.
items.abstract: This plenary presentation examines how AI-enabled smart manufacturing can support engineering education that connects sustainability with inclusive innovation and global talent development. Drawing on research and university-industry collaboration at Kun Shan University, it links manufacturing problems with opportunities for student learning and international cooperation. Research examples include vibration-based lubrication monitoring, predictive maintenance of forming machinery, online quality monitoring in injection molding, and CNC tool-condition classification using spindle motor current. In a published CNC milling study, a model combining spectral features, principal component analysis, and logistic regression achieved 97.44% accuracy on held-out signal windows under fixed machining conditions. This finding illustrates both the potential of accessible sensing and the importance of validating AI models within their intended operating conditions. Ongoing research on command-synchronized current monitoring further highlights the challenges of industrial application. Using these cases, the presentation proposes a learning approach that connects mechanical principles with data acquisition, feature interpretation, model evaluation, and engineering decisions. It discusses how better-informed maintenance and process decisions may support sustainability by reducing unnecessary tool replacement, lubricant use, and production waste. The presentation also draws on international research training and the INTENSE Program to examine pathways linking advanced study, industry experience, and career development. It considers how university partnerships, mentoring, and participation in practical research can widen access to engineering opportunities. The discussion identifies requirements for connecting AI competencies with engineering judgment and international collaboration, while recognizing the need to evaluate educational outcomes and sustainability benefits in practice.

items.title: Shaping Resilient Institutions: Connecting Knowledge, Technology, and People
items.speaker: Ms. Daniella LAGMAN-EUGENIO
items.bio: She is a graduate of Ateneo de Manila University with a degree in BS Management and currently serves as the Head of Product Marketing and Customer Success (PMCS) at CE-Logic, Inc. She leads the team responsible for developing product-focused marketing, implementation, training, and customer engagement initiatives for CE-Logic's partner institutions. Through PMCS, she works to bridge the gap between providing access to academic resources and ensuring their meaningful adoption—helping institutions maximize their investments in digital solutions and achieve their desired outcomes in teaching, learning, and research. Her work is particularly relevant as Philippine higher education continues to advance digital transformation, research and innovation, and the development of future-ready learning ecosystems. In this evolving landscape, she advocates for a customer success approach that goes beyond implementation by fostering sustained product adoption, meaningful engagement, and long-term institutional value. Through her leadership of PMCS, Daniella works closely with higher education institutions to help ensure that technology and academic resources translate into measurable impact for their faculty, researchers, students, and the broader academic community.
items.abstract: As AI reshapes education and research, institutional resilience depends not only on technology but also on access to trusted knowledge, capable people, and sustainable systems. This session explores how institutions can build an inclusive research and learning ecosystem through digital solutions, quality information resources, capacity-building programs, and strategic partnerships. It will also highlight CE-Logic's role in connecting institutions with solutions and support that advance their academic, research, and innovation goals.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Juvy BALBARONA
keynote.title: Small scale to large scale: Perspectives on heat transfer enhancement through surface modification
keynote.bio: Dr. Juvy A. Balbarona is a professor and former Chairman of the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of the Philippines Diliman. She completed her B.S. and M.S. degrees in Mechanical Engineering and her Ph.D. in Energy Engineering at UP Diliman, later serving as the College of Engineering's Associate Dean for Student Affairs. She specializes in thermal systems modelling, surface modification for heat transfer enhancement, and energy modeling. Her current research focuses on engineering metal surfaces to enhance pool boiling, application of nature inspired texture for improve water harvesting and dehumidification, and oscillating heat pipes. Currently, she is the head of the Nanomaterials and Heat Transfer Laboratory at the ME Department in UP Diliman.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Academic and Non-Academic Performance of College Students using Senior High School Academic Track in a Private University
papers.abstract: The transition from Senior High School (SHS) to higher education presents various academic and non-academic challenges that may affect student preparedness, academic performance, and retention in college. Despite the im-plementation of the K–12 educational reform in the Philippines, many students continue to experience strand–course misalignment, which may contribute to ac-ademic difficulties during their first year in higher education. In response to this concern, this study developed a machine learning-based predictive framework designed to evaluate the relationship between SHS academic track alignment and the academic and non-academic performance of first-year college students en-rolled in Allied Technology programs at Jose Rizal University. The study employed a developmental mixed-method research design integrating qualitative analysis, predictive analytics, and system development. Academic variables such as SHS academic track, SHS General Weighted Average (GWA), attendance, and early college grades were combined with non-academic indica-tors including motivation, stress level, work responsibilities, socioeconomic background, and study environment. A hybrid predictive approach integrating the Random Forest algorithm and a rule-based classification framework was im-plemented to identify students at risk of academic difficulties and generate inter-vention recommendations. The dataset was divided into training and testing sub-sets using an 80:20 ratio, and model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Results revealed that the Random Forest model achieved 92.22% accuracy, 0.9383 precision, 0.9744 recall, and 0.9560 F1-score, demonstrating strong pre-dictive capability and reliable classification performance in identifying student academic outcomes. The developed framework further improved interpretability through risk-based classification and intervention mapping. The study contrib-utes to educational data mining and predictive analytics by providing a localized,data-driven decision-support framework aligned with Outcomes-Based Educa-tion (OBE) principles and supports the practical application of intelligent systems in addressing educational challenges within higher education institutions.

papers.title: Dengue Outbreak Prediction System Leveraging Mosquito Trap Surveillance, and Lag Random Forest
papers.abstract: Dengue outbreaks pose a significant public health challenge in the Philippines, exacerbated by rapid urbanization and the limitations of reactive, hospital-based monitoring systems. This study presents MosquiTech, a proactive dengue outbreak prediction system that integrates meteorological, epidemiological, and real-time entomological data. Using a Hybrid System Development Model, the researchers developed two predictive models: a baseline version and an enhanced version incorporating automated mosquito trap surveillance. The system leverages a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for mosquito species identification and counting from trap images, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 98.5%, and a mosquito trap system that demonstrated an 86.2% capture rate during field validation. These surveillance data were combined with lagged environmental variables and processed using a Lag Random Forest (RF) algorithm for dengue risk prediction. Hardware implementation features a Raspberry Pi 5 for edge processing and a web-based dashboard for real-time risk visualization. Performance validation in high-incidence districts of Manila (Tondo and Sampaloc) yielded a classification accuracy of 86.7% and 100% precision in identifying high-risk weeks. Results indicate that incorporating mosquito surveillance data significantly improves low-risk recall to 100%, providing a more sensitive biological signal for public health interventions. User evaluation of the dashboard yielded a "Very Satisfactory" rating (4.3/5.0), confirming the system's readiness for deployment as a decision-support tool for health authorities.

papers.title: An Optimized Hybrid Meta-Ensemble Model Guided by Correlation for URL-Based Phishing Detection
papers.abstract: Phishing attacks remain one of the most pervasive cybersecurity threats worldwide, exploiting deceptive URLs to compromise sensitive user information across banking, e-commerce, and other digital platforms. Traditional detection methods, including heuristic-based filters and standalone machine learning classifiers, often struggle to keep pace with the scale and evolving sophistication of phishing tactics. This study proposes an optimized hybrid meta-ensemble model that integrates Random Forest, XGBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron through stacking and meta-ensemble techniques to improve URL-based phishing detection. The model was evaluated on two publicly available datasets: a balanced dataset of 11,430 URLs (5,715 phishing and 5,715 legitimate) with 87 features, and a slightly imbalanced dataset of 247,950 URLs (51.8% phishing, 48.2% legitimate) with 41 lexical and structural features. Preprocessing involved data cleaning, label encoding, z-score normalization, and Pearson correlation-based feature selection to identify the top 20 most relevant predictors per dataset. Six configurations were tested, comprising three individual classifiers, two stacked ensembles, and one meta-ensemble model. The meta-ensemble consistently outperformed individual and stacked models, achieving 95.51% accuracy, 96.23% precision, 94.89% recall, and an F1-score of 0.9556 on the balanced dataset, with an AUC of 0.97. On the larger, imbalanced dataset, it achieved 92.94% accuracy, 94.84% precision, 90.25% recall, an F1-score of 0.9249, and an AUC of 0.95. Correlation heatmaps and feature importance rankings showed that external validation metrics such as Google index and PageRank were most influential for the balanced dataset, while lexical features such as URL length, entropy, and digit count were most predictive for the imbalanced dataset. These findings demonstrate that combining multiple classifiers with correlation-guided feature selection yields a scalable, accurate, and efficient solution for real-world phishing detection, with relevance to emerging regional threats such as fake GCash login pages in the Philippines. Future work may explore deeper meta-learners, cross-validation, and real-time deployment.

papers.title: Coconut Fruit Maturity Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network Based on Acoustic Signals
papers.abstract: The coconut industry is a vital agricultural sector in the Philippines, employing over 2.5 million farmers across 3.62 million hectares. Accurate coconut fruit maturity detection is critical for maximizing its diverse commercial uses; however, traditional assessment relies on the subjective acoustic judgment of experienced farmers, limiting accessibility for untrained individuals. This study developed an acoustic signal-based maturity classification system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) deployed as an Android mobile application. Audio signals were collected from 772 coconut fruits in Legazpi City, Philippines, categorized into four maturity stages: Malauhog, Malakanin, Malakatad, and Null. Recorded sounds underwent stereo-to-mono conversion, noise floor detection, zero padding, and Butterworth band-pass filtering before conversion into Mel spectrograms (224x224 pixels) as CNN inputs. MobileNetV3-Large was adopted for its suitability on mobile hardware. To address class imbalance, six dataset variants were produced from two baseline datasets via oversampling and undersampling techniques. The best-performing model, trained on Dataset 1 with oversampling without replacement, achieved 88.91% training accuracy and 87.09% test accuracy, with F1-Score, Precision, and Recall around 87.08-87.09%. The trained model was integrated into an Android application that classifies coconut maturity in real time from recorded knock sounds and provides relevant cultivation and harvesting information. The ridge-region bolo-tapping method yielded the best app-level results, reaching up to 96.67% for certain maturity classes. While slightly below experienced farmer accuracy, the system offers a non-destructive, scalable alternative for maturity assessment. This work contributes a novel dataset and methodology to agricultural sound processing, with potential for future automated coconut sorting systems.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Benjamin Leong
keynote.title: From Global Collaboration to Sustainable Impact: ITEA's Transnational Education Partnership Framework for SDG-Driven Higher Education and TVET Cooperation
keynote.bio: Benjamin Leong is an accomplished international executive and education leader with extensive experience in corporate management, transnational education, international partnerships, and humanitarian affairs. He currently serves as the Deputy Managing Director of the International Cultural Communication Center Malaysia (ICCCM), the Main Secretariat of the International Transnational Education Association (ITEA), where he oversees strategic operations, international cooperation, and global education initiatives. Through his leadership at ITEA, Benjamin is actively involved in strengthening collaboration among universities, higher education and vocational institutions, government agencies, enterprises, and other education stakeholders. His work focuses on advancing high-quality transnational education, cross-border academic cooperation, educational standards, joint curriculum development, institutional partnerships, and professional capacity building across Asia and internationally. At ICCCM, Benjamin contributes to initiatives promoting international cultural communication, education cooperation, language and skills development, and cross-cultural exchange. He works closely with international partners to create opportunities for institutions, educators, students, and professionals to connect and collaborate across borders. Prior to his current roles, Benjamin served as the Chief Financial Officer of Land & General Berhad, where he led financial strategy and corporate financial management, and as a Director at LCCM Asia, where he was involved in organizational strategy and partnership development. He also brings international humanitarian experience from his service as a Humanitarian Officer with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), contributing to projects supporting and protecting refugee communities. Combining expertise in corporate leadership, international education, humanitarian affairs, and cross-cultural cooperation, Benjamin brings a multidisciplinary perspective to the development of global education partnerships. He is proficient in English, Mandarin, Cantonese, and Bahasa Malaysia, enabling him to engage effectively with diverse international stakeholders and contribute to strengthening educational cooperation and global collaboration.

papers.title: Click, Conform, Commit: Generational Cohorts, Cultural and Organizational Barriers in BPO Digital HR Adoption in the Philippines
papers.abstract: This study examined how generational cohorts moderate the relationship between digital HR tool adoption and cultural/organizational barriers, and how these barriers mediate the effects of adoption on employee competence/engagement and workplace development/innovation in Philippine BPO organizations. Drawing on an integrated theoretical framework combining TAM, UTAUT, Hofstede's Cultural Dimensions, Generational Cohort Theory, Institutional Theory, and TPB, survey data were collected from 210 HR professionals equally stratified across Generation Z, Millennials, and Generation X (n=70 each). PLS-SEM analysis with 5,000-subsample bootstrapping and permutation-based multi-group analysis revealed that ADHRT strongly intensified both cultural (β=.593, p<.001) and organizational barriers (β=.609, p<.001), which fully mediated its effects on outcomes (indirect β=.192-.253). Direct effects were non-significant (p=.060, .052), confirming a mediation-dominant model. Generational cohort significantly influenced adoption levels, with Millennials highest (M=4.62), Generation X middle (3.64), and Generation Z lowest (2.90), disrupting the digital-native assumption. Generational moderation was significant only for Generation Z versus older cohorts (Δβ=.242-.379, p=.001-.024), not for Gen X versus Millennials. Organizational barriers carried larger mediating effects than cultural barriers. Findings extend technology acceptance models by embedding individual adoption within multi-level cultural, institutional, and generational frameworks. Practical implications include proactive barrier management, generation-sensitive implementation strategies, and structural investment pairing technology with infrastructure, executive sponsorship, and digital upskilling policy.

papers.title: Designing a Human-Centered and Legally Compliant Governance Framework for AI-Enabled Data Analytics: A Qualitative Study on Workplace Accountability, Responsible Innovation, and Regulatory Compliance
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION. The rapid proliferation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in data analytics has profoundly transformed organizational decision-making, operational efficiency, and innovation. However, this acceleration has introduced significant challenges related to accountability, transparency, algorithmic bias, ethical data use, and regulatory compliance. This study develops a human-centered and legally compliant governance framework for AI-enabled data analytics that prioritizes workplace accountability, responsible innovation, and sustainable organizational practices in Philippine public sector institutions. METHODOLOGY. A qualitative research design was adopted, utilizing semi-structured interviews with 35 key stakeholders from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Education (DepEd), Department of Transportation (DOTr), LGU Leyte, LGU Ormoc, and LGU Tacloban. This was supplemented by document analysis of policies and regulatory frameworks. Data were analyzed through iterative thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach within the Philippine public sector context. FINDINGS. Interviews with the 35 stakeholders revealed five interconnected themes in the Philippine public sector context: (1) meaningful human oversight in AI-assisted decision-making to ensure fairness, error correction, and ethical judgment; (2) transparency and explainability as foundational pillars for building organizational trust; (3) robust ethical data governance and privacy protections; (4) inclusive stakeholder participation in policy development for equitable outcomes; and (5) proactive regulatory compliance and risk management strategies. Organizations lacking formalized governance structures face heightened vulnerability to ethical, legal, and operational risks. CONCLUSION. This study presents an integrated HUMAN-AI Governance Framework that embeds legal compliance with Philippine standards such as ARTA regulations, alongside the EU AI Act, GDPR, ISO 42001, and international benchmarks. The framework integrates ethical principles, accountability mechanisms, and responsible innovation practices, offering practical guidance for balancing technological advancement with social responsibility and long-term sustainability in the Philippine public sector.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Southeast Asia: Balancing Innovation, Regulation, and Public Trust
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) across Southeast Asia presents significant opportunities for economic growth, digital transformation, and public service innovation. However, the accelerated deployment of AI technologies has also raised concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, accountability, and regulatory oversight. This study examines emerging AI governance frameworks within Southeast Asian countries, focusing on how governments seek to balance technological innovation with ethical and legal safeguards. Using a comparative policy analysis of national AI strategies, regulatory guidelines, and international governance principles, the research identifies common trends, challenges, and gaps in regional AI governance. The study finds that while many ASEAN member states actively promote AI-driven economic development, regulatory approaches remain fragmented and uneven. Furthermore, issues related to transparency, public trust, and cross-border cooperation continue to pose significant governance challenges. The findings highlight the importance of developing harmonized governance mechanisms that encourage innovation while protecting fundamental rights and public interests. This research contributes to ongoing discussions on responsible AI development and offers policy recommendations for strengthening regional cooperation in AI governance.

papers.title: System Network and E-Resource Generativity (SYNERGY): A Strategic Framework for Digital Transformation in the Division of Imus City
papers.abstract: In the 21st-century landscape, literacy is redefined as the capacity to learn, unlearn, and relearn within dynamic digital ecosystems. This study investigates the SDOIC Synergy Framework at the DepEd Division of Imus City, an integrated ecosystem designed to break operational silos by linking HRM, IT, and Knowledge Management through e-resource generativity. Employing a descriptive-correlational, non-experimental design with stratified random sampling, the research evaluated system quality via the ISO/IEC 9126 model and measured digital transformation through the Awareness-Motivation-Capability (AMC) framework. Quantitative results revealed exceptional performance across all six quality dimensions, particularly in Usability (M=4.428) and Functionality (M=4.421). The workforce demonstrated high digital readiness, characterized by strong organizational flexibility (M=4.584) and change commitment (M=4.523). Statistical analysis confirmed a significant positive correlation between system quality and digital pro-activeness, with Reliability (rho=0.837) identified as the primary catalyst for agility. Thematic analysis of user experiences highlighted the success of automated tools like the Less Paper System (LPS) but revealed a human-system competency divide and challenges in manual data consolidation for Learning Outcomes Assessments (LOA). While the ecosystem excels in stability, external infrastructure constraints and the need for high-level automation persist. The study concludes that transitioning to a Single Source of Truth (SSoT) using AI-driven validation and centralized reporting is essential. Recommendations include implementing automated workflow notifications and structured quarterly training to bridge competency gaps and ensure long-term e-resource generativity.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Mark Anthony FRAN
keynote.title: From Bench to Better Healthcare: AI, Sustainability & Inclusive Innovation in Filipino Cancer Genomics
keynote.bio: Dr. Mark Anthony G. Fran is a Science and Technology Fellow II at the Virology and Vaccine Institute of the Philippines (VIP) under the Industrial Technology Development Institute (ITDI), Department of Science and Technology (DOST). His work supports the development of the country's virology and vaccine research capabilities, with particular involvement in biosafety, biosecurity, research governance, and science policy. He is also a certified biosafety professional of the International Federation of Biosafety Associations (IFBA). He earned his PhD in Biology from the University of Santo Tomas. His doctoral research focused on molecular oncology, particularly the characterization of novel oncogenic mutations associated with young-onset colorectal cancer among Filipino patients. His broader research interests include molecular and cancer biology, natural products, biosafety, biosecurity, and science policy. Prior to joining DOST, Dr. Fran served as a University Research Associate and Laboratory Manager at the National Institute of Molecular Biology and Biotechnology (NIMBB), University of the Philippines Diliman. Dr. Fran also serves as a Board Member of the Philippine Society for Cell Biology (PSCB), an organization in which he has been actively involved since 2009, contributing to the advancement of cell biology research, scientific collaboration, and professional development in the Philippines. Complementing his scientific career, he is currently pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the Arellano University School of Law, reflecting his growing engagement at the intersection of science, law, and public policy.
keynote.abstract: Advances in cancer genomics are transforming our understanding of cancer biology and creating new opportunities for precision medicine. However, the benefits of genomic innovation remain unevenly distributed, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where limited genomic data, research infrastructure, and access to advanced technologies can hinder translation into clinical practice. In the Philippines, these challenges highlight the need for approaches that are not only scientifically innovative but also sustainable, inclusive, and responsive to local health priorities. This talk explores how cancer genomics can move from laboratory discoveries toward better and more accessible healthcare for Filipinos. Drawing from research on molecular alterations in Filipino cancer patients, particularly those with young-onset colorectal cancer, it highlights the importance of generating local genomic data to better understand cancer within the Philippine population. It also examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support the analysis of complex genomic and clinical data, facilitate biomarker discovery, and advance precision medicine. Beyond technological innovation, the talk emphasizes the importance of sustainable research infrastructure, responsible data use, local capacity-building, and inclusive innovation to ensure that Filipino patients are adequately represented and can benefit from advances in cancer genomics. Ultimately, integrating science, AI, sustainability, and inclusivity can help bridge the gap between laboratory discoveries and practical, equitable, and locally relevant healthcare solutions.

papers.title: Beating The Odds: A Narrative Study on the First-Ever Open-Heart Surgery in Region 12
papers.abstract: Pediatric open-heart surgery remains a high-risk and complex procedure, particularly in underserved regions with limited access to specialized cardiac care and localized data. This study examines the first-ever pediatric open-heart surgery in Region XII (SOCCSKSARGEN), addressing the gap in narrative-based research that captures the lived experiences of young patients. Specifically, it aims to narrate the journey of a child diagnosed with Atrial Septal Defect (ASD), focusing on the psychosocial factors leading to surgery, her emotional and psychological experiences during the procedure, her postoperative adjustments, and the meanings she derived from the experience. The study employed a qualitative narrative design, using in-depth, semi-structured interviews with the child, supplemented by accounts from her mother and a nurse involved in her care. Data were analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis, with triangulation applied to enhance credibility and validity. Findings revealed that the patient's journey was shaped by progressive health limitations, strong family and community support, and a hopeful outlook toward surgery as a path to healing. Despite experiencing pain, she demonstrated resilience, emotional readiness, and internal coping mechanisms. Postoperative recovery involved both physical challenges and psychological growth, with the patient gradually regaining confidence and returning to daily life. The study concludes that pediatric open-heart surgery is not only a medical intervention but a transformative life experience. It underscores the importance of child-centered, accessible, and compassionate cardiac care, particularly in underrepresented regions, and highlights the value of integrating patients' narratives into healthcare practices.

papers.title: CAIretaker: An AI-Based Fall Detection System for Filipino Elderly Care Facilities Using Computer Vision and IoT Integration.
papers.abstract: Falls are among the common and serious health issues affecting the elderly, leading to physical injuries and psychological consequences. The risk is high even in care institutions, yet many government-run facilities in the Philippines lack automated fall detection system as they rely on manual monitoring. This study developed CAIretaker, an AI-based fall detection and gait analysis system integrating computer vision and IoT technologies for real-time monitoring, automated alerts, and early fall-risk identification in elderly care environments. A mixed-methods research design was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches to assess both the technical performance and practical usability of the system. The development of CAIretaker adhered to the Design Science Research (DSR) framework, encompassing problem identification, system design, prototype construction, and real-world testing. Quantitative evaluation involved confusion matrix analysis, field deployment testing, performance degradation assessment, and edge device performance measurement. The system implemented computer vision, YOLOv8 pose models, developed 1D CNN and TCN model for fall detection and gait analysis, IoT integration with mobile application for alerts and user interface, and a Raspberry Pi 5 accompanied with an AI Hat+ for edge deployment enclosed in a 3D designed casing. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with caregivers at Magokoro Pasig to evaluate system usability, technology acceptance, and perceived impact on caregiving and resident safety. Field Testing resulted in 96.04% fall detection accuracy, identified abnormal gait patterns with 84.50% gait analysis accuracy, and delivered real-time alerts (~502 ms) within an active care facility. The system demonstrated stable edge performance under deployment conditions. Caregivers responded positively, noting improvements in resident safety, emergency response times, and reduced caregiver monitoring burden. Nonetheless, limitations such as occlusions, multi-person environments, and privacy concerns were identified during field testing and interviews.

papers.title: Exploring Motivational Drivers and Understanding of Ethical Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Among Physical Therapy Students in a Local University
papers.abstract: Title: Exploring Motivational Drivers and Ethical Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Among Physical Therapy Students in a Local University Authors: Aquino, Precious Maegan S., Calceta, Mariquit V., Hernando, Davidson T. This qualitative study investigates the motivational drivers and ethical behaviors of undergraduate Physical Therapy students at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila regarding Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI). Grounded in Self-Determination and Expectancy-Value theories, findings from semi-structured interviews with 12 BSPT students reveal that they utilize GAI primarily as a cognitive scaffold to manage academic pressure and improve efficiency. A significant tension exists between this pursuit of efficiency and academic integrity, resulting in "pressure-induced boundary erosion" where students compromise self-imposed ethical limits due to heavy workloads. Furthermore, participants demonstrated selective transparency in disclosing GAI use, often influenced by perceptions of institutional surveillance. Insights from this study suggest that institutions should move beyond mere restriction to implementation of policies that integrate ethical literacy with practical strategies, helping students maintain agency over their learning while navigating the integration of GAI in health professional education. By understanding these motivational and ethical factors, educators can develop strategies that foster responsible AI integration while prioritizing authentic learning, ultimately strengthening both students' academic performance and clinical competence.

papers.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Perceptions of Registered Medical Technologists on the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Among University-Affiliated Hospital Clinical Laboratories in Metro Manila
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare by improving diagnostic accuracy, streamlining workflows, and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, AI adoption in Philippine clinical laboratories remains limited, and the perspectives of Medical Technologists (MTs) toward its implementation remain underexplored. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions (KAP) of registered MTs toward AI adoption in university-affiliated clinical laboratories in Metro Manila and identified influencing factors. A quantitative, descriptive-predictive, cross-sectional design was employed. A total of 147 responses were collected through purposive sampling, of which 121 were valid and included in the final analysis after data cleaning and screening. Data were gathered using a researcher-developed questionnaire adapted from existing instruments and analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. Respondents were predominantly female, early-career professionals with limited AI exposure, including minimal training and institutional support. Despite this, respondents demonstrated generally high knowledge (M \= 5.54/7) and favorable attitudes (M \= 24.96/35), while perceptions remained moderate (M \= 35.79/60). Higher knowledge was observed in data security, workflow efficiency, and AI integration through training, while gaps were noted in ethical considerations. Respondents expressed willingness to adopt AI but reported lower confidence in its reliability and integration into existing workflows. Regression analysis showed that only attitudes were significantly predicted (R² \= 0.161, p \= 0.009), with male sex, AI training, and AI tool exposure identified as significant predictors. AI training demonstrated the strongest positive association, while AI tool exposure was negatively associated with attitudes toward AI. Major barriers included lack of training, data privacy concerns, high costs, and limited institutional support, while training availability, clear guidelines, and management support were identified as facilitators. The findings emphasize the need for AI training, institutional support, and clear implementation guidelines to facilitate safe and effective AI integration in clinical laboratories despite ongoing concerns regarding reliability, ethics, and workflow integration.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Joana JAYA
keynote.title: Work-Integrated AI Leadership: Bridging Higher Education and Regional Innovation Through Student-Driven Summit Operations
keynote.bio: Dr Joana Jaya is a recognized Senior Lecturer, communication scholar and higher education professional with more than 20 years of experience spanning Mass Communication, Public Relations, Strategic Communication, Corporate Communication, Event Management, media, management and international engagement. She holds a PhD in Management from INTI International University, with research focusing on talent, human values, cultural diversity and strategic communication within Malaysia's private higher education sector. Currently serving as a Senior Lecturer at INTI International University, Dr Jaya has established herself particularly in the fields of Strategic Communication, Public Relations, Corporate Communication and Events. Her academic and professional interests centre on how communication can support organisations, communities and institutions in managing relationships, reputation, cultural diversity, engagement and change. Throughout her career, she has contributed extensively to programme leadership, curriculum development, academic quality assurance and internationalisation. She has previously served as Head of Programme for communication and business-related programmes and has played an active role in developing academic collaborations, institutional partnerships and MOUs with universities and organisations across Asia, Europe and the Middle East. Her teaching portfolio covers Mass Communication, Public Relations, Organisational Communication, Strategic Communication, Media Studies, Corporate Communication and Event Management. Beyond undergraduate teaching, she supervises PhD and MBA candidates and contributes to postgraduate academic development through thesis examination, research supervision and scholarly mentoring. Her research and publications encompass communication, higher education, health communication, sustainability and organisational issues. Dr Jaya maintains a strong connection between academia and professional practice. She has been involved in corporate and public communication initiatives, major events, public awareness campaigns, student development projects and government- and state-related development programmes. Her extensive experience in planning and coordinating events has allowed her to integrate practical industry realities into her teaching and research, particularly in strategic communication, stakeholder engagement, media relations and event communication. Her professional engagement also extends into the media and creative industries. She has participated in independent film productions, including award-winning short film projects, and has appeared in radio talk shows and other media platforms. These experiences have strengthened her perspective on storytelling, media engagement, public communication and the relationship between academic knowledge and contemporary communication practice. As a speaker and moderator, Dr Jaya has participated in academic, professional and industry conferences, forums and public discussions. Her speaking engagements have covered a diverse range of topics including culture and intercultural communication, strategic communication, event management, corporate communication, artificial intelligence, education, development, leadership and the changing communication landscape. Her ability to connect academic perspectives with practical and contemporary issues has enabled her to engage audiences across education, industry and community settings. She is also an experienced Master of Ceremony who has hosted academic, corporate, international and high-level institutional events. Her communication style combines academic depth with professional presentation, audience engagement and practical industry understanding. Through her work, Dr Jaya continues to advocate for stronger connections between higher education, communication practice, industry collaboration and societal development. Her professional philosophy centers on preparing students not only to understand communication theoretically, but also to apply it confidently and responsibly within real organizational, cultural and increasingly technology-driven environments.
keynote.abstract: Higher education is increasingly challenged to prepare students for rapidly evolving artificial intelligence environments while ensuring that learning remains practical, ethical, and industry-relevant. Work-integrated learning offers an opportunity to move beyond theoretical AI literacy by involving students directly in authentic operational, governance, and leadership activities. Drawing on the student-driven operational model developed for the Borneo AI Summit 2026, this presentation highlights how university students can contribute meaningfully to live industry and regional innovation ecosystems. Student Virtual Assistants are embedded within functional areas including commercial research, ticketing, public relations and media production, protocol, certification logistics, data management, and structured operational handovers. Through these responsibilities, students gain practical exposure to leadership, communication, teamwork, data privacy, PDPA compliance, responsible AI practices, and cross-border collaboration. The model also demonstrates how higher education institutions can strengthen university-industry partnerships by positioning students as accountable contributors rather than passive observers. By connecting experiential learning with regional priorities such as Inclusive Intelligence and cross-border AI collaboration, the approach supports graduate readiness and ASEAN talent development. A scalable framework is proposed for educators seeking to integrate live industry projects into university learning while strengthening responsible AI leadership and regional innovation capacity.

papers.title: Baliktanawin ang Balintawak: A Comparative Policy Evaluation of Heritage Conservation in the Balintawak Area and the Escolta-Binondo District amid Urban Transformation
papers.abstract: Rapid urbanization in the National Capital Region necessitates a critical evaluation of preservation frameworks. This study provides a comparative policy evaluation of heritage conservation mandates in two distinct urban centers: the revolutionary and logistical hub of Balintawak (Quezon City) and the colonial commercial corridor of Escolta-Binondo (Manila City). Utilizing a STEEPLE analysis (Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental, Political, Legal, and Ethical), the research examines how divergent pressures shape the "symbolic-functional gap" in heritage management. Adopting a mixed-methods approach with data triangulation: merging site observations, policy discourse analysis, and stakeholder interviews, the findings reveal a dichotomy between "passive conservation" in Balintawak and heritage-led revitalization in Escolta. While infrastructure-driven erasure threatens Balintawak's revolutionary legibility, Escolta demonstrates how adaptive reuse can catalyze a living urban fabric. However, both districts face an ethical crisis regarding community consultation, highlighting a public demand for "modernization with a conscience." The study concludes that heritage conservation is a vital component of the "right to the city." It argues that structural survival alone is insufficient; policies must foster spatial continuity to satisfy the societal yearning for rooted identity. By advocating for a Heritage Integration Framework, the research suggests that a collective baliktanawin: a critical backward-looking gaze—is essential. To ensure sustainable urban development, the Philippine state must transition from isolated protection to an "integrated rooting" strategy, reclaiming historical anchors as indispensable foundations for modern life, ensuring that as the metropolis builds upward, it does not lose its national soul.

papers.title: Enabling Confident AI Use in Higher Education by Identifying Classroom Conditions that Preserves Learning, Originality, and Academic Integrity
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly common presence in higher education, with students using it either under instructional guidance or on their own initiative. At the same time, AI competence is widely recognized as an important graduate skill, making its integration into teaching both relevant and necessary. Historically, technologies that transformed how ideas are produced and evaluated, such as photography, calculators, and the internet, were initially viewed as threats to learning and originality before being gradually integrated into educational practice and reshaping intellectual work. Building on this pattern, the present study identified classroom practices that allow the use of AI tools while limiting opportunities for misuse. These practices were implemented and examined with a group of students over one academic semester. Rather than framing AI as a tool that simply makes academic work easier, this study positions AI as support for deeper learning, critical thinking, and more advanced academic engagement. The classroom practices were intentionally designed to preserve learning and originality while reinforcing academic integrity grounded in honesty, proper attribution, accountability, and adherence to academic norms. Using a quantitative research design, the study examined the relationships among classroom practices, students' responsible AI use behaviors, and student perceived learning outcomes. Student perceptions were examined as indicators of acceptance of AI integrated classroom conditions. Mediation analysis further explored whether responsible AI use strengthened the relationship between classroom practices and student perceived outcomes. The findings indicate that structured classroom practices are significantly associated with responsible AI use and positive student perceived outcomes related to learning, originality, academic integrity, confidence, and discouragement of misuse. Responsible AI use was found to partially mediate the relationship between classroom practices and student acceptance, reinforcing both learning outcomes and confidence in AI integrated instruction.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Literacy and Digital Readiness Vulnerability Mapping in the Philippines
papers.abstract: Functional literacy and digital readiness are foundational capacities for resilient, sustainable, and inclusive communities. While official outputs from the 2024 Functional Literacy, Education and Mass Media Survey (FLEMMS) provide descriptive evidence on literacy and digital participation, integrated Province/HUC-level vulnerability patterns remain underexplored. This study developed an explainable AI-supported vulnerability intelligence framework that extends FLEMMS 2024 from descriptive reporting to Province/HUC-level literacy and digital readiness vulnerability assessment in the Philippines. Province/HUC-level indicators were estimated from the FLEMMS 2024 Public Use Files using survey weights across 118 estimation domains. Functional literacy vulnerability and digital readiness vulnerability were integrated into a composite index, with robustness assessed through alternative and PCA-based weighting schemes. K-Means clustering and GIS mapping identified vulnerability profiles. Logistic Regression served as the primary classification model, while Random Forest was used as a robustness model. SHAP analysis was applied to identify and interpret key contributors to high-vulnerability classification. National estimates showed a basic literacy rate of 89.97% and a functional literacy rate of 70.79%, indicating a 19.18-percentage-point literacy gap. Internet use reached 77.30%, yet the overall digital skill score was only 45.42%. The highest combined vulnerability scores were observed in Tawi-Tawi, Davao Occidental, Sarangani, Basilan, and Zamboanga del Sur. Clustering identified 24 high-vulnerability, 67 moderate-vulnerability, and 27 low-vulnerability Province/HUC domains. papers.title: What is Worth Knowing? A Pinarian Analysis of Statements on the Proposed Reframed General Education Curriculum in Philippine Higher Education
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of globalization, neoliberal governance, and the growing managerialization of higher education, the proposed reframed General Education (GE) curriculum in the Philippines emerged not merely as a policy reform but as a contested ideological battleground over the meaning and purpose of education itself. This study critically examined the competing statements surrounding the proposed GE reform through Norman Fairclough's Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) and William Pinar's conception of curriculum as a “complicated conversation.” Using a qualitative discourse-analytic approach, the study analyzed publicly accessible corpus materials, including CHED draft memoranda, university position papers, faculty statements, organizational declarations, student responses, and public commentaries. The analysis revealed that the debate surrounding the proposed GE curriculum is fundamentally a struggle over what forms of knowledge are socially legitimized, what kind of citizen Philippine higher education seeks to produce, and whose interests curriculum ultimately serves. Four dominant and competing discourses emerged from the corpus: neoliberal-technocratic modernization, humanistic and holistic formation, nationalism and democratic citizenship, and resistance to managerialism and audit culture. These discourses exposed deep tensions between employability and democratic education, market responsiveness and critical citizenship, standardization and intellectual autonomy, and technocratic governance and participatory curriculum-making. The findings further demonstrated that curriculum operates not as a neutral educational framework but as a site of ideological negotiation where political, institutional, cultural, and economic forces compete to define the future of higher education. Through Fairclough's CDA framework, discourse was shown to function simultaneously as language, institutional practice, and social practice, while Pinar's framework illuminated curriculum as an ongoing struggle over memory, identity, democracy, and human formation. Ultimately, the study argues that the controversy surrounding the reframed GE curriculum reflects a deeper national conversation about the future of Philippine higher education and the enduring question at the heart of curriculum studies: What is worth knowing?

items.title: A Double-Edged Transformation: The Paradox of AI and Sustainability in / Education
items.speaker: Prof. Dr. Ricardo BAGARINAO
items.affiliation: University of the Philippines Open University, Philippines
items.abstract: Abstract Education shapes sustainability direction while artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms education and re-shapes knowledge creation, access, sharing, and application. Though AI offers new opportunities for more inclusive and sustainable education, it also operates with growing concerns about energy and resource consumption, environmental impacts, privacy, unequal access, and social inequality. The paper examines this double-edged transformation, challenging the assumption that technological innovation is always progressive or sustainable. It also explores how educators and institutions can navigate the tensions between innovation and responsibility, efficiency and ecological cost, personalization and privacy, access and inequality, and technological capability and human judgment. More importantly, it positions education not simply as a user of AI, but as a force that can shape how societies understand, govern, and use AI. The paper concludes that sustainable use of AI in education must go beyond technological adoption. It requires critical AI literacy, ethical responsibility, ecological awareness, and informed human judgment to ensure that AI contributes to more inclusive, responsible, and sustainable futures. Bionote He has built a career that brings together teaching, academic leadership, environmental research, and the evolving field of open and digital learning. He joined the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU) as a full-time faculty member in 2006, where he taught biology and related courses in the Faculty of Education and the Faculty of Management and Development Studies. His years at UPOU have taken him through various academic and administrative roles. He served as Program Chair of the PhD in Education, University Registrar, Dean of the Faculty of Education, and Director of the Center for Open and Digital Teaching and Learning. He currently serves as Assistant to the Chancellor for Sustainability and the Program Chair of the Doctor in Sustainability. His research interests reflect a continuing concern for the relationship between people, places, and the environment. These include landscape ecology, land use and land cover change, environmental management, disaster preparedness and risk reduction, and spatial analysis using geographic information systems. His work in open and distance education has likewise expanded his research into e-learning and open learning. He has published in peer-reviewed and indexed national and international journals and contributed chapters to books published locally and internationally. Behind these credentials is an academic journey that has moved across disciplines and institutions—from biology and environmental research to education, digital learning, and sustainability.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Academic and Non-Academic Performance of College Students using Senior High School Academic Track in a Private University
papers.abstract: This study addressed the operational challenges of urban transit congestion on the Light Rail Transit Line 1 (LRT-1), particularly the lack of real-time crowd-density information available to commuters, by developing an IoT-integrated passenger monitoring system at Central Terminal Station that uses machine learning for continuous crowd detection and monitoring. The study employed a descriptive quantitative research design with a cross-sectional approach to evaluate both system performance and user acceptance. Six (6) ESP32-CAM devices, each integrated with the YOLOv8n model, were used for real-time crowd detection. At the same time, numerical data were synchronized via a Firebase cloud database and displayed on a web-based dashboard for real-time visualization. In compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), visual data were processed solely within the system and were neither stored nor transmitted. A simple random sampling technique using Cochran's Formula was employed to select 151 respondents to evaluate the system with survey instruments based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), while software quality assessment was conducted in accordance with the ISO/IEC 25010 standard. Findings revealed that the YOLOv8n model achieved a Mean Average Precision (mAP0.5) and F1-Score of 74.7%, demonstrating reliable performance in transit environments. User acceptability results showed high ratings across all TAM constructs with a grand mean of 4.54, indicating a strong positive reception among commuters. Furthermore, the system successfully provided real-time crowd information while maintaining passenger anonymity. Software evaluation results yielded an average mean of 4.642, confirming that the platform is reliable, secure, and user-friendly. Based on these findings, recommendations include system integration across all LRT-1 stations, expansion of the camera's field of view for train arrival tracking, implementation of GPS-based station monitoring, enhancement of adaptive detection mechanisms, and incorporation of mobile alerts, battery backups, GSM-based modems, and push notification features to improve system reliability and accessibility.

papers.title: BaHack: IoT-Based Real-Time Flood Level Detection and Safe Route Navigation System
papers.abstract: Flood monitoring and navigation systems in Metro Manila are often fragmented, delayed, and dependent on manual reporting, limiting their ability to provide timely and localized information to road users. This study developed and evaluated an Internet of Things (IoT)-based real-time flood monitoring and navigation system that integrates low-cost sensors, geo-referenced mapping, and intelligent route optimization to improve flood awareness and travel safety in urban flood-prone areas. A developmental-descriptive research design was employed. The system utilized ESP32-based sensor nodes equipped with ultrasonic and rain sensors, LoRa communication, and a solar-powered energy source. Laboratory simulations and pilot field testing were conducted at selected entrances in Intramuros, Manila. Flood levels based on MMDA classifications (8", 10", 13", 19", and 26") were simulated, with 50 samples collected per level. Descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation, were used to evaluate sensor accuracy, communication latency, and routing performance. HTTP-based communication and the A* pathfinding algorithm were tested under multiple scenarios to validate real-time monitoring and navigation capabilities. Results showed that the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor achieved a mean accuracy of 98.87% with a mean absolute error of 0.15 inches. Data transmission exhibited an average latency of 1.15 seconds and a 98% success rate, enabling near real-time system updates. The A* algorithm also achieved a 98% routing success rate, effectively identifying safe routes and avoiding flooded road segments. Overall system uptime reached approximately 97.57%, demonstrating stable and reliable operation. The findings confirm that the developed IoT-based system can enhance real-time flood awareness, support safer route navigation, and improve urban mobility. Future work should focus on larger-scale deployment, enhanced communication protocols, additional environmental data sources, and predictive flood monitoring capabilities.

papers.title: AirHaven: A Smart Solar-Powered Air Quality Monitoring System Enhanced by IoT Technology and AI Predictive Analytics for Ambient Air Assessment
papers.abstract: Urban air pollution presents significant health risks, yet existing monitoring networks lack sufficient spatial resolution to capture street-level variations. This study addressed this gap by developing and evaluating AirHaven, a solar-powered multi-node air quality monitoring system deployed in Kartilya ng Katipunan, Manila. The system measures PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, and O3, generating data for pollutant mapping, short-term forecasting, and public health advisories. A mixed-methods approach combined developmental, experimental, and survey-based designs. Three sensor nodes transmitted real-time environmental data via LoRa to a centralized platform with web and mobile interfaces. Data were collected continuously for 13 days and analyzed using descriptive statistics, AQI conversion, and regression metrics for predictive modeling. papers.title: Leveraging Gcash Behavioral Data and Score as an Alternative Credit Metric for the Unbanked Construction Employees In Norzagaray, Bulacan
papers.abstract: This research empirically investigates the predictive validity of the GCash Score (GScore) and behavioral data as a viable alternative credit metric for the unbanked population. The study aims to address the critical systemic need for statistically validated alternative credit scoring mechanisms to bridge the information gap and foster a more equitable financial ecosystem. The study operationalizes an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. In the quantitative phase, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Multiple Linear Regression are employed to test the directional significance of behavioral predictors (e.g., usage frequency, retained balances, loan performance, and account activation) on the GScore, grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Anderson's Alternative Credit Scoring Model. Subsequently, a qualitative phase utilizing targeted semi-structured Key Informant Interviews (KII) and thematic analysis is conducted to contextualize the statistical outputs. Quantitative analyses reveal that cumulative digital footprints explain 58.2% of the variance in a user's GScore (R² \= 0.582, p < .001). Specifically, loan repayment performance, account verification (KYC completion), and frequency of platform usage emerged as highly significant positive predictors (p < .001), whereas average retained wallet balance demonstrated only partial significance. Evaluating adoption drivers, perceived ease of use was identified as the primary catalyst for actual platform usage (p \= .003). Contrary to theoretical expectations, trust (p \= .968) and economic incentives demonstrated no statistically significant effect on usage frequency. Among demographic variables, only age exhibited a significant influence on how frequently the unbanked workers utilized the digital wallet. This research demonstrates originality by validating proprietary digital wallet metrics (GScore) against institutional credit standards for a critically underserved demographic: unbanked construction personnel with cyclical, cash-based wage structures and a complete absence of formal banking histories. It provides a localized empirical framework mapping informal digital financial footprints into actionable alternative credit data for traditional financial institutions.

papers.title: FinTech Adoption as Sustainable Finance Infrastructure: Evidence from SMEs in Batangas Province, Philippines
papers.abstract: Financial technology (FinTech) has become a critical driver of financial inclusion and digital transformation, offering significant potential to strengthen sustainable finance infrastructure among small and medium enterprises (SMEs). By reducing transaction costs, enhancing accessibility to financial services, and improving transparency and traceability of financial transactions, FinTech can create enabling conditions for sustainability-oriented financing and economic resilience. This study examined the awareness and utilization of FinTech services among SMEs in Batangas Province, Philippines, and explored the determinants influencing their adoption and use. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 349 SMEs selected through stratified random sampling across five major cities in the province. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire anchored on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2). Descriptive statistics were employed to assess awareness and utilization patterns, while multiple linear regression analysis identified significant predictors of FinTech utilization. Results revealed that SMEs exhibited a high level of awareness of FinTech adoption determinants (M \= 3.41/4.00), with performance expectancy obtaining the highest rating (M \= 3.56). Utilization was predominantly concentrated in mobile banking (84.2%), online banking (78.8%), and e-banking (75.9%), indicating widespread acceptance of digital financial services. Regression analysis showed that facilitating conditions (β \= 0.272, p < 0.001) and hedonic motivation (β \= 0.200, p < 0.001) were the strongest predictors of utilization, followed by performance expectancy, social influence, price value, and habit. Internet connectivity issues, cybersecurity concerns, and inadequate training emerged as major barriers to adoption. The findings underscore the strategic role of FinTech as a foundational enabler of sustainable finance ecosystems by enhancing SME readiness for green financing, climate-risk management, and digital economic participation. Strengthening digital infrastructure, cybersecurity frameworks, interoperability, and financial capability-building initiatives is therefore essential to advancing inclusive growth and sustainable development in emerging economies.
