papers.title: The "Care Penalty" and Gender Asymmetry in the Philippine Labor Market: A Fairlie Decomposition Analysis of Labor Force Inactivity
papers.abstract: Despite structural human capital gains, a persistent gender gap in labor force participation(LFP) defines the Philippine economy. Utilizing individual microdata from the November 2025Philippine Statistics Authority Labor Force Survey (n \= 32,258), this paper investigates themechanisms driving this disparity, focusing on translating findings into municipal extensionframeworks at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM). Descriptive analysis confirmsa 20.5 percentage point participation wedge, heavily underpinned by domestic asymmetry:19.0% of women report full-time inactivity due to household duties, compared to just 1.5% ofmen.We implement a binary probit model and a Fairlie non-linear decomposition across 100replications. Probit marginal effects reveal that women are 19.7% less likely to enter the laborforce than identical men. The decomposition highlights a paradox: while higher femaleeducational endowments compress the gap, this equalizing force is entirely overwhelmed bythe unexplained coefficient effect, which accounts for 88.29% of the divide. This dominantresidual isolates the domestic "Care Penalty". Bridging this gap requires shifting towardtargeted demand-side interventions. We outline localized strategies mapped to PLM extensionagendas, leveraging Manila's existing programs like “Servisyong Yorme” and “Threads of Life”to build sustainable grassroots interventions.

keynote.speaker: Ms. Mary Stephanie CARRANZA
keynote.title: Designing sustainable biomaterials for the future of 3D cell culture and healthcare
keynote.bio: Mary Stephanie S. Carranza is Co-Founder and Managing Director of BIOMATS PH, a Philippine biotechnology startup developing bioprinting technologies and biomaterials for biomedical research. She also serves as Head of the Biomedical Research Unit (BRU) at the Clinical and Translational Research Institute of The Medical City – Ortigas, where she leads research programs supporting translational biomedical innovation. Ms. Carranza is currently leading her own DOST project and is a consultant to several government-funded tissue engineering projects. She previously served as Laboratory Manager (University Researcher II) at the Philippine Genome Center's Protein, Proteomics, and Metabolomics Facility, supporting national research initiatives in metabolomics and proteomics. Carranza has over eight years of research experience in biomaterials, tissue engineering, metabolomics, and translational biomedical research. Her expertise includes biomaterial modification, bioink development, 3D cell culture, and 3D bioprinting for next-generation in vitro models. She also serves as a consultant to several tissue engineering projects, with a particular focus on 3D bioprinting and bio fabrication. Her honors include the Leaders in Innovation Fellowship of the Royal Academy of Engineering (2026), the Short-Stay Scholar Award from the Japan Student Services Organization (2025), and recognition as a finalist in the 2021 Merck Young Scientist Award in the Philippines. Carranza holds a B.S. in Biochemistry and an M.S. in Chemistry, specializing in biomaterials, from De La Salle University - Manila. She also pursued graduate training in biomaterials at Osaka University as a Japanese government (MEXT) scholar.
keynote.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting sits at the intersection of biomaterials, engineering, and biology, offering new opportunities to develop physiologically relevant in vitro models and regenerative tissue technologies. However, the success of a bioprinted construct is not determined by the printer alone. The choice of polymer, method of processing, and design of biomaterials fundamentally influence printability, structural fidelity, cell compatibility, and ultimately the biological function of the printed tissue. This talk will explore key considerations in bioink design, from the intrinsic properties of biomaterials and their rheological behavior to crosslinking, degradation, mechanical performance, and interactions with cells. Examples will illustrate how these considerations change depending on the intended application, from scaffold-based tissue regeneration to the development of reproducible in vitro disease and drug-testing models. Beyond individual bioinks and applications, the discussion will consider sustainability as an ecosystem-level challenge. Developing accessible, adaptable, and locally relevant biomaterials and bioprinting technologies can reduce dependence on imported materials and equipment while enabling researchers to build capabilities suited to regional needs. Establishing shared expertise, characterization infrastructure, standardized approaches, and collaborations across academia, industry, and healthcare can create a more sustainable pathway for bioprinting research and translation. Ultimately, advancing bioprinting in the region requires more than developing better materials or printers, it requires building an ecosystem that allows researchers to move from biomaterial design to functional biological models and, eventually, regenerative applications.

papers.title: Navigating Hilot, Google, and ChatGPT: Healthcare Decision-Making and Health Information Resilience in Rural Cavite
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how individuals access and interpret health information, creating new opportunities to address persistent health information inequities. In rural communities, however, healthcare decisions remain influenced by a complex interplay of traditional healing practices, digital information sources, social networks, and formal healthcare systems. Understanding how these information pathways converge is critical for building resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities. This study examined the role of AI in healthcare decision-making among rural Filipinos and explored its contribution to health information resilience: the capacity to access, evaluate, validate, and utilize reliable health information from multiple sources. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed among 350 adult residents from selected rural communities in Cavite, Philippines. The quantitative phase assessed AI utilization, health literacy, trust in information sources, and healthcare-seeking behaviors using structured questionnaires. Descriptive and inferential analyses identified factors associated with informed healthcare decision-making. The qualitative phase involved in-depth interviews with purposively selected participants to contextualize quantitative findings and explore experiences in navigating traditional, digital, and AI-assisted health information environments. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings revealed that healthcare decision-making is increasingly characterized by dynamic navigation among hilot, internet searches, AI-powered platforms, family networks, and healthcare professionals. AI users demonstrated significantly higher health information self-efficacy, health literacy, and confidence in healthcare decision-making than non-users (p < .05). The study generated the Health Information Resilience Framework, illustrating how rural residents integrate cultural knowledge, digital resources, and AI-generated information when making health decisions. The framework provides a culturally grounded model for integrating AI into community health initiatives, demonstrating how emerging technologies can complement traditional knowledge systems, reduce information inequities, and strengthen resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities.

papers.title: Voices From The Spectrum: Lived Experiences of Employment Among Autistic Adults
papers.abstract: Introduction: Employment remains one of the most significant barriers to social inclusion for autistic adults despite growing recognition of their strengths and contributions in the workplace. Existing literature has predominantly focused on childhood autism, leaving the employment experiences of autistic adults, particularly within the Philippine context, insufficiently explored. This study aimed to examine the lived experiences of employment among autistic adults, with emphasis on the challenges they encounter, the coping strategies they employ, and the factors that facilitate meaningful workplace participation. Methods: A qualitative descriptive phenomenological design was employed to capture the participants' lived experiences. Five autistic adults aged 24–33 years with formal Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnoses and current or previous employment experience were purposively recruited through autism organizations, personal networks, and snowball sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews conducted either face-to-face or via secure online platforms. Audio-recorded interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological framework with NVivo software to facilitate systematic coding and theme development. Trustworthiness was established through member checking, audit trails, and adherence to established ethical principles. Results: Three interconnected themes characterized the participants' employment journey: Pre-Employment, Intra-Employment, and Post-Employment. Participants reported barriers related to recruitment, workplace communication, sensory sensitivities, and social expectations, often requiring continuous self-regulation and masking behaviors to maintain employment. Nevertheless, supportive supervisors, reasonable workplace accommodations, and opportunities that matched individual strengths promoted resilience, professional growth, self-confidence, financial independence, and a stronger sense of identity and belonging. Discussion: The findings demonstrate that employment barriers experienced by autistic adults arise primarily from systemic workplace limitations rather than individual impairments. Creating neurodiversity-affirming workplaces through inclusive organizational policies, employer education, flexible accommodations, and strengths-based employment practices can substantially improve workforce participation and well-being.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Client Care: Knowledge and Readiness of Nursing Students in Manila
papers.abstract: This study examined nursing students' level of knowledge and perceived readiness to use artificial intelligence (AI) in client care at a selected institution in Manila. A quantitative descriptive-correlational, cross-sectional design was utilized to determine the level of knowledge and perceived readiness of nursing students and to examine the relationship between these variables. A total of 205 nursing students from the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th year levels were selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire measuring knowledge (conceptual and ethical) and perceived readiness (intent to use AI, anxiety toward AI use, and perceived competence in client care). Descriptive statistics, Spearman's rho, and independent samples t-test were used for data analysis. Findings showed that respondents demonstrated a good level of knowledge, with ethical knowledge slightly higher than conceptual knowledge. They also reported high perceived readiness, particularly in intent to use AI and perceived competence, while anxiety toward AI use was at a moderate level. The results further showed variations in perceived readiness across selected demographic characteristics. Selected demographic variables such as age, sex, and year level showed significant relationships with perceived readiness, while extent of AI exposure did not. No significant relationship was found between level of knowledge and perceived readiness. The study concludes that respondents demonstrated good knowledge and high perceived readiness toward AI in client care; however, level of knowledge was not significantly associated with perceived readiness, suggesting that readiness may be influenced by factors other than knowledge. The findings contribute to the growing body of evidence regarding the use of AI in nursing education and client care.

keynote.speaker: Prof. Zarah Dane Dimagmaliw-Tan
keynote.title: AIyayay! Opportunities and Pitfalls of AI Use in Language Learning and Teaching
keynote.bio: Zarah Dane R. Dimagmaliw-Tan is an Assistant Professor at the University of the Philippines Diliman. Currently on study leave to pursue a doctorate in Language Sciences at the Université de Rouen Normandie, her dissertation aims to study and propose a sustainable training program for DepEd French-language teachers. She holds two master's degrees: one in French Translation from the UP Diliman and one in language didactics from the Université Sorbonne Nouvelle. She is an active member of the Association des professeurs de français aux Philippines where she served as president from 2011-2018 and 2024-2025.
keynote.abstract: How is Artificial Intelligence transforming foreign language learning and teaching? Before ChatGPT, students were already using AI in the form of machine translation tools like Google Translate to understand or produce a text in the target foreign language that is beyond their current proficiency level. But for this, the student needs to be able to understand or produce a text in another language where the student has a higher proficiency in. Now, with generative AI such as ChatGPT, there is no need even for that. Students can simply transform what they need to accomplish into a prompt that the AI can execute. Yet AI should not be viewed solely as a shortcut or a threat to language learning. When used critically and appropriately, AI can become a powerful tool for learning, teaching, and creating more inclusive and innovative language-learning environments. This raises important questions: Is AI use in language learning sustainable? What does sustainable AI use mean in foreign language learning? How can educators harness AI without undermining the development of genuine linguistic competence, critical thinking, and learner autonomy? And how can AI help transform foreign language learning communities into resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities? This keynote explores these questions by examining the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in foreign language education through personal experiences in the field and by reflecting on how its responsible integration can contribute to more sustainable and innovative approaches to language learning and teaching.

papers.title: From Traditional Lesson Planning to AI Governance: A Comparative Policy Analysis of DepEd Orders and Its Implications for Preservice Teachers' Field Studies
papers.abstract: Introduction. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has transformed lesson planning and created new policy challenges concerning instructional quality, teacher accountability, ethical practice, and preservice teacher preparation. This study examined how DepEd Order No. 016, s. 2026 reforms lesson planning through AI governance compared with DepEd Order No. 42, s. 2016 and analyzed the implications of these reforms for Field Study courses in teacher education. Methodology. Employing a qualitative educational policy analysis through systematic document analysis, the study examined four primary documents: the two DepEd Orders and the syllabi for Field Study 1 and Field Study 2. The study used Walt and Gilson's Policy Triangle for policy comparison, Responsible AI Governance for analyzing AI provisions, the OECD Policy Evaluation Criteria for evaluating the revised policy, and Bardach's Eightfold Path for developing policy recommendations. Findings. The findings revealed a major policy transition from standardized, compliance-oriented lesson planning toward a flexible, learner-centered, and reflective learning-design framework governed by explicit AI provisions. DepEd Order No. 016, s. 2026 has introduced human oversight, ethical AI use, transparency, validation of AI-assisted outputs, data protection, and teacher accountability while positioning AI as a professional support tool rather than a substitute for instructional judgment. The revised policy was found to be highly relevant and coherent with contemporary educational reforms, although its long-term effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability remain dependent on systematic implementation, professional development, and institutional support. The analysis further showed that the current Field Study courses require enhancement in AI literacy, ethical AI use, AI-assisted lesson planning, professional accountability, and authentic assessment to align with the revised policy environment. Conclusion. Responsible AI governance should be integrated into preservice teacher education through human-centered, transparent, and evidence-informed instructional practices, thereby strengthening future teachers' capacity to use AI ethically while preserving professional autonomy and pedagogical quality.

papers.title: Inverting the Digital Migrant: An Autoethnographic Inquiry into a Sustained Human-AI Dialogue-Generated N-Node Network Framework of Instructional Prompt Engineering
papers.abstract: Even though there has been an exponential rise in the usage of generative artificial intelligence technologies in higher education, prompt engineering is still relatively untheorized as a quantifiable learning technique. Most available guidebooks for prompt engineering simply frame it either as a skillful use of phrasing or a list of generic tips, leaving faculty without a linguistic toolkit through which they can determine prior to receiving any kind of output if a particular prompt will succeed instructionally. In this paper, I constructed such a linguistic toolkit. I employed a methodological approach based on an extended and natural conversation between a 64-year-old Filipino educator and a cutting-edge large language model. The effective prompts that emerged during the discussion process were coded using binary coding to N instructional nodes. The co-activation of cases was re-conceptualized using the logic of Exploratory Graph Analysis to identify three latent communities which are named by the researcher as the X Frame, the Y Frame, and the Z Frame. The PVID rubric consisting of ten points was also developed based on N nodes and tried against a pair of naive and expert prompts. The contribution is four-pronged: first, a coding system for analyzing the rhetoric of an instructional prompt; second, a tri-frame design well-suited to network psychometric validation; third, an a-priori rubric for the evaluation of prompt quality, and; fourth, a position statement asserting that teaching experience, gained through years and years of instruction, is not a liability in the time of generative AI, but rather a valuable source of knowledge.

papers.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Higher Vocational Colleges in Sichuan, China: A Mixed-Methods Study of Adoption, Utilization, and Policy Implications
papers.abstract: This study investigated the status of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and utilization in higher vocational colleges in Sichuan Province, China, and examined the challenges and policy implications of institutional AI integration. Using a mixed-methods, descriptive-comparative design, we combined a survey of 1,085 respondents (administrators, teachers, and students) with interviews and on-site observations to profile prevalent AI tools, frequency and purposes of use, and the extent of AI integration in teaching, language learning, and research, while also comparing stakeholder perceptions and identifying barriers to effective adoption. Results indicate a moderate level of AI adoption in Sichuan's vocational colleges: approximately 70–75% of faculty and administrators reported adopting AI tools, while student uptake was lower, with nearly one-quarter unsure whether they had used AI. Utilization was strongest for routine tasks and language learning (notably AI-supported translation and tutoring), whereas AI use for research-related activities remained comparatively limited. Domestic platforms such as Baidu ERNIE Bot and Alibaba's Qwen were the dominant tools, consistent with China's technology ecosystem and access constraints, whereas foreign models such as ChatGPT were used minimally. Formal AI capacity-building was scarce—fewer than 10% reported receiving structured training—yet individuals with prior training or institutional support showed higher usage. Statistical analyses further found no significant differences in overall AI utilization levels among students, teachers, and administrators, suggesting a broadly cohesive pattern of adoption across roles. Key challenges included limited training opportunities, inadequate infrastructure and access, uncertainty or resistance toward AI use, and concerns about data privacy and academic integrity. Based on these findings, we propose a comprehensive academic policy framework to guide the ethical and effective integration of AI across teaching, learning, research, and administration, emphasizing AI literacy programs, infrastructure enhancement, clear usage guidelines, and sustained implementation support, aligned with China's educational modernization agenda.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Magin Benedict FERRER
keynote.title: Project Resin Green: Overview of Initiative and Focus on the Increased Efficiency of DUV Photolithography of Chitosan Bioresist with New Water-soluble PAGs
keynote.abstract: Microchip production constitutes a very important industry; however, current fabrication processes use chemicals that pose health risks and environmental hazards during disposal. The RESIN GREEN Project aims to develop new resist materials and nanometrology methods with the goal of reducing the ecological footprint of digital technology. Bio-sourced polymers have been studied to aid in the transition to eco-friendlier processes. The polysaccharide chitosan has shown promise as a water-soluble photoresist in photolithography at 193 nm (Deep UV), already behaving as a positive tone resist via chain scission of its glycosidic bonds. A commercial photoacid generator (PAG 0) was tested to enhance this effect; however, its sensitivity is still lower than industrial standards. Two new fluorine-free water-soluble PAGs conceptually inspired by commercially available sulfonium salts were synthesized and incorporated in the chitosan resist platform significantly improving the sensitivity of the resulting films in DUV photolithography by reducing the dose-to-clear value and demonstrating the possibility for photomask patterning.

papers.title: Effects of Plasma Priming Treatments on Seed Germination and Early Seedling Growth: An Innovative Approach for Enhancing Crop Establishment
papers.abstract: Atmospheric pressure plasma (APP) technologies have emerged as sustainable, non-chemical strategies for improving seed performance, crop establishment, and productivity. Among these approaches, direct APP treatment and plasma-activated water (PAW) priming have demonstrated strong potential by modifying seed surface characteristics and stimulating key physiological processes involved in germination and early seedling development. Both systems generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) and charged particles that enhance seed coat permeability, improve water uptake, and activate metabolic pathways essential for successful germination. In this study, we evaluated PAW priming across a range of horticultural and agronomic crops, including bok choy, mustard, kangkong, okra, corn, rice, peanut, soybean, and roselle, alongside direct APP treatment applied to adlay, okra, and bitter gourd. Across species, PAW produced from distilled water exposed to moderate plasma conditions consistently improved germination percentage, accelerated germination rate, enhanced germination uniformity and seed vigor, and promoted more robust shoot and root development. Physicochemical analysis of PAW further showed increased acidity, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, and elevated levels of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Similarly, direct APP treatment significantly enhanced germination and seedling growth across crops. These beneficial effects were associated with plasma-induced modifications on the seed surface, including etching and partial erosion of the seed coat, increased formation of oxygen-containing functional groups, enhanced hydrophilicity, and reduced surface tension and contact angle. These structural and chemical changes were confirmed through scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and goniometric analysis. However, results also indicated that excessive plasma exposure, whether through prolonged direct treatment or overly extended PAW activation, can inhibit germination and seedling development due to excessive reactive species accumulation. This highlights the critical need to optimize treatment parameters to balance stimulation and stress effects. Overall, APP and PAW priming offer promising, and innovative seed enhancement technologies with significant potential for agriculture.

papers.title: Design and Development of Air Contactor Geometry for Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)-Based Direct Air Capture Machine for CO2 Sequestration Yielding Liquid Potash as By-Product
papers.abstract: Direct Air Capture (DAC) is a crucial negative emissions technology for mitigating climate change, yet widespread industrial adoption is severely hindered by high energy demands and infrastructure costs. This study presents a highly innovative, solar-powered Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)-based DAC system engineered specifically for scalable deployment in tropical environments. Driving this technological advancement is a novel DNA-inspired double helical ribbon air contactor, intelligently designed to enhance CO2 mass transfer efficiency while drastically minimizing aerodynamic resistance, ultimately yielding liquid potash (K2CO3) as a commercially viable by-product. The engineering methodology utilized three-dimensional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to optimize airflow distribution and mass transfer. A physical prototype, measuring exactly 1000 mm in length, 570 mm in width, and 1060 mm in height, was fabricated and integrated with a smart ESP32 control unit, solar power architecture, and stainless-steel wool packing to create a responsive, resilient infrastructure. Field testing was conducted outdoors during overnight periods to measure real-time performance, followed by laboratory potentiometric titration to determine chemical saturation limits. Evaluations revealed that the fabricated prototype significantly optimized fluid dynamics, achieving an actual pressure drop of just 0.21 to 0.61 kPa compared to the simulated 7.75 kPa. The advanced contactor system recorded a peak CO2 uptake efficiency of 64.90% and utilized up to 67.16% of its theoretical chemical capacity. Crucially, the intelligent system operated at an average specific energy consumption of only 0.64 kWh/kg, representing a massive 70% reduction compared to established baselines. Integrating this complex, double helical geometry within a controlled DAC framework provides a highly viable, energy-efficient technological leap for industrial carbon sequestration, offering a resilient and sustainable infrastructure solution for atmospheric carbon removal.

keynote.speaker: Atty. Chad Patrick OSORIO
keynote.title: Transregional Collaboration in the Age of AI
keynote.bio: Chad Patrick Osorio is an international academic and lawyer-economist, advocating for human and environmental rights. He is currently concluding his PhD at Wageningen University and Research, the Netherlands. He is also Adjunct Assistant Professor at the School of Environmental Science and Management, and former Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics, University of the Philippines Los Baños. In 2026, he served under the Balik Scientist Program of DOST-PCAARRD with the UPLB Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Extension, in conjunction with UPLB SESAM and UPLB Institute of Computer Science Chad serves as Expert Mentor specializing in Sustainability and AI SMEs with the IP for Business Division of the World Intellectual Property Organization. He is Expert Contributor for the World Bank Group's Business Ready. (B-READY) Report for international trade policy and infrastructures (2025-26). He is strategic legal and business operations consultant for a select number of national and international firms and institutions, where he details his experiences and expertise in his upcoming book, “The Hungry Startup's Guide to the Economics of Information.”
keynote.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping research, business, and public governance, yet its opportunities and risks extend beyond the capacity of any single institution or country. Drawing on my personal and professional experience across academia, international organizations, and industry-support initiatives from across different continents, my keynote examines what meaningful transregional collaboration requires in practice. I reflect on connecting interdisciplinary research with international policy processes, translating governance principles into tools that businesses can use, and ensuring that innovation responds to diverse institutional and social realities. I highlight recurring challenges, including unequal technical capacity, fragmented regulation, limited access to data, and partnerships that risk reproducing technological dependence. Effective collaboration must move beyond technology transfer toward shared agenda-setting, reciprocal learning, responsible data governance, and equitable participation in the benefits of AI. I conclude with practical pathways for universities, international organizations, governments, and businesses to build trusted, durable, and accountable transregional partnerships.

papers.title: The ASEAN Maritime Silk Road: A Comparative Analysis of Transboundary Digital Trade Regulation and Governance Between Malaysia and the Philippines
papers.abstract: Due to the accelerating rate of global digitisation, the international maritime logistics sector is revolutionising at an unparalleled pace, from physical paperwork to automated, digital exchanges. It facilitates expedited trade between ports, bypassing the latency of traditional papers, reduced administrative time, bolstered security and lower expenditure. Notwithstanding positive prospects of Electronic Bills of Lading (“eBLs”) and smart port advocacy, these present unique challenges in terms of efficiency and poses complex regulatory quagmires for emerging economies. The paper seeks to examine the legal framework for digital maritime trade by comparing two crucial ASEAN coastal states, namely, Malaysia and the Philippines. Malaysia (influenced by the Hague-Vigsby Rules) and the Philippines (influenced by the US Congress) have legislated rules on Bill of Lading (“BOL”) into their domestic laws, including but not limited via the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 1950 and the Digital Signature Act 1997, and the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, Commonwealth Act No. 65 and the Electronic Commerce Act, Republic Act No. 8792 respectively, the question of an eBLs remains a determinant issue. This paper argues that due to the absence of a harmonised standard on digital trade in both coastal states, this ambiguity invokes major legal obstacles, aggravating cross-border dispute resolutions. Overall, this paper proposes that the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records 2018 (“MLETR”) and the CMI Rules for Electronic Bills of Lading 1990 shall be investigated for regulatory and legal harmonisation between both countries. Similarly, there is potential integration of these harmonised rules across ASEAN and their major trading partners as a whole. This would ensure a uniform legal mechanism, promoting equitable, secure and a legally binding digital maritime regime within our region. Keywords: Digital Maritime Trade, Electronic Bill of Lading, ASEAN, Malaysia-Philippines Partnership, UNCITRAL.

papers.title: A Comparative Content Analysis of Facebook Pages of Selected Mayors for Good Governance (M4GG) in the Philippines
papers.abstract: This study conducted a comparative content analysis of the Facebook posts of selected mayors who are members of Mayors for Good Governance (M4GG), a coalition of local chief executives from different municipalities and cities in the Philippines. It aimed to analyze how Facebook was used as a platform for digital governance communication by examining posts published from August 20 - December 20, 2025. Specifically, the study focused on the communication elements present in texts, images, and videos, as well as the dominant themes and frames reflected in the selected posts. Using a mixed-method research approach, the study combined quantitative content analysis and qualitatie framing analysis. A total of 1,325 publicly available Facebook posts published within the selected period were analyzed. The quantitative component identified the distribution and frequency of communication elements across different media formats, while the qualitative component examined how governance-related themes were constructed and presented. The analysis focused on key themes such as transparency, accountability, public service delivery, community participation, leadership visibility, and relational communication. Findings revealed that the selected mayors used Facebook as a strategic communication tool to present governance activities, public service initiatives, and community engagements. Text-based posts were commonly used to provide indormation, announcements, and explanations, while images and videos emphasized visual documentation, leadership presence, ciitzen interaction, and service delivery. Across the analyzed posts, the most evident themes were public service, community participation, transparency, accountability, and leadership visiblity. These themes showed how Facebook allowed local officials to make governance more visible and accessible to the public. However, the study also found that many posts focussed more on positive representation, public visibility, and engagement than on detailed explanations of outcomes, measures, or participatory decision making process. While Facebook strengthened the communication reach of local officials, it also framed governance as a visible and performative practice.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Rayane HEDNA
keynote.title: Programmable Biointerfaces: Opportunities for Sustainable Biomaterial Design
keynote.bio: Dr. Rayane Hedna is a postdoctoral researcher at the Institute of Materials Science of Mulhouse (IS2M), Université de Haute-Alsace and CNRS, France. She holds a PhD in Biology and Health from Aix-Marseille University and has a background in biotechnology. Her research focuses on designing protein-based materials for biomedical applications, particularly programmable biointerfaces using virus-like particles. She is interested in controlling the presentation of biochemical cues at material surfaces, understanding how these cues influence cell–material interactions, and translating this knowledge into new materials for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. Her work combines protein engineering, biomaterials science, surface biofunctionalization, and advanced biofabrication to create cell-instructive materials with broader healthcare applications.
keynote.abstract: Biological responses to biomaterials are fundamentally governed by surface biochemical cues. However, conventional biofunctionalization strategies relying on native extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins or synthetic peptides often suffer from batch variability, high costs, and limited control over ligand organization. To address these limitations, we developed a programmable and a resource-efficient platform using multivalent virus-like particles (VLPs) to present biological signals at material interfaces. We engineered VLPs to display ECM-derived bioactive peptides, including RGD, YIGSR, and a bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) sequence, via direct genetic fusion or modular SpyTag/SpyCatcher ligation. Applied to cell-repellent model surfaces, these VLP-functionalized interfaces successfully promoted cell adhesion, migration, proliferation, and differentiation. Notably, RGD-presenting VLPs supported cell adhesion at levels comparable to full-length fibronectin and superior to synthetic RGD peptides. This modular approach enabled precise control over ligand density and the co-presentation of multiple signals, yielding adaptable, multifunctional cellular microenvironments. Furthermore, we developed light-based patterning techniques to spatially control VLP distribution across two- and three-dimensional architectures. This spatial programmability confines bioactivity to defined regions, facilitating the design of heterogeneous, cell-instructive materials.Ultimately, compared to conventional coatings, this VLP-based strategy offers opportunities for more resource-efficient surface functionalization. By concentrating minimal bioactive cues, adapting a universal scaffold, and enabling mild, solvent-free aqueous conjugation, this platform provides a promising framework for sustainable design of next-generation biomaterials.

papers.title: Digital Health Technologies and Self-Efficacy of Tuberculosis Patients: A Multi Phase Design
papers.abstract: Introduction The advancement of digital health technology services signifies a transformative approach to healthcare delivery, not just technological advancements, but also a significant shift in attitudes and perceptions toward healthcare (Rosenlund et al., 2023). Methods This multi-phase study explores the relationships between profiles, effectiveness of the use of digital health technologies, and self-efficacy of tuberculosis patients using Digital Health Readiness Questionnaire. It aimed to develop interventional programs such as digital literacy training, user-centered design enhancements, motivational support, or tailored tech onboarding sessions for TB patients. Results Results revealed that mean scores across the dimensions of digital access, usage, literacy, and learnability were moderate. Self-efficacy outcomes reflected a mixed perception among the participants. While some respondents expressed confidence and ease in using digital technology, others reported difficulties, reliance on manuals, and confusion, particularly with new applications and technical jargon. Several items showed high means for negative experiences, such as feeling overwhelmed or wasting time with technology, suggesting that emotional and psychological barriers impede full digital adoption. Linear regression results affirmed that perceived digital health effectiveness significantly predicts TB patients' self-efficacy (β \= 0.516, p < .001), explaining approximately 43.6% of the variance in self-efficacy outcomes. This justifies the development of the proposed intervention program titled "TECH4TB: Empowering TB Patients through Digital Health and Self-Efficacy, designed to strengthen TB patients' ability to access, use, and benefit from digital health technologies through targeted, data-driven strategies. It aimed to improve health outcomes, treatment adherence, and patient autonomy. Conclusion Perceived digital health effectiveness significantly predicts TB patients' self-efficacy. This finding underscored the reciprocal influence between how patients view digital health tools and their confidence in using them. Addressing these gaps can significantly improve both the practical and psychological dimensions of digital health use among vulnerable populations.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Virtual Reality-Based Intervention in Enhancing Physical Function Among Young-Older Adults in Selected Barangays of La Trinidad, Benguet
papers.abstract: Introduction: While age-related physical decline threatens functional independence in older adults, conventional rehabilitation suffers from low adherence, lack of interest and real-time feedback, and clinical accessibility barriers. Virtual Reality (VR) offers an immersive, motivating alternative that enhances compliance and motor learning. Addressing the scarcity of localized, community-based evidence, this study evaluates a VR-based intervention's effectiveness on the mobility, balance, endurance, and ambulation of community-dwelling young-older adults in La Trinidad, Benguet, Philippines. This study aimed to evaluate a VR-based intervention by assessing baseline status and comparing pre- and post-test physical function scores within and between the intervention and control groups. These evaluations specifically measured changes and post-test outcomes across mobility, balance, endurance, and ambulation. Methodology: A randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of an 8-week VR-based intervention among 60 community-dwelling young-older adults, aged 65–74, in La Trinidad, Benguet. Participants were allocated to either the VR intervention or a non-exercise control group. Mobility, balance, endurance, and ambulation were assessed pre- and post-intervention using the Timed Up and Go test, Berg Balance Scale, and 6-Minute Walk Test. Data were analyzed using Jamovi (p < 0.05). Findings: At baseline, the intervention and control groups exhibited no statistically significant differences in mobility, balance, endurance, and ambulation. After the VR-based intervention, the intervention group achieved highly significant improvements across mobility, balance, endurance, and ambulation. Compared directly to the control group, improvements were only seen in balance and endurance. However, endurance and ambulation remained statistically equivalent between the two groups overall. Conclusion: The VR-based intervention significantly improves physical function among young-older adults compared to a control group, though endurance and ambulation outcomes were statistically equivalent. Consequently, healthcare workers and community leaders should integrate structured VR programs into wellness initiatives, while future researchers should utilize larger sample sizes and longer intervention durations.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Stephanie Marie R. COO
keynote.title: Reading Agency in Clothing: Sartorial History as a Lens for Resilient, Inclusive Futures
keynote.bio: Stephanie Marie R. Coo is an Associate Professor of History at the Ateneo de Manila University (Philippines) and a researcher at CHAM – Centro de Humanidades, Universidade Nova de Lisboa (Portugal). She holds a PhD in History from Université Nice Sophia Antipolis (France) and has held research fellowships at the Universidad de Granada (Spain), NOVA School of Law, Universidade Nova de Lisboa (Portugal) and Ruhr-Universität Bochum (Germany), including a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship. She is the award-winning author of Clothing the Colony: Nineteenth-Century Philippine Sartorial Culture, 1820–1896, recipient of the IIAS-ICAS International Book Prize for Best Book in Humanities (Netherlands, 2021), National Book Award and the John C. Kaw Prize for Best Book in History (Philippines, 2022). Her second book, Seams of Sedition: Sartorial Symbols in José Rizal´s Noli Me Tángere (Ateneo de Naga University Press, 2025), expands the study to clothing, literature, and resistance in late colonial Philippines. It was launched internationally at the Leipzig Book Fair 2025, Frankfurt Book Fair - Philippines as Guest of Honor Nation 2025, Berlin Ibero-American Institute (Berlin, 2025), Biblioteca Palácio Galveias (Lisbon, 2025), and at the National Museum of Fine Arts (Manila, 2026). Her work explores the intersections of material culture, dress, gender, and colonial society in the nineteenth-century Philippines and the broader Iberian world.
keynote.abstract: Drawing on two book-length studies of Philippine sartorial history, Clothing the Colony: Nineteenth-Century Philippine Sartorial Culture, 1820–1896 and Seams of Sedition: Sartorial Symbols in José Rizal's Noli Me Tangere, this keynote examines clothing as an underused archive of human agency, identity, and adaptation, treating dress not as decorative or peripheral but as a primary source through which marginalized groups negotiated power, expressed dignity, and shaped their own narratives within colonial systems and their aftermaths. Organized around several guiding questions, this seeks to address how individuals exercise agency within systems of imposed regulation, whether sartorial, colonial, or technological. What can material and literary details reveal about identity formation that formal records omit? How did power, everyday practice, and encoded meaning intersect in the lived experience of colonial subjects, and how might that intersection be traced in other systems of constraint? And, most centrally for this audience, how might historical methods of reading agency, resilience, and adaptation inform the design, evaluation, and study of present-day inclusive systems and emerging technologies? Though these questions are first posed in a nineteenth-century colonial context, they are deliberately framed to travel forward, since any system that regulates behavior through unstated rules, whether a sumptuary ordinance or an algorithm, raises the same basic question of who is served and who must quietly adapt. To answer these questions, the study is grounded in a layered theoretical framework spanning power, practice, and meaning. Pierre Bourdieu's theory of cultural and symbolic capital and Michel Foucault's analysis of power and the disciplined body explain how dress functioned as both currency and mechanism of colonial stratification. James C. Scott's concept of everyday resistance and Michel de Certeau's distinction between imposed strategies and improvised tactics inform how small, low-visibility sartorial choices are read as meaningful acts of agency within constraint. Marcel Mauss's theory of gift and reciprocal exchange and Daniel Miller's work in material culture studies anchor clothing as socially constitutive rather than merely decorative, while Roland Barthes's semiotics of fashion, Homi Bhabha's theory of colonial hybridity, and Jacques Derrida's method of deconstruction provide the interpretive tools for reading garments and texts as unstable, layered sign systems. Guided by this framework, the underlying research draws on an extensive body of primary sources, including nineteenth-century artworks, studio and family photographs, period newspapers, foreign travelers' accounts, novels, and surviving garments, cross-referenced with one another and combined with close literary reading of Rizal's prose, allowing material and textual evidence to illuminate one another. This body of evidence shows how clothing functioned as both a tool of colonial control and a medium through which Filipinos exercised choice and self-determination, and how literary and historical sources, read together, reveal the ways sartorial detail encodes social hierarchy, aspiration, and emerging national identity, with agency often expressed in small, easily overlooked acts rather than overt confrontation. In seeking to answer these questions, the keynote aims to establish clothing and literature as rigorous sources for understanding social agency, to model an interdisciplinary method linking material culture, literary analysis, and history, and to translate these historical insights into a practical framework for evaluating inclusivity in contemporary innovation. In line with the conference theme, "Shaping Resilient Futures: AI, Sustainability, and Inclusive Innovation," the keynote extends this framework to invite researchers across disciplines to bring the same attentiveness to overlooked detail, adaptation, and agency when designing, deploying, and studying technologies and systems meant to serve plural communities.

papers.title: Mga Pamilya ng Mater Dolorosa
papers.abstract: This study examines the cultural, religious, and familial significance of a century-old image of Mater Dolorosa (Our Lady of Sorrows) preserved by a Filipino family and venerated within the local community. While devotion to Mater Dolorosa remains central to Philippine Catholic spirituality, limited research has explored family-owned devotional images as enduring expressions of faith, heritage, and identity. Using a qualitative case study design, the study investigates the image's historical origins, the customs and traditions surrounding its veneration, its influence on family and community life, and the transmission of devotion across generations. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews, participant observation during devotional activities, and document analysis of family and historical records. Thematic analysis identified four major themes: the image as a sacred family inheritance, devotion as a source of family unity and resilience, the image as a center of community religious life, and intergenerational transmission of faith and stewardship. Findings reveal that the Mater Dolorosa is regarded not merely as a religious artifact but as a cherished family member whose presence strengthens kinship ties, nurtures everyday spirituality, and provides hope amid suffering. Family traditions, including communal prayers, novenas, and annual feast celebrations, reinforce religious identity and social cohesion while encouraging community participation. Older generations intentionally transmit devotion through storytelling, ritual participation, and shared responsibility for the image's care. The study concludes that family-owned images of Mater Dolorosa serve as enduring symbols of faith, collective memory, and cultural identity, contributing to the preservation of Filipino Catholic traditions and the continuity of intangible religious heritage across generations.

papers.title: Project Dapitan Blueprint: Eradicating Theoretical Performativity in Engineering Education Through Rizalian Applied Praxis and Inclusive Community Innovation
papers.abstract: Introduction: This action research addresses the institutional crisis of "theoretical performativity"—a contemporary mutation of the colonial "education of fear" identified in José Rizal's Noli Me Tángere. In modern engineering education, students frequently default to rote memorization to navigate high-stakes credentialing, separating abstract mathematics from community utility. This study pilots an innovative curricular intervention that challenges engineering scholars to convert theoretical formulas into inclusive, human-centric municipal solutions. Methodology: Implemented as a three-week action-research sprint, engineering scholars identified localized mechanical inefficiencies within urban Manila. Applying the Law of Rotational Equilibrium, researchers designed a 3D CAD schematic restructuring the standard local street-sweeper handcart. To democratize this data and bypass algorithmic compression and digital apathy, the structural design was launched via a specialized 2x2 high-resolution digital grid coupled with direct, localized peer engagement. Findings: Quantitative calculations proved that moving the handcart's wheel axle backward by precisely 1.5 inches reduced upward lifting strain for street sweepers by 80.2%, dropping mechanical labor stress from 16.2 lbs to 3.2 lbs. Qualitative feedback from the target student peer group ($n=35$) demonstrated a distinct epistemological shift from grade-centric performance to applied public service and an awakening to the socio-economic dignity of informal labor. Conclusion: Project Dapitan Blueprint establishes a repeatable model for inclusive innovation in higher education. By liberating engineering equations from whiteboards to optimize grassroots labor safety, the study proves that humanizing technical curricula builds resilient, future-ready communities. It provides an scalable framework for transforming traditional technical education into an active mechanism for sustainable civic development.

papers.title: Social Responsibility Awareness among College Students of City of Malabon University: Basis for Social Responsibility Awareness Advocacy Program
papers.abstract: Social responsibility awareness among university students has become increasingly important as higher education institutions are expected to develop socially responsible and civically engaged citizens. Despite this, limited local studies have examined how students' awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, and personal norms vary across demographic factors, particularly in the context of City of Malabon University. Using a quantitative descriptive-comparative research design, data were gathered from 286 college students through a Social Responsibility Awareness Scale and analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests. The major finding revealed that students demonstrated a high level of Social Responsibility Awareness, with an overall composite mean of 3.31 (Strongly Agree). Among its dimensions, Ascription of Responsibility obtained the highest composite mean (3.36), followed by Personal Norm (3.30) and Awareness of Consequences (3.26), all interpreted as Strongly Agree. Key results further showed that awareness of consequences demonstrated significant differences across age (p \= 0.030), year level (p \= 0.010), and degree program (p \= 0.045), but not in sex (p \= 0.118). Ascription of responsibility showed no significant differences across age (p \= 0.375), year level (p \= 0.091), and degree program (p \= 0.130), although a significant difference was found in sex (p \= 0.022). Meanwhile, personal norm showed significant differences across age (p \= 0.015), sex (p \= 0.027), year level (p \= 0.005), and degree program (p \= 0.021). The study concludes that higher education institutions contribute significantly to developing students' civic consciousness and ethical responsibility and sustainable social action among students.

papers.title: D'PIXSCOPE: A DIGITAL PIXEL MICROSCOPE WITH SUSTAINABLE DESIGN, BUILT-IN MOBILE APPLICATION, AND INTEGRATED ILLUMINATION
papers.abstract: This study developed the Digital Pixel Microscope with Sustainable Design, Built-In Mobile Application, and Integrated Illumination, an affordable and eco-friendly innovation aimed at enhancing STEM education. The microscope utilized a recycled plastic base to promote sustainability while reducing environmental waste. It incorporated a USB-powered digital imaging system with an adjustable flashlight to improve visibility in educational and research settings. Additionally, the D'PixSCOPE Mobile Application, developed using Android Studio and Kotlin, enabled users to capture, store, delete, and share microscope images seamlessly. The research employed a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative insights from 23 Grade 12 STEM students and 3 science teachers from Emigdio A. Bondoc High School. Data collection included product testing, Likert-scale surveys, and open-ended responses to evaluate usability, portability, and learning impact. Descriptive statistics analyzed user satisfaction, while thematic analysis extracted key insights from qualitative responses. Findings revealed that the D'PixSCOPE enhanced learning by providing affordable, accessible, and sustainable microscopy for students and educators. The integration of a mobile application modernized the microscopy experience, offering a portable, user-friendly, and efficient alternative to traditional laboratory tools. Observations confirmed its durability, functionality, and ease of use, with sustainability efforts ensuring environmental responsibility. Future improvements may refine design aspects and explore broader applications beyond the classroom.

papers.title: Meaning Beyond Words: A Pragmatic Analysis of Taglish Code-Switching in Selected Philippine Advertisements
papers.abstract: Code-switching is a successful advertising technique in the Philippines, although it may also be viewed as less sophisticated or polished than monolingual English or Tagalog. Analyzing at a deeper view on how Taglish is used in advertisements because it must look beyond words to grasp the connections between meaning, identity, and customer persuasion. This study investigates code-switching in advertising discourse, particularly Taglish, which links formal marketing to the actual Philippine language environment. Gumperz's Codeswitching Theory (1982) and Sperber and Wilson's Relevance Theory (1986) serve as the foundation for this qualitative interpretivist approach. Twenty 30-second TV ads addressing areas such as food, hygiene, and digital services that were broadcast between 2023 and 2025 are used in this study. The study uses pragmatic analysis to demonstrate how advertisers operate in the Philippines' multilingual environment to make sure their products are accessible and appealing. The results demonstrate that Taglish is a linguistic opportunity for individuals who identify as bicultural. Every language has a distinct function; for example, English is used to demonstrate authority and knowledge, whereas Tagalog is meant to foster understanding, comfort, and emotional connection. The use of Taglish helps to create trust with customers and makes people more interested by reflecting real-world situational or conversational patterns. Results show that the contextual meaning and persuasive intent in Philippine advertising highlight the growing cultural identity in the Philippines. Future studies may include quantitative research to analyze how lexical choices and sentence structures affect consumer perceptions in terms of products. This type of study can provide a better understanding of the factors influencing consumer behavior in the Philippines by integrating language, psychology, and culture into the advertisements.

papers.title: Reflective Teaching, Self-Efficacy and Research Practices among CvSU Naic Faculty Members: Basis for Capability Enhancement Programs
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the interrelationships among reflective teaching, self-efficacy, and research practices among faculty members of Cavite State University Naic (CvSU Naic), with the goal of informing faculty development programs. Employing a mixed-methods design, the research integrates quantitative and qualitative data to analyze faculty perceptions and professional experiences. Findings reveal a significant positive correlation between reflective teaching and self-efficacy, both of which contribute to increased research engagement. Faculty members who regularly engage in reflective teaching exhibit higher self-efficacy, which in turn enhances scholarly productivity. Among the demographic variables analyzed, age significantly predicted self-efficacy, suggesting that confidence in teaching grows with experience; however, academic rank, employment status, and other factors showed no significant effects. These insights highlight the importance of institutional support systems such as structured reflection and research mentorship in fostering a culture of pedagogical innovation and scholarship. The study advocates for targeted faculty development initiatives that support continuous professional growth and excellence across all ranks. Future studies could adopt longitudinal and in-depth qualitative approaches to further explore the development of faculty self-efficacy and research involvement over time. Keywords: Reflective Teaching, Self-Efficacy, Research Engagement, Faculty Development, Higher Education

papers.title: The Mediating Effect of Self-efficacy on the Academic Resilience and College Adjustment of First-year Local University Students
papers.abstract: It was reported by the Commission on Higher Education that for the school year 2023-2024, the attrition rate for universities and colleges was at 35.15%. Although slightly lower than that of the previous year, it is still concerning particularly for local universities whose students are recipients of the free tertiary education through Republic Act 10931 or the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act (UAQTEA). With the government's limited resources, it is important to ensure that those who start tertiary education should also finish them so that they can in turn contribute to nation-building and economic growth as part of the local workforce and of the global labor market. Towards such a goal, college adjustment was identified as one of the keys to better retention and completion. With Filipinos known for their resilience, it was of interest for the researcher to find the relationship of this trait, and their belief in their ability, self-efficacy, to college adjustment. This quantitative study gathered data from 384 first year local university students and used survey instruments that measured self-efficacy, academic resilience and college adjustment. In summary, it found that the respondents are fairly resilient, have high self-efficacy, and rated their college adjustment as “somewhat good”. There is a very weak positive but significant relationship between academic resilience and self-efficacy, between self-efficacy and college adjustment and between academic resilience and college adjustment. Through Path Analysis, it was found that self-efficacy has a mediating effect between academic resilience and college adjustment. First year Local University students have enough resilience and belief in themselves to handle typical stressors, but they are not the only factors that can impact college adjustment.

papers.title: Phonological Patterns of an L1 English–Tagalog Child
papers.abstract: Bilingualism is a common linguistic experience among Filipinos, and English–Tagalog is one of the most common language pairs in the Philippines. The acquisition of each language in bilingual children does not happen in isolation. Research on bilingual children shows that English acquisition in the Philippines occurs within a bilingual and/or multilingual environment, resulting in observable cross-linguistic influences in early language development (Tan de Ramos, 2023). This study contributes to the literature on L1 English language acquisition patterns among L1 English–Tagalog children and whether they follow typical or atypical phonological development, which remains relatively limited. Using a descriptive research design, the study observed the speech patterns of a 4-year-old child whose first languages are both English and Tagalog to examine the child's English productions and whether they exhibit the typical development of L1 English phonological rules and the influences of cross-linguistic transfers from Tagalog. Findings revealed that occurrences of fronting, gliding, and stopping—common early developmental processes—make frequent occurrences in the child's speech, as well as greater articulatory control of final consonants than consonants in the initial position, which is an atypical acquisition pattern that may be cross-linguistic in nature. Other cross-linguistic transfers from Tagalog observed include hyper-articulation of vowels and stopping of labiodental fricatives to bilabial stops. These results indicate that both normal developmental speech patterns and cross-linguistic influence can be observed in the child's speech and contribute to an understanding of the phonological systems of simultaneous bilingual children.

papers.title: Letran's Schoolscape as a Source of Raising Catholic Religiosity and Awareness
papers.abstract: As the linguistic landscape becomes a prominent field of inquiry, the emergence of schoolscape, an analysis of languages in educational space, has the potential to uncover awareness and learning, multilingualism, community perceptions, and language domination in institutions. These recent developments leave behind the emphasis of schoolscape on the development of religiosity and awareness. Thus, this study investigated the schoolscape of Letran as a source of raising Catholic religiosity and awareness. Framing from functional categories of schoolscape signage and situated semiotics, the study utilized quantitative-qualitative multimodal content analysis, combining the systematic, distributive approach of quantitative content analysis through frequency counting and spatial distribution with the flexible, interpretive methods of qualitative content analysis through focus group discussions of students, faculty, employees, and administrators across Letran campuses. The results revealed that required signs and the English language dominate the institution's schoolscape. Further, the schoolscape produced Catholic-Dominican identity through lived experiences, curriculum, socialization, and evocation of affect. Letran's schoolscape further constructed agency, embodied experiences, and physical and social structures toward Catholic awareness. To reinforce the faith-based identity and promote health, school leaders should diversify signage, while retaining required signs, to integrate Catholic-Dominican spirituality and encourage student engagement with visual materials for spiritual and interreligious understanding. An exploration of the schoolscape's role in institutional and national identity, and promotion of social justice in community initiatives, can be further explored.
