papers.title: Tuning Out: Multimodal Strategies and Learners' Engagement as Basis for an Interactive-Communicative Teaching Tool
papers.abstract: In the contemporary digital age, higher education faces a pervasive behavioral phenomenon termed "tuning out," where cognitive overload and a relentless influx of digital stimuli diminish learners' attention and physical engagement during face-to-face instruction. This challenge is particularly critical for Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSED) English pre-service teachers, as sustained focus is a fundamental prerequisite for mastering communicative competence and pedagogical skills. Despite the proven efficacy of multimodal strategies—the strategic integration of verbal and nonverbal cues—in fostering meaning-making, existing literature within the Philippine context remains limited and inconclusive regarding how these specific instructional behaviors influence student engagement in higher education.To bridge this research gap, this study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design to investigate the nexus between teachers' multimodal strategies and learner engagement at the University of Cabuyao. The quantitative phase involved a survey of 83 BSED English students to identify patterns in instructional delivery, while the qualitative phase utilized semi-structured interviews with six participants to provide nuance to these findings. Results indicated that while educators possess high proficiency in verbal simplification and facial expressions, their application of proxemics remains underdeveloped and stationary. Furthermore, while learners demonstrated high levels of visual focus, they expressed a strong preference for collaborative participation over individual inquiry.The findings underscore that the synchronization of cognitive logic with sensory anchors is a pedagogical necessity for transitioning students from passive observers to active learners. Consequently, this study developed "Tuning In," a digital application designed to operationalize these multimodal strategies, supported by a comprehensive architectural system design. This research concludes that purposeful, intentional multimodal delivery is vital for sustaining learner focus, providing actionable insights for instructional communication and future-proofing teacher education in the modern classroom.

papers.title: ChatGPT Usage Profile and Prompt Generation Quality of Grade 10 Students in Contemporary Issues Towards a Proposed Classroom Policy on Artificial Intelligence Use
papers.abstract: The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) tools has leaded to the transformation of the educational landscape. Modern AI language models can generate information, assists with research, answer academic questions, and help with creative and analytical tasks. These technologies enable students to tap into vast knowledge sources and personalized academic support in real time, fostering more efficient and self-directed learning. This study investigated the ChatGPT usage profile and prompt generation quality of Grade 10 students in Contemporary Issues and served as the basis for proposing a classroom policy on the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education. Research suggests that students use the AI tool to a certain extent, indicating that the AI is an additional learning tool and as a resource and not a replacement for their academic work. Frequent or increased use of AI tools does not automatically lead to improved prompt construction. Instead, the findings suggest that effective prompt generation is influenced more by critical thinking, communication skills, prior knowledge, and guided instruction, rather than by usage frequency alone. Students recognize both the educational benefits and limitations of ChatGPT, demonstrating awareness of its usefulness while acknowledging concerns regarding misinformation, dependency, and academic integrity. This indicates an emerging level of digital awareness, although structured guidance is still necessary to translate awareness into effective practice.

papers.title: A Convergent Mixed-Methods Assessment of Coaching and Mentoring Implementation by Master Teachers in Selected Schools in the Schools Division Office - Manila: Basis for a Data-Driven Action Plan for Program Enhancement
papers.abstract: This convergent mixed-methods study assessed the coaching and mentoring implementation by Master Teachers in the Schools Division Office – Manila to develop a data-driven action plan for program enhancement. Grounded in Instructional Leadership Theory, the study employed an enhanced Input-Process-Output framework with feedback loops. The quantitative strand surveyed 128 Beginning to Proficient teachers across six Key Result Areas (KRAs) of the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST). The qualitative strand interviewed 15 Master Teachers using outcome-based phenomenography. Findings indicated that coaching and mentoring were implemented "often" across all KRAs (M=3.89-4.02), with Diversity of Learners and Curriculum and Planning rated highest, and Learning Environment lowest. No significant differences were found based on sex, educational attainment, or teaching experience (p > .05). Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: practices which were described as structured, collaborative, and flexible approaches; strategies such as learner-centered instruction, observation, modeling, and reflective dialogue; challenges like time constraints, workload, and teacher resistance; and perceived impact including enhanced competence, confidence, and career advancement. Integration revealed convergence in confirming active implementation, complementarity in explaining statistical patterns, and divergence in highlighting challenges not captured quantitatively. A key contribution is identifying coaching and mentoring within a dual development-accountability system under the Performance Management and Evaluation System (PMES), creating tensions between developmental and compliance-oriented practices. The study concludes that implementation effectiveness depends on contextual factors, relational dynamics, and balancing institutional demands with authentic professional learning. A data-driven action plan was developed to address identified gaps and strengthen implementation across KRAs.

papers.title: Sustaining the Lexicon: Strategies for Translating Ecological and Material Terms in Steinbeck's The Pearl
papers.abstract: This research aimed to translate from English to Filipino the cultural terms found in The Pearl by John Steinbeck. The research used descriptive-qualitative design. It purposefully selected and analyzed two linguistic categories: ecological words, covering fauna and flora, and material culture. Utilizing the communicative approach theory and translation strategies proposed by Peter Newmark (1988), interpreting, and applying contextual understanding, finding equivalence was done. Results revealed that there were cultural words with no exact equivalence such as ant lion, horned toad, fiddler crab, tuna cactus, and Winchester carbin; insufficient equivalent for ingredients and methods of food preparation terms such as corn cake and pulque; use of metaphor in describing faunal terms like flutes and puma; and possibility of reduction of meaning in the translation of cultural terms from the source to target language such as brush house and hanging box. However, the study also showed that many cultural words found in The Pearl may be translated in Filipino language through the cultural equivalence strategy proposed by Newmark. The following strategies were used in the translation of the cultural terms: 1) cultural equivalence 2) couplet 3) descriptive translation 4) transference 5) naturalization 6) functional equivalence and 7) recognized translation. Our study demonstrates how leveraging the richness of Filipino cultural, ecological, and material vocabulary drives intercultural learnings and exchanges. By integrating these indigenous insights, we can preserve ancestral ecological wisdom while building resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities. Ultimately, this work highlights that translating cultural concepts is not a mere linguistic exercise, it is a vital bridge that merges environmental stewardship and cultural sustainability.

papers.title: Satisfied but Exhausted: Faculty Workload, Job Satisfaction, and Burnout in a State University College
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships among faculty workload, job satisfaction, and burnout among tenure-track faculty members in a State University College in the Philippines. Using a quantitative descriptive-associative research design, data were gathered from 29 faculty respondents through a researcher-developed workload assessment instrument, the Job Satisfaction Survey, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Educators Survey. Descriptive statistics were used to determine workload, job satisfaction, and burnout levels, while Pearson correlation coefficients were computed to examine the direction and magnitude of associations among the variables. Findings showed that faculty workload was multidimensional and varied widely among respondents, with an average workload score of 45.43. Faculty members were generally satisfied with their work, with the highest satisfaction reported in Nature of Work, Supervision, and Coworkers, while Operating Procedures received the lowest rating. In terms of burnout, respondents reported moderate Emotional Exhaustion, low Depersonalization, and high Personal Accomplishment. Correlation results indicated that workload had a moderate positive association with Emotional Exhaustion and a weak positive association with Depersonalization, but negligible associations with overall job satisfaction and Personal Accomplishment. Overall job satisfaction showed negligible associations with Emotional Exhaustion and Depersonalization, but a weak positive association with Personal Accomplishment. The findings suggest that faculty members may remain satisfied and professionally accomplished while still experiencing emotional strain from workload demands. The study concludes that faculty well-being should be treated as an institutional responsibility, requiring holistic workload monitoring, streamlined operating procedures, wellness support, and sustained recognition of the meaningful and relational dimensions of academic work.

authors.name: Rufo Gil Albor
authors.affiliation: UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES LOS BANOS

papers.title: EMOTIONS IN LEARNING MATHEMATICS AMONG COLLEGE STUDENTS: BASIS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOCIO-EMOTIONAL LEARNING PROGRAM (SEL)
papers.abstract: This study involved the investigation of the different emotions experienced by first-year collegestudents in learning Mathematics in City of Malabon University for the school year 2025-2026. Different emotions such as enjoyment, anger, anxiety, hopelessness, and boredom were elicited in connection to mathematics that affectedmotivation, engagement, and achievement of students in their classes. The use of Control-Value Theory guided the study as the research used the quantitative approach of descriptive-survey employing the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire-Mathematics (AEQ-M). Age, sex, and academic program were considered demographic factors for analysis using Mann-Whitney U test and Kruskal-Wallis test. The findings showed that enjoyment recorded the highest mean of 2.87 (Agree), which indicated satisfaction and achievement in learningmathematics. Anger scored the least mean of 1.91 (Disagree), which implied that frustration was minimal among students in learning math. Anxiety received the most prevalent mean of 2.42 (Disagree), while hopelessness (2.34, Disagree) and boredom (2.30, Disagree) were also experienced by the respondents. Statistically significant difference occurred when sex (enjoyment, p \= 0.046; anxiety, p \= 0.002; and boredom, p \= 0.049) and academic program (anger, p \= 0.032) were used as grouping variable. The negative emotions were characterized by anxiety, which inhibited participation and success; however, enjoyment made individuals feel more confident and determined. With these findings, the researcher developed the ADAPT-MATH SEL Program (Adaptive Socio-Emotional Learning for Mathematics), which was to complement the KAPWA Mental Health Advocate Program in schools. Whereas KAPWA aimed at increasing awareness of emotions in general, ADAPT-MATH sought to help reduce mathematics-related anxiety through guided problem solving, self-confidence building exercises, and effective instruction. The program involved training studentadvocates to assist their peers in emotional well-being and encouraging teachers to adopt emotion-friendly teaching techniques. This research highlights the need to incorporate socio-emotional learning into mathematics education and calls for more research in this area.

papers.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence in Science Education: Utilization Patterns and Perceptions Among BSEd-Science Students
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly significant educational technology that enhances teaching and learning, particularly in science education. This study examined the utilization patterns and perceptions of Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Science (BSEd–Science) students regarding the use of AI tools in their academic learning. A convergent mixed-methods research design was employed involving 53 BSEd–Science students selected through total enumeration sampling. Quantitative data were collected using a validated researcher-made survey questionnaire with four-point Likert-scale items, while qualitative data were gathered through open-ended survey questions. Quantitative data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and composite mean, whereas qualitative responses were analyzed through thematic analysis. The findings revealed that ChatGPT (54.7%) and Google Gemini (50.9%) were the most frequently utilized AI tools. Students primarily used AI to generate explanations for science concepts (64.2%), perform proofreading and grammar checking (62.3%), and create study summaries (49.1%), with most respondents using AI several times a week (41.5%). Students demonstrated moderate perceptions of AI utilization in laboratory work (M \= 2.91), lecture-based learning (M \= 3.06), and other learning areas (M \= 3.03). Thematic analysis generated five themes: AI as a Valuable Learning Companion in Science Education, Critical and Responsible Utilization of AI, AI as a Catalyst for Innovative Science Learning, Human Judgment Remains Essential in Science Education, and Maximizing the Educational Potential of AI in Science Learning. These findings indicate that BSEd–Science students actively integrate AI into their learning and perceive it as a valuable supplemental tool for science learning while recognizing the importance of critical thinking, ethical AI use, and teacher guidance. The study highlights the need to strengthen AI literacy and promote the responsible integration of AI in teacher education programs.

papers.title: Assessment of College Students' Perceptions on Mathematics Learning Interaction: Basis for an Enhanced Training Program
papers.abstract: Mathematics learning in higher education is increasingly recognized as an interactive process shaped by teacher support, student motivation, and self-regulated learning. However, limited studies have explored how these components collectively influence college students' learning experiences, particularly in the Philippine context. This study assessed the perceptions of first-year college students on Mathematics Learning Interaction (MLI) as a basis for developing an enhanced training program. A quantitative descriptive-comparative design was employed, involving 285 respondents from six college departments in City of Malabon University. Data were gathered through a validated survey questionnaire measuring teacher-promoting interaction, math intrinsic motivation, and self-regulation in learning mathematics, and were analyse using weighted mean and non-parametric tests. Findings revealed that students generally have positive perceptions of MLI, with teacher-promoting interactions (TPI) rated highest, followed by self-regulation in learning mathematics (SRLM), while math intrinsic motivation (MIM) obtained the lowest mean. No significant differences were found when grouped by age and sex, leading to the failure to reject the hypothesis; however, a significant difference emerged in intrinsic motivation across college departments, leading to the rejection of the hypothesis. This study concluded that while teacher support and self-regulation are consistently evident, students' motivation varies depending on academic background, highlighting the need for contextualized and engaging instructional strategies.

papers.title: Mathematics Self-Efficacy and Anxiety Among Undergraduate Non-Mathematics Major Students: Basis for Mathematics Confidence Enhancement Program
papers.abstract: This study examined mathematics self-efficacy and mathematics anxiety among undergraduate non-mathematics major students in the College of Teacher Education at City of Malabon University. It aimed to identify the levels of students' confidence in mathematics and their anxiety, determine differences based on demographic variables, and examine the relationship between mathematics self-efficacy and mathematics anxiety. The findings served as a basis for proposing a Mathematics Confidence Enhancement Program designed to support students in improving their mathematical learning experience. This study used a quantitative descriptive–comparative–correlational research design. A total of 291 undergraduate non-mathematics major students participated in the study. The Mathematics Self-Efficacy and Anxiety Questionnaire (MSEAQ), a validated instrument, was used to gather data. Weighted mean and standard deviation were used to describe the levels of the variables. Mann–Whitney U test, Kruskal–Wallis H test, and Spearman's rho were used to analyze differences and relationships among variables.The results showed that students often demonstrated moderate mathematics self-efficacy with a composite mean of 2.61 and moderate mathematics anxiety with a composite mean of 2.80. Significant differences were found in mathematics self-efficacy (U \= 5537, p \= .049, r \= .159) and mathematics anxiety (U \= 5157, p \= .007, r \= −.216) when grouped according to sex. In terms of degree programs, mathematics self-efficacy showed a significant difference (χ²(4) \= 15.38, p \= .004), while mathematics anxiety showed no significant difference (χ²(4) \= 6.64, p \= .156). Furthermore, a significant negative relationship was found between mathematics self-efficacy and mathematics anxiety (ρ \= −.299, p \= .001). These results highlight the importance of strengthening students' confidence to reduce anxiety and improve learning outcomes. Based on these findings, a Mathematics Confidence Enhancement Program is proposed to help students build stronger confidence, reduce anxiety, and improve their overall performance and experience in mathematics learning.

papers.title: SOLAR SYSTEM SCOPE MOBILE SIMULATION IN TEACHING SCIENCE AMONG GRADE 6 LEARNERS
papers.abstract: This study assessed the efficacy of the Solar System Scope 3D simulation in enhancing Grade 6 pupils' understanding of solar system concepts. A pre-test and post-test control group quasi-experimental design was utilized. The participants consisted of 36 Grade 6 pupils from Rabanes Elementary School, allocated into experimental and control groups via split-group sampling. The primary instrument for data collection was a researcher-made, curriculum-aligned 20-item multiple-choice test. Data were analyzed using a t-test, weighted mean, frequency/percentage distributions, and standard deviation. Pre-test results indicated low prior knowledge across both groups with no statistically significant difference (p>.05; experimental M \= 10.61, SD \= 4.24; control M \= 9.11, SD \= 3.77. Post-intervention, both groups demonstrated improvement; however, the experimental group achieved a significantly higher average score (M \= 15.82, SD \= 2.99 compared to the control group (M \= 13.44, SD \= 3.50, p<.05). Additionally, the experimental group showed a highly significant within-group gain from pre- to post-test (p<.001). These findings suggest that the 3D simulation is more effective for teaching solar system concepts than traditional methods. The integration of interactive, visual elements enables better comprehension of planetary motion and spatial relationships, ultimately leading to greater learning gains.

papers.title: Development of an Automated Class Scheduling System for Colegio de la Ciudad de Tayabas using Genetic Algorithm
papers.abstract: Class scheduling is one of the most complex processes in academic institutions, including various constraints such as room availability, faculty's workload, courses allocation, and considering the institutional policies. At an institution like Colegio de la Ciudad de Tayabas, the manual scheduling process results in an overlapping schedule, inefficient allocation of resources, and an increase in the administrative workload. Thus, this study aimed to develop an automated real-time class scheduling system that uses a Genetic Algorithm (GA) to generate an optimized and a conflict-free schedule. The system was developed using Agile methodology and integrated with PostgreSQL and Docker for the system's backend database management. The system's algorithm (Genetic Algorithm) applied its operations, such as selection, crossover, mutation, and fitness evaluation, to iteratively improve the scheduling solutions. The system evaluation was conducted using a heuristic evaluation and the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality standards. Results showed that the system achieved a high user satisfaction with an overall rating of 4.38 from its end-users or the generic users and 4.46 from an IT expert. Thus, the algorithm successfully generated conflict-free schedules under its feasible constraints. The study demonstrates that genetic algorithms are effective in solving complex scheduling problems in the academic institutions.

papers.title: Exploring Competency Challenges of Flying Cadets in Simulator Training Through CBT-Based Interventions
papers.abstract: The study aimed to identify competency challenges of flying cadets in simulator training through CBT-Based Interventions. Specifically, it sought to utilize a phenomenological approach to explore the lived experiences of flying cadets regarding competency challenges in simulator training and the use of Cognitive Behavioral Theory (CBT)-based interventions in aviation education. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings of this study revealed that flying cadets encounter significant challenges in developing essential flight competencies during simulator training. Based on the findings, competency development is not solely dependent on technical skill acquisition but is also influenced by the cadets' ability to manage complex and simultaneous tasks within a high-pressure environment. The study recommends that aviation training institutions be encouraged to integrate psychological skills training into their existing simulator programs.

papers.title: Reliance on the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools among Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) Students of Daraga Community College
papers.abstract: The researchers employed a quantitative research design, specifically a survey method, to determine the commonly used AI tools among Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) students (N \= 332), how these tools are utilized, and the level of student reliance on them. The findings revealed that the majority of college students at Daraga Community College commonly use ChatGPT (87.09%), Google Bard (also known as Gemini) (51.81%), Photomath (20.78%), Canva (90.36%), and CapCut (95.48%). These preferences highlight the practical adoption of user-friendly and versatile AI tools that enhance productivity and foster innovation among BEEd students. In terms of utilization, the results showed that students primarily use AI tools to enhance grammar, correct spelling, and improve the overall clarity of their work (84.94%); quickly locate reliable academic sources (58.73%); obtain step-by-step explanations for homework (57.53%); create visually appealing presentations efficiently (56.93%); and generate AI-assisted video lectures and tutorials (43.98%). Furthermore, BEEd students commonly rely on AI tools for academic support and productivity-related tasks. Despite the availability of direct answers from AI tools, they primarily use them to improve grammar and vocabulary (WM \= 3.67), assist with projects and homework (WM \= 3.66), and read and analyze study materials (WM \= 3.43). Conversely, students expressed disagreement with using AI tools to answer exams (WM \= 2.07), relying on AI instead of independently solving problems (WM \= 2.56), and submitting AI-generated assignments without proper review (WM \= 2.28). Hence, college students oppose unethical uses of AI and do not heavily rely on these tools for their academic tasks, instead using them as supportive resources for learning.

papers.title: ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS AND CONSERVATION ATTITUDE OF JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS IN CABUYAO: BASIS FOR YOUTH ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM
papers.abstract: The study examined the environmental awareness and conservation attitudes of Junior High School students in Cabuyao, Laguna, particularly those studying near Laguna de Bay, where environmental issues such as pollution and ecosystem degradation highlight the need to strengthen youth environmental engagement. It aimed to determine the level of students' environmental awareness and conservation attitudes and examine their relationship.A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed. Data were collected from 357 students in selected public schools using a structured questionnaire. Statistical tools such as frequency, percentage, weighted mean, Kruskal–Wallis test, Mann–Whitney U test, and Spearman's rho were used to analyze the data.Findings revealed that students demonstrated a very high level of environmental awareness in terms of environmental issues, human–environmental issues, and environmental protection practices. However, their conservation attitudes were found to be at a very low level in terms of environmental responsibility, participation, and initiative, indicating a clear gap between awareness and actual environmental behavior. Significant differences were observed in selected indicators when grouped according to demographic profile, particularly age, sex, and grade level, depending on the variable. Moreover, results showed a significant but generally weak relationship between environmental awareness and conservation attitudes, indicating that higher awareness does not consistently translate into active environmental behavior.Based on these findings, a youth environmental program is proposed, incorporating school-based activities, community engagement, and experiential learning strategies to strengthen both awareness and conservation attitudes. The study concludes that enhancing environmental education and youth programs can improve students' awareness and encourage active participation in environmental conservation efforts in support of sustainable community development.

papers.title: Humor in Action: Exploring Humor as a Pedagogical Technique in Elementary Araling Panlipunan Discussions
papers.abstract: This study examined the use of humor as a pedagogical strategy in elementary Araling Panlipunan instruction in selected public schools in Lucena City. Using a qualitative phenomenological design and reflexive thematic analysis, the study gathered data from sixteen licensed Grades 4 to 6 teachers purposively selected for their demonstrated use of humor. Data were collected through online focus group discussions. The study explored how teachers integrate humor to sustain engagement, reinforce comprehension, and support a respectful classroom climate. It also examined students' emotional responses, cognitive engagement, and participation when humor was embedded in lessons. Contextual factors shaping humor use—including school socio-political conditions, students' cultural backgrounds, and teacher–student relational dynamics—were likewise identified. Findings showed that teachers intentionally employed humor through storytelling, contextualized examples, spontaneous jokes, and playful commentary to capture attention and maintain participation. Students generally responded with increased interest, active involvement, and clearer understanding when humor aligned with instructional aims. Humor also fostered a relaxed atmosphere that eased discussions of complex or sensitive topics. Its effectiveness, however, depended on appropriate timing, relevance, and cultural sensitivity. Teachers adjusted their use of humor based on class diversity and situational cues, emphasizing the need for professional judgment and relational awareness. Insights from the study informed the development of a research-based instructional material, Humor's Civic Spark: Playful Pedagogy Playbook for Elementary Araling Panlipunan. Overall, the study concludes that humor functions as a purposeful instructional tool that enhances engagement, meaning making, and sustained and positive interaction.

papers.title: Development and Validation of INSPIRE (Inclusive Science Preparedness and Individual Readiness Evaluation): An Exploratory Factor Analysis
papers.abstract: This study developed and validated the Inclusive Science Preparedness and Individual Readiness Evaluation (INSPIRE) Scale, a localized instrument designed to measure junior high school students' readiness for inclusive science classrooms in Mandaluyong City. An exploratory sequential mixed-method design was employed. In the qualitative phase, initial items were generated from literature and students' lived experiences, then subjected to expert review to ensure clarity, relevance, and necessity. In the quantitative phase, the Content Validity Index (CVI) was computed to provide statistical evidence of content validity. Items with an Item-CVI (I-CVI) of 0.78 and above were retained, those between 0.70–0.77 were revised, and those below 0.70 were removed. At the scale level, the Scale-CVI/Ave (S-CVI/Ave) reached 0.98, while the Scale-CVI/UA (S-CVI/UA) was 0.90, both interpreted as Excellent and exceeding the minimum threshold of 0.80. The validated instrument was then administered to 250 junior high school students enrolled in inclusive science programs. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) revealed a clear and interpretable factor structure consistent with the proposed dimensions of readiness, with all items demonstrating acceptable loadings above 0.40. After the EFA process, 47 final items were retained and grouped into meaningful readiness dimensions. Reliability testing further confirmed the robustness of the scale, with Cronbach's alpha at 0.975 and McDonald's omega at 0.976, both surpassing the minimum threshold of 0.70 and indicating excellent internal consistency. The findings confirm that the INSPIRE Scale is a valid and reliable tool for assessing readiness in inclusive science education. Its development provides educators, administrators, and policymakers with a culturally relevant, empirically supported instrument to strengthen inclusive practices and promote equitable science learning opportunities in the Philippine context.

papers.title: Guided and Unguided AI Use in Assessments: Student Engagement and Satisfaction
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has changed how students plan, draft, revise, and complete assessment tasks. However, there is still limited evidence on how instructional guidance shapes students' experiences with these tools. This study examined whether guided AI use in assessments differs from unguided AI use in terms of student engagement and learning satisfaction among undergraduate students in the Philippines. A quantitative, cross-sectional, two-group comparative design was employed involving 50 undergraduate students from information technology-related programs, with 25 students in the guided AI use group and 25 in the unguided AI use group. Student engagement and learning satisfaction were measured using multi-item Likert-scale subscales administered through an online post-assessment survey, and group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests after assumption checks for normality and homogeneity of variance. Results showed that the guided AI use group reported significantly higher student engagement than the unguided group. The guided group likewise obtained significantly higher learning satisfaction than the unguided group. These findings indicate that AI does not improve educational outcomes through access alone. Instead, its value depends on pedagogical structure, explicit expectations, and instructor support. The study provides quantitative evidence that guided AI use can promote more active engagement and more satisfying assessment experiences than unguided use. It also offers practical implications for designing AI-supported assessment in higher education.

papers.title: Micro and Game-based Learning (MGL) Materials in Improving Students' Engagement and Academic Performance in Mathematics 7
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of Micro and Game-based Learning (MGL) materials in improving students' engagement and academic performance in mathematics 7. Specifically, this study aimed to: (1) assess the control and experimental group through pretest; (2) develop Micro and Game-based Learning (MGL) materials; (3) integrate Micro and Game-based Learning (MGL) materials among the experimental group, (4) assess the control and experimental group through posttest, (5) determine the significant difference between the pretest and posttest of control and experimental, (6) determine the significant difference between the posttest scores of control and experimental, and (7) achieve improved students' engagement and academic performance in mathematics 7 through MGL materials. This study used a quantitative, quasi-experimental research design, with two (2) sections of Grade 7 from Lucena Dalahican National High School as respondents. Meanwhile, microlearning uses short and focused content, while game-based learning adds interactive elements to make learning engaging. Data were collected through pretest and posttest and analyzed using Mean Score, Weighted Arithmetic Mean, Paired t-Test, Independent t-Test, Wilcoxon Signed Ranked Test, and Mann-Whitney U Test. Findings revealed that MGL positively affect the experimental group's engagement and academic performance in Mathematics 7 than control group. Statistical analysis showed a significant difference between the pretest and posttest of both control and experimental group. Despite this, there was a significant difference between the posttest scores of two groups, comparing the posttest scores of control group, and on the post-test of experimental group (p-value < 0.001), and on the students' engagement post-test of control group, there is a statistically significant difference to the posttest under experimental group (p-value \= 0.004). The result indicated that control and experimental group shows difference in their level of engagement after the utilization of micro and game-based learning, and greatly increased the experimental group's academic performance in Mathematics 7.

papers.title: Interactive Gamified Storybooks with Structured Comprehension Checks on Enhancing Functional Literacy
papers.abstract: Persistent deficiencies in the functional literacy of learners, particularly in decoding accuracy and reading comprehension, continue to hinder their ability to attain expected grade-level competencies, highlighting the need for context-responsive and engaging instructional interventions. This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of interactive, gamified storybooks in enhancing learners' decoding skills and reading comprehension. Employing a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest research design, the study involved 40 selected Grade 3 learners in Pulo Elementary School, Philippines, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-developed assessment instrument aligned with targeted competencies. Findings revealed that prior to the intervention, learners demonstrated Average Mastery in both decoding (M \= 2.45; MPS \= 35) and reading comprehension (M \= 3.88; MPS \= 48.50). Following the implementation, performance improved to Moving Toward Mastery in decoding (M \= 5.75; MPS \= 82.14) and Closely Approximating Mastery in reading comprehension (M \= 7.08; MPS \= 88.50). Results showed a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores. The results suggest that interactive, gamified storybooks can effectively enhance foundational reading skills and promote deeper text comprehension, offering a contextualized, scalable reading intervention plan for similar educational settings.

papers.title: Project SULAT: A Development-Oriented Scriptwriting Learning Guide for Multimedia Production
papers.abstract: This capstone project developed Project SULAT, a development-oriented scriptwriting learning guide for multimedia production (radio, television, and new media) tailored to the BA Communication program of Batangas State University - The National Engineering University. Rooted in the Development Communication (DevCom) approach, the project utilized a modified Operational P-Process Framework to bridge the gap between theory and practice. During the Inquire phase, a baseline aligned with industry standards was established by assessing third- and fourth-year students' Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) alongside insights from 18 key informants from education, media, and the development sector, selected via purposive sampling. The Strategic Design phase translated these findings into a communication strategy, establishing learning objectives infused with DevCom's "laymanized" and "masa-oriented" approaches. Grounded in expert interview data, specialized writing activities and multimedia formats were embedded into a learner-centered design to target identified competency gaps. In the Create and Test phase, the strategy materialized into the learning guide draft. It immediately underwent formative evaluation, featuring rigorous expert reviews and pilot-testing with 64 respondents. Direct feedback was used to refine the material for high usability and functionality. Evaluative results revealed high acceptability, with composite mean scores for Usefulness, Appeal, and Design ranging from 3.58 to 3.64, interpreted as "Excellent." These metrics indicate the material effectively met learner needs, proving both functional in achieving instructional objectives and visually engaging. The Mobilize and Monitor phase will introduce the refined guide into a real-world academic setting, tracking student responses and performance to ensure instructional efficiency. Finally, the Evaluate and Evolve phase will measure the guide's success in empowering students to produce development-oriented content, providing critical outcome data to guide future improvements for the evolving multimedia landscape. Ultimately, Project SULAT offers a highly functional, student-centered instructional material shaped directly by academic and industry experts.

papers.title: Shaping Resilient Literacy Frameworks: Scaling the ChatGPT-Assisted Learning Method (CALM) for Sustainable Public Education
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine the efficacy of ChatGPT-Assisted Learning Method (CALM) in enhancing reading proficiency among 9th-grade students in a public secondary school situated in the Philippines. The study used a sequential explanatory mixed-methods, single-group pretest–posttest design. A total of N \= 50 students were purposely selected who were identified as frustrated readers during the Phil-IRI assessment. The intervention period lasted eight weeks and was assessed using a pretest and posttest. To gain a deeper understanding of the participants' significant experiences, this was followed by a qualitative phase, in which five participants were selected as the saturated sub-sample to undergo one-on-one semi-structured interviews and focus groups. Thematic analysis was used to isolate the functional mechanisms of the AI-mediated scaffold. Results from the quantitative data revealed an increase in reading proficiency, with M \= 5.66, and students reaching "Proficient" or "Advanced" levels rising from 54% to 92%. Cohen's d \= 1.45 indicates a large effect, while η2 \= .34 suggests that 34% of the variance in reading proficiency is attributable to the CALM intervention. Hence, a reduction in the mean standard deviation from 4.13 to 2.82 indicates a significant improvement in reading performance. Furthermore, five themes emerged from the qualitative findings supporting the result from the quantitative phase which described as core functional mechanisms: (1) instructional responsiveness and mastery growth; (2) dialogic adaptability and strategic autonomy; (3) diagnostic feedback and self-regulated revision; (4) metacognitive prompting skill building; and (5) ownership and clarity through reconstructed expression, marking the internalization of the digital scaffold. This evidence establishes the Theory of Distributed Reading Gains (TDRG) through the CALM Feedback−Prompt−Scaffold (FPS) Instructional Framework cycle, which operationalizes how distributed gains arise in resource-constrained high-density environments.

papers.title: Arduino-based Braille Interactive Learning Device for Visually Impaired Individually
papers.abstract: Despite the availability of Braille books and assistive technologies, visually impaired learners still have limited access to affordable interactive tools that support Braille literacy. The high cost of many existing Braille learning devices creates a need for more accessible alternatives. In response to this need, this study developed an Arduino-based Braille Interactive Learning Device for Visually Impaired Individuals. The study aimed to develop an affordable and interactive learning device that assists visually impaired learners in acquiring foundational Braille literacy skills, including the alphabet, numbers, and selected punctuation marks. The developed system consists of a hardware prototype and a companion mobile application called B-Dots, designed to provide an accessible and engaging learning experience. The prototype utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller, micro-servos, and user-friendly controls, while the B-Dots application was developed using Flutter and Dart. The application includes features such as text-to-speech, Braille translation, and Wi-Fi connectivity to support learning and accessibility. The system was developed using the prototyping model, with continuous feedback from a Special Education teacher throughout the development and testing phases to ensure that it met user needs. The functionality, reliability, and usability of both the hardware and software components were evaluated through user assessments and quality testing based on ISO 25010 standards. Results showed that the prototype and mobile application received a mean score of 4.60, indicating high performance and user satisfaction. The findings indicate that the developed system is an effective and accessible tool for supporting foundational Braille learning and enhancing the learning experience of visually impaired individuals.

papers.title: FACTORS AFFECTING THE UTILIZATION OF ONLINE LEARNING AT SELECTED HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS: BASIS FOR INSTITUTIONALIZED POLICY FORMULATION
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Online learning has become an essential instructional modality in nursing education, yet its effective utilization depends on multiple learners, technological, and institutional factors. Understanding these factors is critical for designing innovative academic systems that uphold quality, safety, financial sustainability, and long-term population health outcomes. This study examined the issues affecting online learning among nursing students and explored how emerging evidence could inform the development of innovative, nursing-led care and education models that shape future-ready health systems. Methodology A descriptive–correlational design was used among 331 nursing students from a Higher Education Institution in Dasmarinas Cavite, Philippines selected through stratified random sampling. Data was collected using a modified version of the Muilenburg and Berg (2005) Student Barriers to Online Learning Survey. Statistical analyses included frequency distribution, weighted means, and Spearman's Rho to determine significant relationships. Findings Respondents demonstrated very high ability and confidence with online learning technology, high learning effectiveness, and high enjoyment in an online learning environment. They reported a low extent of perceived significance of common online learning issues (administrative/instructor factors, academic and technical skills, social interactions, motivation, time/support, cost/access, and technical problems). No significant relationship was found between most perceived issues and the three learning-related variables; however, a significant association emerged between Cost and Access to Internet Issues and Learning Effectiveness. Findings informed about the development of an institutionalized online learning policy. Conclusion This study confirms that nursing students possess strong digital readiness, perceive minimal barriers to online learning, and identify internet cost and access as a key factor affecting learning effectiveness. Thus, it recommended the creation of institutionalized policies to enhance online learning experiences and prepare future nurses for digital health environments.

papers.title: Cyclists' Perceived Cyclability: Examining the Influence of Urban Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Cycling as a mode of transportation has been increasing in popularity due to its environmental benefits and sustainability; however, its effectiveness in urban areas like Manila is greatly influenced by existing urban infrastructure. While well-designed infrastructure, such as safe road conditions and dedicated bike lanes, can significantly improve cyclists' safety and comfort, poor infrastructure and unsafe traffic environments can discourage cycling. Despite this, specific urban infrastructure factors that influence cyclists' preferences and experiences remain underexplored. This study aims to examine the perceived cyclability of commuter cyclists in Manila, anchored on the Theory of Planned Behavior. A qualitative phenomenological research design was employed, using purposive sampling of eight commuter cyclists, with data collected through in-depth online interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed key issues such as poor road conditions, misuse of bike lanes, and traffic-related safety concerns, which affect cyclists' route choices, safety, and overall experience. These results may guide urban planners and policymakers in improving cycling infrastructure, enhancing road safety, and promoting cycling as a sustainable mode of transportation.

papers.title: EXTENT OF STAKEHOLDERS PARTICIPATION AND LEVEL OF SCHOOL PERFORMANCE: BASIS FOR SCHOOL'S SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM
papers.abstract: This study investigated the extent of stakeholders' engagement and itsrelationship with the level of school performance in public elementary schools within theBustos District, Division of Bulacan, for the School Year 2025-2026. The researchemployed a quantitative, descriptive-correlational design, surveying 201 keystakeholders, including school heads, teachers, SPTA officers, and LGU officials.Data were collected using adapted survey questionnaires and the DepEd School-Based Management Tool. Findings revealed that stakeholders perceived theirengagement in planning and decision-making, implementation of school programs andactivities, monitoring and evaluation, and resource mobilization as "Very Good."Similarly, the perceived level of school performance across academic achievement,school management and leadership, teachers' performance, and learning environmentwas rated as "Very Satisfactory."A significant positive correlation was found between all dimensions ofstakeholder engagement and school performance indicators. The study concludes that a 8 high level of stakeholder engagement is crucial for enhancing school performance and fostering sustainable development.Recommendations include ensuring balanced stakeholder representation,institutionalizing engagement practices, strengthening participation in monitoring,evaluation, and resource mobilization, implementing evidence-based academicinterventions, and developing a comprehensive School Sustainable DevelopmentProgram.

papers.title: Effectiveness of the Flipped Classroom Approach in Improving Academic Performance in Grade 9 Science in a Private Sectarian Secondary High School in Malabon City, Philippines
papers.abstract: The study aimed to determine the effectiveness of the flipped classroom approach as an instructional tool in teaching Grade 9 Science. This approach maximizes the use of online learning technologies, such as the internet and instructional videos, to deliver science content outside the classroom while utilizing face-to-face sessions for active learning and student engagement. The intervention was implemented among selected Grade 9 students taking Science at a Private Sectarian Secondary High School in Malabon City, Philippines. The flipped classroom approach is grounded in constructivist learning theory, which emphasizes student-centered knowledge construction through active engagement, reflection, and the integration of prior knowledge with new learning experiences. A quasi-experimental design was employed involving six sections, each composed of 38 students. Participants were equally divided into control and experimental groups, with the experimental group exposed to the flipped classroom approach. Student profiles, including age, sex, and learning preferences, were gathered using a standardized form and Multiple Intelligences (MI) checklist. Pretest and posttest assessments were administered to measure academic performance. Results revealed no significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores of the control group. In contrast, the experimental group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in posttest scores, leading to the rejection of the null hypothesis. These findings indicate that the flipped classroom approach, grounded in constructivist principles and supported by technology-enhanced instruction, is an effective instructional strategy for improving student achievement in high school Science.

papers.title: Understanding Neophyte English Teachers' Career Trajectories: Orchestration of an Appropriate Professional Development Plan Framework
papers.abstract: This descriptive phenomenological study explored the perceived career trajectories of neophyte English teachers in public secondary schools within the Schools Division Office of Manila. Despite recent policy initiatives like DepEd Order No. 29, s. 2022, aimed at structuring career progression, beginning teachers often encounter uncertainties, limited access to tailored support, and a perceived lack of clear pathways for professional growth. Drawing on foundational theories such as Super's Life-Span, Life-Space Theory, Schein's Career Anchors Theory, and Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, this research sought to delve into the authentic lived experiences of ten purposefully sampled neophyte English teachers, each with less than three years of teaching experience. Employing a rigorous qualitative design, data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and were analyzed using Colaizzi's Seven-Step Method. The study aimed to uncover participants' preferred career paths (e.g., horizontal advancement as Master Teachers or vertical progression into administration), their key motivations and challenges, and how contextual factors and personal aspirations influenced their career decisions. The findings yielded a comprehensive understanding of their professional journeys, culminating in the orchestration of a responsive, evidence-based professional development plan framework. This framework specifically addresses the unique needs of early-career English teachers, bridging the gap between national policies and lived realities, and offers actionable insights for policymakers and school administrators to enhance teacher retention, motivation, and effective professional growth within the Philippine educational system.

papers.title: TEACHERS' STRATEGIES IN MANAGING STUDENTS' MISBEHAVIOR IN KEY STAGE 1 CLASSROOM
papers.abstract: Classroom management is important to create a positive learning environment and improve the effectiveness of teachers' strategies. However, student misbehavior remains a challenge that hinders the flow of the class, which also influences the performance of teachers in delivering class instruction. This study used a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design to examine the relationship between the major factors contributing to misbehavior and the frequency of students' misbehavior in key stage 1 classrooms in selected schools in District II, Malabon City. A simple random sample of 164 Key Stage 1 teachers participated in a standardized survey questionnaire that had been validated (Cronbach's α \= 0.81-0.86). The data was analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and the Spearman Rho correlation coefficient. The results showed a significant positive relationship (p=0.003) between the major factors contributing to misbehavior, such as “Parents who do not instill pro-school values in their children.”, “Students who lack self-discipline.”, and “Students with emotional and/or behavioral difficulties.” (mean=3.51), and the frequency of students' misbehavior (mean=3.36). This shows that the more these major factors are observed in the classroom, the occurrence of misbehavior also increases. The results showed that proactive and constructive strategies can lessen the misbehavior of the students inside the classroom, these strategies include counseling, organized participation, and behavioral observation. This study underscores the significance of having effective and proper teaching strategies inside the classroom that aids in managing students' misconduct and to create a strong relationship between the parent and the teacher to lessen the misbehavior and create a good behavior and supportive environment for the students.

papers.title: "Pamana: An Exposition on the Interface of Hybridity in Cultural Studies."
papers.abstract: The study investigates the shaping of Filipino culture, history, and heritage in the digital world. Online platforms, social media, and digital archives have birthed complex approaches in the preservation and dissemination of Filipino traditions. The concepts of narrativization, conceptualization of identities, and reimagination of Filipinoness and Filipinism have become a possibility in the digital realm, mainly for those with historical baggage of marginalization (nakalilimutan o naisasantabi). This study, focusing on the intersections of ethnicity, gender, and class, considers digital spaces to provide new orientations to old narratives of Filipino history that would allow a younger generation to engage with its past in previously unexplored ways to also become an avenue to renegotiate identify notions. Cultural hybridity, one of the guiding theories behind this study, is one that was proposed by Homi K. Bhabha. Bhabha offered an understanding that identity in culture is never static but must be understood in relation to the ongoing interfacing of different cultures. This assertion, in the Filipino case, lays emphasis on how present-day Filipino identities are hybrids of indigenous traditions, colonial histories, and modern global influences that consider digital platforms as a maximizing factor in such cultural hybridity as the medium that offers people contemporary ways of approaching their heritage, reshaping cultural narratives, and contesting personal and collective histories. Questions and Gaps: 1. How do these digital platforms help create new and hybrid Filipino identities in today's world? 2. Will an electronic version of Filipino history ever be possible without changing its already complex narratives? 3. What obligations do we have to ensure diverse, inclusive, and historically correct digital spaces?

authors.name: Joven Albert Castillo
authors.affiliation: Polytechnic University of the Philippines/FAITH Colleges

papers.title: Impact of Songs and Singing as an Intervention for reading Comprehension
papers.abstract: This research crafted a kind of intervention that pupils thrive at school and enjoy learning led by reason and objective. According to BetterLessons, 2022, the Theory of Action is a Student-Centered Learning Teaching, therefore educational songs and lyrics used in crafting reading materials made available in slide presentations, with the actual and successive procedure of the reading activities on the lesson plan were used for this research. After the data have been treated and interpreted, findings are as follows: There were 117 or 70.1% pupils attained the frustration level and 50 or 29.9% got instructional level. None of the pupils reached independent level during pre-intervention; There were 116 learners (or 69.5%) attained “Independent Level” and 17 or 10.2% got “Frustration Level” of their reading comprehension during the post-test/post-intervention; The pre-interventional level is 9 while the post intervention is 18 with Wilcoxon coefficient based on the negative ranks of .000 which indicated the rejection of the null hypothesis. Conclusions: Majority of learners belong to frustration level; The learners went to “Independence Level' after taking the post-test and receiving the reading comprehension intervention; The post-intervention reading comprehension evaluation demonstrated a remarkable improvement, with a large rise in the proportion of pupils obtaining the highest level of reading competency, known as the independent level. Using songs as an instructional technique to increase decoding and language comprehension, a significant improvement in overall reading comprehension skills; There was a significant difference in the learners' reading comprehension levels before and after reading comprehension intervention. This suggests that the crafted method of reading intervention is effective.

papers.title: Pre-service teachers' emergent literacy activities during their internship
papers.abstract: The practice teaching program is an essential element in teacher preparation where pre-service teachers can learn important traits needed in developing their personal and professional knowledge. One of the key components to prevent reading failure specifically in kindergarten are well-trained teachers that can integrate guided reading and phonics to meet the needs of struggling readers.This paper aims to describe the field experiences of early childhood pre-service teachers about emergent literacy activities implemented during their internship using descriptive qualitative document analysis of their reflective journals. After analyzing 40-50 journal entries from three pre-service teachers, it revealed that the emergent literacy activities focus more on print awareness and letter knowledge through integration of letter activities, phonological awareness specifically identifying the specific sound of a letter, emergent writing through tracing activities, oral language and comprehension through teacher created songs and stories using different instructional materials in printed and digital format. Noticeably, remedial activities were also conducted to selected kindergarten students. The results of the study provide insights into the importance of teacher preparation on literacy instruction for young learners.

papers.title: GRADE 7 STUDENTS' CHALLENGES AND COPING STRATEGIES IN WRITING POETRY: A BASIS FOR DEVELOPING INSTRUCTIONAL MODULE
papers.abstract: This qualitative research is conducted to identify the challenges and coping strategies of students in writing poetry. The participants of this study were limited to ten Grade 7 students from Laboratory High School at President Ramon Magsaysay State University-San Marcelino Campus, for the Academic Year 20242025. The study utilized purposive sampling to ensure a specific result free from biases. The researchers employed a questionnaire to gather data. Findings indicated that the challenges faced by grade 7 students include creation of rhyme, complexity of meter, development of theme, knowledge of figurative language, and knowledge of various poetic styles. Moreover, reading books and dictionaries, collaborating with peers, taking notes, imagination, and practicing poetry writing emerged as their primary coping strategies. Based on the results, the researchers developed an instructional module to help students address their challenges and enhance their poetry writing skills. This study recommends the following: reading books to improve vocabulary, practicing writing poetry to enhance writing skills, taking notes to have guide when writing, and gathering feedback from friends to share ideas. Furthermore, schools must encourage programs related to writing to enhance students' writing skills. In addition, curriculum developers should create ore instructional materials to lessen the challenges the students experience in writing poetry. Future researchers are also encouraged to study the effect of individual writing and collaboration with friends on writing activities.

papers.title: Teaching Performance of Public Elementary Teachers in Malabon City
papers.abstract: Teaching performance has a direct impact on students' academic success and general development; it is important to provide a quality education. The Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST) are used in the Philippines to determine the level of teacher competence. However, limited localized studies examine teaching performance in relation to demographic variables. This study was conducted to assess the teaching performance of public elementary school teachers in Malabon City using the PPST domains and to determine whether significant differences exist when teachers are grouped according to their demographic profiles. The results showed that teachers generally had high-level teaching performance in all domains of PPST such as Content Knowledge and Pedagogy (p \= 3.68), Learning Environment (p \= 3.68), Diversity of Learners (p \= 3.58), Curriculum and Planning (p \= 3.63), Assessment and Reporting (p \= 3.65), Community Linkages and Professional Engagement (p \= 3.66), and Professional Growth and Professional Development (p \= 3.67). The respondents mostly in the age of 41-45 (19.69%) with experience more than 10 years in service (61%), mostly female (83.86%), and with bachelor's degree (67.32%). Statistical analysis showed that there were no significant differences in teaching performance when classified according to age, sex, and found partial significant differences when classified according to educational attainment, particularly in terms of Community Linkages and Professional Engagement (p \= 0.005), and Personal Growth and Professional Development (p \= 0.016). Teaching Performance was also found partial significant differences when classified according to years of teaching, particularly in Learning Environment domain (p \= 0.018). This implied that demographic factors do not serve as significant factors on the differences in overall teaching effectiveness. The study has shown that professional competence and standards adherence are more influential to the teaching performance than demographic characteristics.

papers.title: Perceived Effects of ChatGPT on the Academic Learning Experiences of Grade 12 Students at Asia Source College of Arts and Technology, Inc.
papers.abstract: This study explored the perceived effects of OpenAI's ChatGPT on the academic learning experiences of Grade 12 students at Asia Source College of Arts and Technology, Inc.. As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into education, students have begun utilizing AI-powered tools to support their academic tasks and learning processes. The study aimed to determine how ChatGPT influences students' study habits, comprehension, critical thinking, and overall learning experiences. Furthermore, it sought to identify both the advantages and potential drawbacks of using AI in academic settings. The research employed a qualitative case study design to gain an in-depth understanding of students' perceptions and experiences regarding the use of ChatGPT. Data were collected from selected Grade 12 students through questionnaires and survey forms that examined their frequency of use, purposes for utilization, and personal insights about the tool's impact on their studies. Responses were analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns and significant observations related to the educational use of ChatGPT. The findings revealed that students commonly use ChatGPT for answering questions, generating ideas, completing assignments, and improving their understanding of lessons. Most participants perceived ChatGPT as a helpful and convenient learning tool that supports comprehension and enables them to accomplish academic tasks more efficiently. However, the study also found concerns regarding students' excessive reliance on AI, which may negatively affect the development of independent thinking, critical analysis, and problem-solving skills. The study concludes that ChatGPT has both positive and negative effects on students' academic learning experiences. Its impact depends largely on students' responsible and ethical use of the technology. Hence, educators and institutions are encouraged to promote guided integration of AI tools in education to maximize learning benefits while minimizing potential academic and cognitive drawbacks.

authors.name: Erwin HILARIO
authors.affiliation: Asia Source College of Arts and Technology, Inc.

papers.title: Historical Sources and Modern Technology: An Analysis of the Utilization of Artificial Intelligence in the Retrieval and Classification of Historical Sources
papers.abstract: This paper aims to examine the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the retrieval and classification of historical sources. Through a comprehensive analysis, this study weighs the strengths and weaknesses of utilizing AI in the preliminary stages of research. Descriptive analysis was employed to systematically outline the current state, capabilities, and limitations of modern AI tools within the context of historiography, without altering their inherent nature. Ultimately, the research emphasizes that while AI significantly aids in data retrieval and categorization, it cannot replace the critical lens, analysis, and human interpretation that a historian brings to historical sources.

papers.title: Scholar Graduates' Competencies And Challenges In Teaching Life Sciences
papers.abstract: This descriptive qualitative study examined the perceived and manifested competencies of RA 10612 scholar graduates in Ilocos Norte, the challenges they encountered, and the implications for teaching life sciences. Despite the increasing deployment of RA 10612 scholar graduates in public schools, limited evidence exists on their competencies and the challenges they encounter in teaching life sciences. Using purposive sampling, data were gathered through interviews and focus group discussions with 19 participants, including scholar graduates, immediate heads, peers, and students. The interview and focus group discussion guides were anchored on the seven domains of the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST). Results-Based Performance Management System (RPMS) portfolios and Individual Performance Commitment and Review Form (IPCRF) ratings were analyzed to triangulate the findings. Guided by Albert Bandura's Self-Efficacy Theory, transcribed data were analyzed thematically. Findings revealed that RA 10612 scholar graduates demonstrated strong competencies across the seven PPST domains, supported by RPMS portfolios, IPCRF ratings, and the perspectives of immediate heads, peers, and students. However, participants identified challenges, including subject mismatch, learner management difficulties, limited pedagogical strategies, weak lesson planning foundations, delayed access to professional development, and unclear career progression pathways. These challenges constrained teaching effectiveness and professional growth. The findings highlight the roles of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) and the Philippine Normal University (PNU), together with its network of teacher education institutions, in strengthening pre-deployment preparation and continuous support for scholar graduates transitioning into the teaching profession. The study concludes that addressing these challenges is essential to maximizing the potential of RA 10612 scholar graduates and recommends targeted professional development, structured mentoring, and institutional support to strengthen instructional competence, teaching confidence, and professional growth across the seven PPST domains.

papers.title: Science for All: An Online Educational Resource (OER) Connecting the Filipino Teachers to International Science Competencies
papers.abstract: The continuous low performance of the Philippines in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) underscores an urgent crisis in national science education, characterized by resource scarcities and learning competencies lagging years behind international benchmarks. While the Department of Education launched the streamlined MATATAG Curriculum to focus on foundational skills, secondary science teachers face persistent barriers, including inadequate training and a lack of digital materials that explicitly bridge national goals with global standards. This developmental and evaluative study introduces "Science for All," a student- and teacher-friendly Online Educational Resource (OER) designed to close this gap for Grade 7 to Grade 10 science education.The conceptual and theoretical design of the OER is anchored on the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and Social Constructivism. The platform serves as a digital scaffold to transition educators from traditional lecture methods to inquiry-based, student-centered practices. Utilizing a mixed-methods research design, the study profiles the current TPACK readiness levels of fifteen (15) secondary science teachers in the Philippines. Following an intervention period where teachers utilize the OER and an accompanying video tutorial to implement an internationally aligned topic, their shifting competencies will be remeasured. Simultaneously, five (5) industry experts will evaluate the platform across three core domains: content validity, pedagogical soundness, and technical usability.Statistical treatments will include mean scores to measure localized TPACK competencies, percentages for expert evaluations, and a grouped T-test to determine if engaging with the OER significantly improves the teachers' readiness to implement international standards. Ultimately, this research aims to provide a sustainable, downloadable, and highly collaborative platform that empowers Filipino science educators and informs instructional designers.

authors.name: Diosa Madonna Melody ARCHE
authors.affiliation: Polytechnic University of the Philippines- Open University

papers.title: UTILIZATION OF GAMIFICATION AS A LEARNING TOOL IN TEACHING BIOMOLECULES AND CHEMICAL REACTIONS: A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN
papers.abstract: Gamification is a learner-centered approach that addresses persistent challenges in Chemistry achievement, such as misconceptions, low motivation, and reliance on conventional teaching methods. This study introduced EN-CHEM-TADIA, a validated gamified learning tool aligned with Chemistry content, to enhance Grade 10 students' achievement. Existing interventions often lack specificity, sustained engagement, and subject alignment; thus, EN-CHEM-TADIA was developed to target competencies in biomolecules and chemical reactions. Using a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design, the study involved 76 students during the School Year 2025–2026, who were divided into an experimental and a control group. A validated assessment aligned with the Department of Education Most Essential Learning Competencies (MELCs) was administered before and after the intervention. Findings revealed that the experimental group exposed to EN-CHEM-TADIA achieved significantly higher posttest mean scores for both biomolecules and chemical reactions than the control group, with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001). These results confirm that EN-CHEM-TADIA significantly enhances learners' Chemistry achievement, demonstrating that well-designed and validated gamified learning tools can serve as effective instructional materials. Overall, the study underscores the potential of gamification as an innovative strategy for improving engagement, conceptual understanding, and academic performance in Chemistry education.
