items.title: Human-Centred AI in Higher Education: From Intelligent Technology to Ethical, Inclusive and Future-Ready Universities
items.speaker: Dr. Mohd Erfino JOHARI
items.bio: Dr. Mohd Erfino Johari is a Malaysian academic leader with over 30 years of experience in higher education governance, international academic diplomacy, public service, and corporate leadership. He currently serves as Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic and Internationalisation) at Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM), where he leads academic transformation, global partnerships, dual-degree initiatives and institutional internationalisation strategies. He previously served as Director of Industrial Linkages and Academic Internationalisation (ILAI) and contributes actively to university governance through Senate committees and scholarly editorial boards. His career spans significant roles within the Malaysian Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Higher Education, including service as Education Attaché for Malaysia in the United Kingdom and Ireland and later as Director & Counsellor (Education) at the Malaysian High Commission in New Zealand, advancing bilateral academic cooperation and cross-border education initiatives. He also held senior corporate leadership roles as Chief Corporate Officer and Acting Chief Marketing Officer, contributing expertise in strategic governance, institutional branding and organisational performance. Internationally engaged, he serves as Visiting Professor/Lecturer at Universidad De Ixtlahuaca Mexico, Universitas PGRI Indonesia, Universitas Nahdlatul Ulama Indonesia and Universitas Ahmad Dahlan Indonesia. Appointed as International Research Fellow at Shinawatra International University Thailand and the International Cultural Communication Center Malaysia (ICCCM). He was invited as Keynote Speaker at SCTE2025 in Cairo, Egypt. He currently holds ten research grants including the FRGS (MOHE) and published more than 20 indexed journal articles for the last 3 years across Scopus, Web of Science, ERA, and MyCite. His research has earned Best Paper Awards at ICAR2023 and ICAR2025, as well as the Best Presenter Award at ICAR2025. He holds a PhD from UPSI in Education, a Master's degree from OUM, and a Bachelor's degree from University of Jordan, with additional qualifications in education, management and counselling. His research focuses on Geo-Islamica education, Shariah-compliant governance, higher education policy, internationalisation strategy and nation-building. Guided by principles of integrity, inclusivity, and service, he continues to advance globally connected universities and future-ready graduates through scholarship, diplomacy, and strategic academic leadership.
items.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) rapidly redefines the global educational landscape, higher education institutions stand at a critical crossroads. The mandate facing academic leaders is no longer merely adopting intelligent technologies, but strategically steering them to serve human flourishing, educational equity and institutional resilience. This keynote outlines a comprehensive framework for embedding Human-Centred AI (HCAI) across university ecosystems by integrating the universal ethical principles of Maqasid Shariah (the higher objectives of Islamic law). By translating these profound objectives, the preservation of values, human dignity, intellect, future generations and equitable resources, into a modern techno-academic context, the presentation offers a robust philosophical and practical model for AI governance. Drawing from strategic initiatives at Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM), the session addresses five interconnected pillars: ethical governance, authentic assessment, inclusive pedagogy, responsible innovation and sustainable institutional transformation. Ultimately, this presentation advocates for a balanced academic ecosystem where intelligent technology and human wisdom co-exist to prepare ethical leaders for an automated world.

papers.title: Predicting Students' Academic Performance Using Machine Learning Regression Models Based on Socioeconomic and Behavioral Factors
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of machine learning regression models to predict students' academic performance using socioeconomic and behavioral factors. Utilizing the Student Performance Metrics Dataset, we investigated models including Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Decision Tree, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The dataset integrates variables such as academic background, family income, attendance, computer skills, and extracurricular involvement. After preprocessing and encoding, four regression models were trained and evaluated using multiple metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R²). Results revealed that Decision Tree Regression outperformed other models with an R² score of 0.8898, highlighting its ability to capture non-linear patterns in student data. The study aims to support educators in identifying at-risk students and implementing targeted interventions based on predictive insights.

papers.title: ACTIVE LISTENING SKILLS AND THE CONFLICT MANAGEMENT STYLE OF CHARGE NURSES IN THE SPECIALTY UNITS OF SELECTED HOSPITALS
papers.abstract: Introduction Active listening is a vital nursing skill that involves fully concentrating, understanding, and responding to patients and colleagues, thereby promoting effective communication, patient safety, and quality care. Methodology This descriptive quantitative study highlighted the critical role of active listening in nursing practice by examining how it shapes the conflict management styles of charge nurses in the specialty units of selected hospitals. Data were gathered using the Active Listening Skills of the Charge Nurses by Steven L. McShane (2000) and Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (2000). Frequency, Weighted Mean, and Pearson's r were used. Findings Most of the nurses were 22-35 years old, male, 2 to 5 years of work experience, and less than two years as charge nurse. They have a high level of active listening skills in terms of avoiding interruption, maintaining interest, postponing evaluation, organizing information, and showing interest; they utilized avoiding most frequently as conflict management strategy. There was no correlation between level of active listening, age, gender, length of experience, and as charge nurse. There was a moderate positive correlation between competing and age; weak negative correlation between accommodating, competing and their length of experience as a charge nurse. There was a significant positive relationship between avoiding interruption and compromising; a negative relationship between maintaining interest and avoiding; and a positive relationship between showing interest, accommodating and collaborating. Conclusion In conclusion, while charge nurses demonstrated high levels of active listening and a tendency to use avoidance in conflict management, only selected aspects of listening skills showed significant relationships with specific conflict management styles, indicating the need for targeted communication development in nursing leadership.

papers.title: TRAINING NEEDS ASSESSMENT AMONG MIDDLE – LEVEL NURSE MANAGERS IN A SPECIALIZED TERTIARY HOSPITAL IN QUEZON CITY
papers.abstract: Introduction Training Needs Assessment (TNA) has emerged as a systematic approach to identifying competency gaps and aligning training programs with actual role requirements in healthcare settings. Methodology This partial sequential explanatory study assessed the level of importance of the training needs of middle-level nurse managers at a specialized tertiary hospital in Quezon City, using the Hennessy-Hick's Training Needs Questionnaire. Findings Most of the middle-level manager nurses were 31-40-year-old, female, married, and BSN holder; have high level of importance of training needs for all the domains (research and audits, administrative and technical, communication and teamwork, management and supervisory, and clinical activities). There is significant relationships between level of importance of training needs: and age in the domain clinical activities; and sex in the domains: communication and teamwork and clinical activities. Problems encountered by the middle level nurse managers in terms of their current skills and competencies in the areas requiring professional development were: limited knowledge in conducting clinical audits; low application of evidence-based practice; poor patient flow and long waiting times; low understanding of insurance & billing processes; inefficient stock and supply management; poor time and schedule management; communication breakdown between professionals; weak interdisciplinary collaboration; ineffective unit/ward leadership; weak performance monitoring; and errors in Electronic Health Records. Conclusion Middle-level nurse managers expressed high training needs across various domains, while facing critical challenges such as limited clinical audit knowledge, poor evidence-based practice application, communication issues, and management inefficiencies that impact their professional performance and patient care.

papers.title: POLYGON: A Raspberry Pi-Based 3D Printing Machine using Recyclable Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) Bottles as Filament
papers.abstract: Plastic bottle waste is one of the most visible environmental problems in schools and communities today, yet most of these discarded bottles are simply thrown away despite their potential to be transformed into something useful. At the same time, 3D printing, a technology that can turn digital designs into real physical objects remains largely unavailable in many schools because the materials it requires are too expensive. This study explored whether used PET plastic bottles could be recycled and converted into 3D printing filament using a machine built around a Raspberry Pi microcontroller, making 3D printing more environmentally responsible for schools like the City College of Tagaytay. The developed machine automates the conversion process of melting and reshaping plastic waste into filament, carefully controlling the temperature and speed of the process using an Arduino Uno microncontroller to produce consistent and usable output. The resulting filament is then fed into the next part of the system to print three-dimensional objects, creating a complete cycle from waste to finished product. To make the machine use simple, both filament creating and 3D printing process are both controllable via the built-in Android tablet, wirelessly. Testing and evaluation confirmed that the prototype successfully performs its intended functions while also serving as a viable alternative to commercial filament, embodying the Industry 4.0 standards whilst aiming to contribute to the United Nations' SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, alongside SDG9 and SDG 11.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of TikTok Influencers in Influencing Purchase Decision for Skincare Products in Districts 1, 2, and 3 of Manila
papers.abstract: Introduction: This study examined the effectiveness of TikTok Affiliate Creators, Celebrity Key Opinion Leaders, and Professional Key Opinion Leaders in influencing skincare purchase decisions in Districts 1, 2, and 3 of Manila. The research compared these influencer types based on relatability, popularity, and credibility to determine how these attributes affect consumers' variety-seeking buying behavior. Methodology: The researchers employed a quantitative descriptive-comparative and correlational design. Data were gathered through a structured, self-administered survey questionnaire distributed to 385 active TikTok users, aged 18 to 29, who have purchased skincare products within the last 12 months. The data were analyzed using weighted mean, standard deviation, Multiple Linear Regression Analysis, Friedman Test, Durbin-Conover Procedure, Repeated Measures ANOVA, and Tukey Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) to find the significant relationships and differences. Findings: Professional Key Opinion Leaders were the most effective influencer type in driving skincare purchase decisions due to their credibility and expertise. Affiliate Creators ranked second, effectively leveraging relatability and authentic demonstrations. Celebrity Key Opinion Leaders ranked lowest among the three types. Credibility emerged as the strongest attribute affecting purchase decisions, whereas popularity showed the weakest influence. Furthermore, TikTok influencer marketing significantly encouraged variety-seeking buying behavior among the respondents. Conclusion: The study concludes that formal expertise and relatable trust are more persuasive to consumers than massive celebrity followings. Consequently, the researchers proposed a TikTok Influencer Marketing Framework grounded in Ohanian's Source Credibility Theory (1990). This framework guides skincare brands and marketers to prioritize Professional Key Opinion Leaders for final purchase decisions, utilize Affiliate Creators for consumer engagement, and leverage Celebrity Key Opinion Leaders strictly for initial brand awareness within the social commerce industry.
keywords: TikTok. Skincare. Influencers. Attributes. Purchase Decision

papers.title: The Relationship Between Lifestyle and Consumer Purchasing Behavior of the Nocturnal Workforce in the City of Manila: Basis for Creating Business Opportunities for BPO Companies
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) industry has expanded the number of employees working non-traditional schedules, particularly night shifts, creating lifestyle patterns that differ significantly from those of daytime workers. Despite the increasing presence of this nocturnal workforce, limited local research has examined how these lifestyle changes influence consumer purchasing behavior, particularly within the context of the City of Manila. This study aimed to examine the relationship between lifestyle and consumer purchasing behavior among night shift BPO employees and explore how these insights may serve as a basis for identifying business opportunities for companies operating in the nighttime economy. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design. Data were collected from 336 night shift BPO employees through a structured survey questionnaire. Statistical tools used for analysis included frequency distribution, weighted mean, Pearson's correlation coefficient, and multiple linear regression to determine relationships among variables. Findings revealed that night shift work significantly influences employees' lifestyle, particularly in terms of disrupted sleep patterns, limited social interaction outside the workplace, inconsistent physical activity, unhealthy dietary habits, and stress-related coping behaviors. These lifestyle conditions were found to shape consumer purchasing behavior, with employees tending to prioritize convenience, accessibility, energy-boosting products, and immediate consumption needs when making purchasing decisions. The study further established a significant relationship between lifestyle and consumer purchasing behavior, with demographic factors influencing the strength of this relationship. The study concludes that the distinct routines associated with night shift work directly affect purchasing behaviors, highlighting opportunities for businesses and BPO companies to develop products, services, and workplace initiatives tailored to the needs of the nocturnal workforce.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of Meme Content Style and Traditional Advertising on the Cognitive, Affective, and Conative Perception of Generation Z in the City of Manila
papers.abstract: Meme content style advertising, which relies on humor, satire, and cultural relevance, has become a prominent alternative to traditional advertising's structured, factual approach, yet limited research has directly compared the two among Generation Z consumers in the City of Manila. This study examined how each format influences consumer perception across cognitive, affective, and conative dimensions, and whether the two differ significantly in informativeness, entertainment, and irritation. The study employed a comparative, quantitative research design using a structured four-point Likert survey distributed to 400 Generation Z respondents (ages 18–29) in Manila, all of whom had prior exposure to both advertising formats. Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation) profiled each format's perceived effectiveness, while a Paired Sample T-test determined whether differences between formats were statistically significant. Results showed Traditional Advertising scored higher in Informativeness (M \= 3.281) than Meme Content Style Advertising (M \= 2.961), while Meme Content Style Advertising scored higher in Entertainment (M \= 3.520 vs. 3.016) and was perceived as slightly less irritating. Both formats received high Cognitive scores with no significant difference (p \= 0.385), but Meme Content Style Advertising significantly outperformed Traditional Advertising in Affective, Conative, and overall Consumer Perception (all p < 0.001, Cohen's d \= -0.303, small-to-moderate effect). The study concludes that Traditional Advertising remains the more credible source of product information, while Meme Content Style Advertising is more effective at emotionally engaging Generation Z and driving behavioral intentions such as sharing and purchase consideration. These findings suggest marketers should adopt a balanced strategy — using traditional formats to build credibility and meme-based content to drive engagement and action.

authors.name: Julian Echaluce
authors.affiliation: Acosta, Felicity May T., Aguirre, Margarette T., Balatero, Faith F., Borja, Alexa Mae T., Guillen, Ashley Mae L., Rondina, Ronnelyn Kate B.

papers.title: Development of a Mobile PLC-based Power Backup System
papers.abstract: The research, titled The Development of a Mobile PLC-Based Hybrid Power Backup System, was thoroughly researched and designed for the primary purpose of providing a reliable, portable and durable emergency power supply. This is designed as contingency system to provide stable flow of electrical power supply while ensuring unimpeded operability even in the most testing environment midst spontaneous grid failures, instant power interruptions, and irregular or possibly damaging voltage excesses. This compact system contains a PLC, solar panel, battery with inverter and charge controller and a transfer mechanism for 220V power supply. The PLC (programmable logic controller) is responsible for monitoring conditions and switching between AC mains and solar backup. This is ideal for residential, commercial and duplex. The performance tests for discharge, capacity and voltage regulation were carried out on the battery. Performance evaluation included battery discharge, capacity, and voltage regulation tests. Results demonstrated that the developed system successfully transferred power with no delay, maintained stable output voltage, and sustained connected loads during utility power outages. The integration of renewable solar energy also reduced dependence on conventional electricity while improving energy efficiency. In conclusion, the developed Mobile PLC-Based Hybrid Power Backup System proved to be an effective, reliable, and sustainable backup power solution capable of providing uninterrupted electrical service while promoting the utilization of clean energy resources. Results demonstrated that the developed system successfully transferred power within a short response time, maintained stable output voltage, and sustained connected loads during utility power outages. The integration of renewable solar energy also reduced dependence on conventional electricity while improving energy efficiency. Overall, the developed Mobile PLC-Based Hybrid Power Backup System proved to be an effective, reliable, and sustainable backup power solution capable of providing uninterrupted electrical service.

papers.title: ETHICAL LEADERSHIP ON PERFORMANCE AND TURNOVER INTENTION AMONG HOSPITAL EMPLOYEES: A CONVERGENT PARALLEL ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: Ethical leadership and employee performance can significantly influence turnover intentions. Specifically, ethical leadership has been shown to negatively impact turnover intentions. Conversely, ethical leadership is positively linked to performance. This mixed methods research made use of the convergent parallel research design to correlate ethical leadership, performance, and turnover intention and explore the experiences on ethical leadership, performance, and turnover intention among 324 hospital employees in a private hospital in Mandaue City for the first half of 2025. Findings revealed that the ethical leadership was very high. Moral manager, moral person, and overall ethical leadership were very high. Qualitative findings converges with the findings on ethical leadership. Overall, the performance was high. Task and contextual performance were rated as high while counterproductive work behavior was low. The overall performance was high. Qualitative findings converges with quantitative data as informants were able to provide how work performance is being measured and is affected by technology and leadership and that it is influenced by different contributing factors. The turnover intention was moderate. Qualitative findings converges with quantitative data where informants view turnover intention is a normal phenomenon needing to be addressed and that in an organization there are several factors that contribute to a high and low turnover intention. Moral manager, moral person and overall ethical leadership were correlated with task, contextual performance and overall performance. Moral person and overall ethical leadership were correlated with counterproductive work behavior while moral manager was not. The moral manager and moral person and the overall ethical leadership was not correlated with turnover intention. Task, contextual performance, counterproductive work behavior and overall performance were not correlated with turnover intention. Based on the findings an emergent model was created and a retention plan was proposed.

papers.title: REPORTING BEHAVIOR AND PERCEPTION OF NURSES IN SAN LAZARO HOSPITAL REGARDING MEDICATION ERRORS
papers.abstract: Introduction Medication errors are among the most common medical errors, harming at least 1.5 million people every year. Methodology This descriptive-correlational determined the reporting behavior and perception of nurses regarding medication errors. Data were gathered using the revised Modified Gladstone (2001). Mean, Standard Deviation, One-Way Anova, and Pearsons were used for statistical treatment. Findings Results of the study showed that most of the respondents were 31- 40 years old; female; single; bachelor's degree; working for 10 years and above; working 8 hours shift; assigned in the adult department; mostly has no medication errors during their career; mostly informed through DOHP (Discussions with Other Healthcare Professionals); with only 1 incident report during their career; has a high level of perceptions regarding medication errors; mostly reporting errors to nurse manager; has moderate level of nurses' perception regarding medication errors: whether or not a medication error occurred; whether or not the physician should be notified; whether or not an incident report should be completed; has moderate perceived level of confidence regarding view on reporting medication errors; has significant difference between level of nurses' perception regarding medication errors and their profile work shift; lastly, there is a significant relationship between the level of nurses' perception regarding medication errors and their perceived level of confidence regarding their view on reporting medication errors. The problems encountered by nurses in terms of reporting medication errors were professional, managerial, work-related, and personal factors. Conclusion Nurses generally demonstrate high awareness of medication error conditions but face persistent barriers to reporting. Understanding these behaviors provides actionable evidence for designing innovative, nurse-led safety models that reinforce quality, safety, and sustainable healthcare delivery.

papers.title: Relapse and Recovery: Exploring the Lived Experiences and Personal Journeys of Patients in Rehabilitation Centers
papers.abstract: Background: Substance use disorder stays as a crucial public health concern, with relapse presenting a constant challenge in achieving sustained recovery. Despite the availability of rehabilitation programs, many existing studies strengthen clinical and quantitative outcomes while neglecting the profundity of the lived experiences of the patients. Objective: This study aims to explore and understand the lived experiences and personal journeys of patients in rehabilitation centers, with particular focus on factors influencing relapse, recovery processes, and coping mechanisms. Methods: A quantitative phenomenological research design was employed to capture the subjective experiences of individuals undergoing rehabilitation in selected centers in Cebu City, Philippines. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth, semi- structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and core themes related to relapse and recovery. Results: Findings revealed that relapse and recovery are shaped by a complex interplay of psychosocial, environmental, and cultural factors. Key themes include the influence of social support systems, emotional and environmental triggers, effectiveness of rehabilitation programs, and the role of personal coping strategies. Participants highlighted that recovery is a nonlinear process, where relapse is often experienced as part of personal growth rather than failure. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of adopting a patient-centered and empathetic approach in rehabilitation practices. Understanding the lived experiences of patients provides valuable insights for healthcare professionals, policymakers, and rehabilitation institutions in improving intervention strategies and promoting long-term recovery.

papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF FINANCIAL SERVICES ACCESSIBILITY ON THE SAVINGS OPTIMIZATION OF MINIMUM WAGE EARNERSIN RODRIGUEZ, RIZAL
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The study analyzes how financial services accessibility influences the savings optimization of the minimum wage earners residing in San Jose, Rodriguez, Rizal. Using a descriptive-correlational research design and quantitative approach, the researchers gathered data from 93 respondents using a self-made printed questionnaire that was reliability tested using the Cronbach's Alpha and uses purposive sampling technique to ensure the validity and accuracy of the data. The results have revealed that the financial services accessibility – alongside its factors: affordability, availability, awareness, ease of use, and safety and reliability – significantly influences the savings optimization of the minimum wage earners in terms of their savings behaviors, ability, and planning. The findings show that when a financial service is accessible, minimum wage earners adopt formal financial systems that lead to improved financial stability and savings habits.

papers.title: Hyper-Personalized AI Recommendations and Parasocial Trust in Influencers: Effects on Online Consumer Decisions in Quezon City
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of hyper-personalized artificial intelligence (AI) recommendations and parasocial trust in influencers on online consumer decisions among residents of Quezon City. In today's highly digitalized environment, consumers are increasingly exposed to AI-driven recommendations and influencer-generated content that shape their purchasing behavior. Anchored on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) Theory, the study investigates how technological and social stimuli influence consumer perceptions and behavioral responses in online purchasing contexts. A quantitative research design was employed using descriptive and inferential methods. Data were collected from 104 respondents aged 30 to 45 who actively use social media and engage in online shopping. A structured questionnaire measured hyper-personalized AI recommendations in terms of perceived personalization and accuracy, parasocial trust in terms of interaction and trust in influencers, and online consumer decisions in terms of purchase intention and actual behavior. Multiple regression analysis was utilized to determine the predictive effects of the independent variables. Findings revealed that respondents generally perceive AI recommendations positively, particularly for enhancing convenience and facilitating shopping decisions, although perceptions of accuracy remain moderate. Parasocial interaction and trust in influencers were also found to be at a moderate level, indicating cautious consumer attitudes toward influencer endorsements. Online consumer behavior was influenced more strongly during the information search and evaluation stages rather than in directly triggering purchases. The results further indicated that both hyper-personalized AI recommendations and parasocial trust significantly influence and predict online consumer decisions, with AI recommendations demonstrating a stronger predictive effect. The study concludes that consumer decision-making is shaped by the combined influence of data-driven personalization and social trust mechanisms. It highlights the importance of integrating transparent AI systems with authentic influencer strategies to enhance consumer engagement and decision-making in digital marketing environments.

papers.title: THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF NURSES CARING FOR DOMESTICALLY ABUSED PATIENTS IN CEBU CITY
papers.abstract: Abstract Nurses caring for domestically abused patients encounter emotionally demanding situations that may negatively impact their psychological well-being and the quality of care delivered. Repeated exposure to trauma-related cases can lead to stress, compassion fatigue, and challenges in maintaining professional equilibrium. This study examines the lived experiences of nurses caring for domestically abused patients in Cebu City, with emphasis on their emotional responses, coping mechanisms, and professional challenges. A hermeneutic phenomenological approach was employed to gain deeper insight into participants' experiences. Five female nurses assigned to the Pink Room, each with at least one year of clinical experience, were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews and analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns and meanings. The analysis identified five themes: facing emotional challenges, effects of personal experience, need for preparedness, cultivating compassion, and seeking validation. Nurses reported emotional strain and secondary traumatic stress, but demonstrated resilience through coping strategies including peer support, self-reflection, and professional detachment. Insufficient training and support further contributed to these difficulties. The findings underscore the necessity for structured support, such as stress debriefing, mental health programs, and specialized training. Enhancing these interventions may improve nurses' well-being, strengthen coping mechanisms, and promote compassionate, effective care.

papers.title: Use, Reuse, and Disposal of Plastic Gallons (SDG 6) Towards Sustainable Plastic Waste Management (SDG 12)
papers.abstract: Use, Reuse, and Disposal of Plastic Gallons (SDG 6) Towards Sustainable Plastic Waste Management (SDG 12) https://orcid.org/0009-0006-3858-4664 By: Dr. James D. Marshall, FRIEdr, CSSYB Regular Full-Time Faculty, College of Accountancy, Business Administration, Hospitality and Tourism Management This study explores the use, reuse, and disposal of plastic gallons in Metro Manila's water refilling stations, with emphasis on sustainability practices aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 2030) 6 and 12. Using a qualitative approach, in-depth interviews were conducted with a water refilling station manager to examine handling, maintenance, and waste disposal processes. Thematic analysis revealed four major themes: (1) safe handling through regular cleaning and laboratory testing; (2) reuse supported by proper sanitation and customer orientation; (3) disposal mainly via junk shops due to financial and logistical limitations; and (4) sustainable improvements through recycling collaboration and application of the 3Rs. Findings highlight the importance of strengthening partnerships between local stations and recycling facilities while promoting environmental awareness and operational efficiency. The study concludes that small-scale water refilling stations can significantly contribute to sustainable plastic waste management through disciplined practices, policy support, and circular economy integration.

papers.title: Mobile Application for Assessing Anxiety of Students in City College of Tagaytay
papers.abstract: This study developed Calmademic, a mobile application designed to support the assessment and monitoring of anxiety among students of City College of Tagaytay. The application aims to provide a digital platform for the Guidance and Counseling Services Unit to facilitate more accessible and organized anxiety assessment and student monitoring. The application was developed for Android devices using Flutter and Dart, with Firebase as its database. It incorporated the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) for monthly assessment and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) for weekly assessment. Additional features included counseling appointment scheduling, mood tracking, therapeutic tasks, and interactive games intended to support students in managing their emotional well-being. The study utilized the Iterative Process Model in developing and refining the application based on user feedback and testing. The system underwent unit, integration, system, and user acceptance testing. Its quality was evaluated using the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality model involving 22 faculty, instructors, and clients and 277 students. The application obtained an overall mean rating of 4.58, interpreted as Excellent. The findings indicate that Calmademic can serve as a useful digital tool for supporting anxiety assessment, monitoring, and student well-being within the educational setting.

papers.title: SafeDrive: AI-Powered Driver Monitoring and Accident Prevention System
papers.abstract: Road accidents caused by driver fatigue and drowsiness are particularly prevalent among public utility bus drivers who operate over long distances and extended driving hours. In order to address this issue, this study presents SafeDrive, an AI-based driver monitoring system that employs computer vision, machine learning, and the Internet of Things to detect early signs of drowsiness in real-time. SafeDrive integrates multiple detection mechanisms including facial recognition, eye-closure detection, and behavioral cue analysis alongside GPS tracking and immediate audio and visual warnings. The system was implemented by utilizing Raspberry Pi 4B paired with peripherals such as Raspberry Pi NOIR V2 Camera, NEO-6M module, MPU 6050 module, OLED display, and a piezo buzzer to provide a compact and cost-effective solution that is suitable for deployment in public utility buses (PUB). The components work jointly to continuously monitor the state of PUB drivers during long drives and trigger visual and audio warnings to alert the driver when it detects early signs of drowsiness. The alert logs are recorded locally and sent to SafeDrive's companion website when WiFi connectivity is present. Through that, the administrators of the company can monitor the driver's condition continuously. A field test was conducted to evaluate the system through a Victory Liner bus along the Olongapo to Cubao route. The results showed 100% accuracy during evening testing, while the morning testing showed a decreased accuracy of 20.56% due to misalignment of the device and obstruction of the facial feature. The system records an average latency of 57.75 ms per frame or around 17.3 fps, and the user acceptance average indicates a positive system acceptance with a mean of 3.80 and 3.00 for reliability. The study concludes that the system effectively enables real-time monitoring and its applicability in reducing fatigue-related accidents and improving road safety among provincial bus drivers.

papers.title: Assessing the Contribution of Talipapa Markets and Supportive Agricultural Policies to Non-Farm Income Generation of Smallholder Farmers in the Philippines
papers.abstract: Philippine smallholder farmers increasingly depend on non-farm income for livelihood diversification to buffer against farm risk. This paper estimated the importance of talipapa markets to the non-farm income of these farmers and examined their perceptions towards favorable agricultural policies. The contribution of these informal markets, as well as the perception of farmers on related policies, was, however, not previously quantified. Through a non-experimental descriptive-quantitative type of design, the research involved 118 smallholder farmers in Central Luzon and was undertaken by using the structured interview. Data included socio-demographics, sources of income (including talipapa-related), perceived effectiveness of policies, and preference for new interventions. Percentage analysis (for income contribution) and means of the rated Likert Scale (for perceptions) were used. The reliability (Cronbach's Alpha: 0.80-0.85) and validity of the research tool were high. Findings showed that talipapa-related non-farm activities account for a substantial portion (23.4 percent) of the total household income, highlighting their economic terms of reference. Farmers rate current agricultural policies as Moderately Effective" to "Effective"; there remains considerable scope for improvement. High priority responses included specific micro-credit, good marketing training, and better market infrastructure. In sum, talipapa markets are critical to the livelihood of smallholder farmers as a primary non-farm income-generating activity. In conclusion, short policies need to be refined to enable discriminating access to finance, strengthen extension, and logistics for the markets, while allowing for a glued regulatory environment to make the most of these informal markets for sustainable rural development.

papers.title: Swipe, Click, Book: Exploring the Influence of Digital Marketing on Hotel Booking Decisions using Third Party Platforms among Millennials.
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of digital marketing has reshaped the hospitality industry, particularly in how millennials make hotel booking decisions through third-party platforms. This study, Swipe, Click, Book: Exploring the Influence of Digital Marketing on Hotel Booking Decisions using Third Party Platforms among Millennials, investigates the role of digital strategies—such as social media ads, influencer endorsements, email campaigns, and online reviews—in shaping consumer behavior. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework, the research examines millennials' perceptions of usefulness, ease of use, and behavioral intention toward platforms like Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com. A descriptive quantitative design was employed, with purposive and random sampling targeting millennials aged 29–44 residing in Quezon City who have booked at least once through third-party applications. Data were collected via structured surveys and analyzed using frequency distribution, weighted mean, Likert scaling, and regression analysis. Results reveal that the majority of respondents (67%) fall within the 29–33 age range, with Agoda.com emerging as the most preferred platform (52%). Travel frequency is largely occasional, with 53% traveling only once a year, though a notable 17% travel more than three times annually. Findings highlight that integrated search engine results and user reviews are perceived as the most useful digital marketing tools, while ease of navigation and mobile convenience strongly influence platform adoption. The study concludes that digital marketing strategies significantly affect millennials' hotel booking decisions, with transparency, trust, and user-friendly design emerging as critical factors. Recommendations include prioritizing review integration, enhancing search visibility, and leveraging influencer-driven content to engage millennials effectively. By aligning digital marketing with millennial preferences, hotels and booking platforms can strengthen customer loyalty, optimize engagement, and remain competitive in a tech-driven hospitality landscape.

papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF GREEN MARKETING PRACTICES ON CONSUMER BUYING BEHAVIOR IN SELECTED COFFEE SHOPS OF BRGY. BATASAN HILLS, QUEZON CITY
papers.abstract: Green marketing has become an important approach in the coffee shop industry as businesses respond to growing environmental awareness among consumers. Nevertheless, there aren't many local studies that concentrate on how green marketing strategies influence consumers buying behavior in small, neighborhood coffee shops. The purpose of this study was to determine how green marketing strategies influence consumer's buying behavior in selected coffee shops in Barangay Batasan Hills, Quezon City. Regular coffee shop patrons were given a structured survey questionnaire as part of a descriptive-quantitative research design. The study looked at consumer purchasing behavior in terms of purchase decision and post-purchase evaluation, as well as green marketing strategies in terms of social responsibility and environmental consciousness. The results showed that consumers believed green marketing strategies had a significant influence on their buying behavior. The findings revealed that green marketing practices were interpreted as very influential in influencing consumer buying behavior. Being environmentally conscious had a strong influence on purchasing decisions, and social responsibility had a significant influence on consumers' willingness to support and recommend coffee shops. The findings also revealed a significant relationship between green marketing practices and consumers' buying behavior. From the findings, the study concludes that effective green marketing practices can have a positive impact on consumer behavior and can enhance customer support for coffee shops in the local setting of the Philippines. The study has provided valuable insights for coffee shop owners to develop effective green marketing strategies.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF GRAB PH ADVERTISEMENTS TO THE PURCHASING DECISION OF GEN Z IN BARANGAY NORTH FAIRVIEW
papers.abstract: This study examined the impact of Grab PH advertisements on the purchasing decisions of Generation Z consumers residing in Barangay North Fairview. Utilizing a quantitative descriptive correlational research design, data were gathered from 130 respondents aged 18 to 26 through purposive sampling and a structured 5-point Likert scale survey. Demographic findings revealed that most respondents were aged 21–23, predominantly female, and had a monthly allowance below ₱5,000. Facebook emerged as the primary platform for advertisement exposure. Statistical analysis using Pearson's Correlation yielded a coefficient of 0.706, indicating a significant moderate positive relationship between Grab PH advertisement factors and the purchase decision process. The study found that while the advertisements' content clarity and platform appropriateness were highly rated, the long-term recall of these advertisements was comparatively lower. The researchers rejected the null hypothesis, concluding that Grab PH advertisements significantly shape the information search and alternative evaluation stages of the Gen Z consumer journey. Recommendations include enhancing advertisement creativity and utilizing multi-platform coordinated strategies to improve brand engagement and long-term recall among young consumers.

papers.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF MARKETING STRATEGIES OF SELECTED COFFEE SHOPS IN QUEZON CITY: A CUSTOMER-BASED STUSY FOR DEVELOPING A STRATEGIC MARKETING PLAN
papers.abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of marketing strategies of selected coffee shops in Barangay Commonwealth, Quezon City using the 7Ps of the marketing mix framework. The primary objective was to assess customer perceptions of product, price, place, promotion, people, process, and physical evidence, and to determine whether evaluations differ across demographic groups. A quantitative descriptive research design was employed, utilizing a structured survey questionnaire administered to 150 customers. Data were analyzed using frequency distribution, weighted mean, and nonparametric tests to identify differences in perception based on sex, occupation, and income level. Findings indicate that the customer base is predominantly composed of female, student, and lower-income respondents, suggesting a youth-driven and price-sensitive market. Overall, the marketing mix elements were positively evaluated, with particularly high ratings for service reliability, staff approachability, cleanliness, ambiance, and product presentation. Pricing and promotional strategies were also viewed favorably, especially in terms of value for money and promotional offers. However, comparatively lower ratings were observed in product creativity and digital service availability, indicating areas for improvement. Statistical tests showed no significant differences in perceptions across sex, occupation, and income for most marketing mix elements, except for physical evidence, where variation was noted between occupational groups. The study concludes that current marketing strategies generally meet customer expectations and have broad demographic appeal, but enhancements in innovation and physical environment features may further strengthen competitiveness and customer satisfaction.

papers.title: HOUSEHOLD LEVEL OF AWARENESS AND COMPLIANCE WITH LGU's SEWAGE MANAGEMENT POLICIES
papers.abstract: The study aimed to assess household level of awareness and compliance with the LGU's sewage management policies in Tayabas City. It addressed the respondents' demographic profile and examined differences in awareness and compliance across demographic groups, as well as the relationship between awareness and compliance within households. An informative video was also developed based on the findings to increase awareness and compliance regarding City Ordinance No. 24-02, also known as the Sewage and Septage Management Ordinance of the City of Tayabas. This study employed a quantitative approach using descriptive-survey, descriptive-evaluative, descriptive-comparative, and descriptive-correlational designs. A total of 369 household heads were purposively selected using two-stage cluster sampling. A self-developed, validated, and pilot-tested survey questionnaire was used to collect data, which were analyzed using appropriate statistical tools. The findings revealed a diverse demographic profile in terms of income, household size, and residential location, with most households belonging to the lower income bracket, having small family sizes, and residing in cluster 3. Significant differences in awareness and compliance were observed across residential locations, and a strong relationship between awareness and compliance was identified. The study concluded that households in Tayabas City are highly aware of and compliant with City Ordinance No. 24-02.

papers.title: LettuVault: An Auto-Regulating Storage Box for Lactuca Sativa with Image Processing for Postharvest Logistics
papers.abstract: STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM: Traditional postharvest storage and transportation of leafy vegetables in the Philippines are often unregulated, leading to rapid moisture loss and physical deterioration. Lettuce (Lactuca sativa), being highly perishable, typically reaches unmarketable states within 1–4 days under ambient tropical conditions. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY: The research employed a developmental - experimental design conducted over a 10-day trial period. Ten samples were categorized into four primary groups: LettuVault (Experimental), Commercial Refrigeration (Reference Benchmark), and two Ambient Controls. The system utilized an ESP32- regulated sensor network to monitor real-time environmental data, while a YOLOv8 deep learning model was integrated for automated anomaly and freshness detection. Preservation efficacy was quantitatively measured through weight retention percentages and a 10-point Visual Freshness Scale (VFS) mapped to the established Kader Index. SUMMARY OF THE FINDINGS: The technical analysis showed that the BME280 sensor had 99.02% and 99.71% accuracy rates of temperature and humidity respectively. The system was able to stabilize the inside microclimate at temperatures between 15°C and 18°C, and this kept the produce out of harm from changes in temperature in the surroundings. With regards to preservation, the LettuVault was able to increase the marketable life of the lettuce to 8 days or more, remarkably higher than ambient storage which indicated severe deterioration in 3.5 days. The image processing module had an 85% accuracy rate in detecting lettuce and 70% in detecting wilting but low 55% accuracy in detecting worms. Moreover, the IoT surveillance app reached 100% notification delivery rate, and the responding time of all triggered events was less than a second.

papers.title: Human Resource Management Strategies and Economic Stability of Virtual Assistants: The Mediating Roles of Work Engagement and Job Autonomy and the Moderating Effect of Work–Life Balance
papers.abstract: Despite the increasing significance of the role of virtual assistants in the digital economy, there is no empirical research that explores the interaction between HRM practices, job satisfaction, job autonomy, work engagement, work-life balance, and economic stability. The current research addresses these gaps by examining the linkage among variables and provides a full picture of the direct and indirect effect of HRM interventions on the job satisfaction and financial well-being using the motivation, autonomy and work-life balance. Quantitative research design was used, with 146 active virtual assistants selected using snowball sampling. The findings indicated that work engagement played a partial mediating role between the influence of HRM strategies on job satisfaction (axb=0.278, 38%, p<.001) and economic stability (axb=0.334, 34.5%, p<.001), which emphasizes the role of promoting employee energy, commitment, and absorption in remote work. Job autonomy was established as a weak mediator (axb=0.0410, 5.6%; axb=0.0882, 9.11%, p<.001), which shows that autonomy is a contributor to a smaller extent than the predominant role of HRM strategies. The work-life balance did not have any significant moderation effects on the tested relationships (p=0.589; p=0.806, ns), but it exhibited significant direct effects on employee outcomes, indicating that WLB should be regarded more as an independent predictor and contextual variable rather than a moderator. The results underscore the importance of HR policies that enhance autonomy, promote equitable and supportive HRM systems, and support work-life balance, while contributing to SDG 3, SDG 8, and SDG 10 through the promotion of healthy and inclusive remote work practices.

papers.title: Assessment of Light Aircraft Safety: Defect Detection and Component Life
papers.abstract: The safety and reliability of light aircraft are paramount concerns in the aviation industry. Effective non-destructive testing (NDT) methods play a crucial role in detecting defects and assessing the remaining life of critical components. However, more research needs to be conducted on the specific NDT practices employed in the light aircraft domain. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the NDT knowledge and practices of apprentice mechanics and aircraft mechanics working on light aircraft. The findings provide valuable insights into the current state of NDT implementation and highlight the need for enhanced training and adoption of advanced techniques to improve light aircraft safety and maintenance. The study on the assessment of light aircraft safety, defect detection, and component life involved 30 participants: 15 apprentice mechanics and 15 aircraft mechanics. The results revealed that the participants' average age was 28.4 years, with a standard deviation of 5.2 years. The average length of experience in the field was 3.8 years for apprentice mechanics and 11.2 years for aircraft mechanics. The findings also showed that apprentice mechanics scored lower on the NDT knowledge questionnaire compared to aircraft mechanics, with average scores of 62% and 84%, respectively. Both apprentice mechanics and aircraft mechanics reported using general visual inspection and dye penetrant testing as the primary NDT methods for light aircraft. Other NDT techniques, such as eddy current testing, ultrasonic testing, and magnetic particle inspection, were rarely or never used by the participants. The study also found that apprentice mechanics were more likely to rely solely on general visual inspection. In contrast, aircraft mechanics were more likely to supplement visual inspection with dye penetrant testing. Additionally, years of experience in the field positively correlated with the use of dye penetrant testing, with more experienced mechanics being more likely to employ this technique.

papers.title: An Evaluation of Document Image Enhancement Techniques for OCR on Degraded Barangay Clearance Form
papers.abstract: Introduction: Barangay clearance is among the most widely issued Philippine administrative documents, yet many barangays still store paper records subject to fading, folding, bleed-through, and low-quality photocopying. Optical character recognition (OCR) on degraded scans often produces errors that require manual re-encoding, delaying digitization. Although enhancement-first OCR pipelines have been evaluated on Southeast Asian administrative forms, Vietnamese government documents (Bui et al., 2025) and Thai transcripts (Wattanacheep et al., 2025), no peer-reviewed study has assessed such pipelines on Philippine administrative forms. A review of 1,019 papers found no counterpart study. This study evaluates enhancement techniques on barangay clearance forms as a representative case. Methodology: The study constructs the Philippine Administrative Document (PAD) Dataset from blank barangay clearance templates with synthetic fill-in data and simulated degradation (bleed-through, ink fading, low-DPI photocopy, folding, ink bleed). Two approaches are compared: classical preprocessing (deskew, CLAHE, Otsu binarization) and deep learning (DIBCO-trained U-Net binarization). OCR accuracy on printed text fields is measured using Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER) with Tesseract, PaddleOCR, and EasyOCR, with and without enhancement. PSNR and SSIM serve as secondary metrics. Cross-dataset validation uses the DIBCO benchmark. Findings: The evaluation quantifies whether enhancement reduces OCR errors versus unprocessed images and which technique performs better under identical conditions. Expected outcomes include before-and-after comparisons across three OCR engines, barangay clearance baselines, and an ethics-compliant benchmark without real personal data. Conclusion: Results will inform preprocessing for barangay record digitization and support AI-driven local government document management. The contribution is empirical evidence and reusable OCR performance baselines for Philippine administrative forms.

papers.title: EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT AND CREATIVE PERFORMANCE DURING COVID-19 PANDEMIC BASIS FOR SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTIVITY IN SELECTED TELECOMMUNICATION COMPANIES
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of employee engagement on creative performance and the interactions between these variables in fostering sustainable productivity among employees at selected telecommunication companies in the Philippines. In a more dynamic work environment, organizations need to ensure a high degree of employee motivation, teamwork, and flexibility to ensure the sustainability of organizational performance and competitive advantage. The study found essential dimensions of employee engagement, namely vigor, dedication, and absorption, and investigated their association with creative performance, including task performance, contextual performance, and adaptive performance. Additionally, the study assessed how organizational practices, such as training and development programs, reward systems, and employee support initiatives, influence employee behavior and overall productivity. A quantitative research design was used, with survey data being collected from employees of the sampled telecommunication companies. Statistical tests were used to analyze the relationship between the variables in the study. The results indicated that v employees typically exhibited a high degree of engagement, creative performance, and productivity. Although some demographic variables were statistically significant predictors of employee engagement and creative performance, their overall impact was small, which means that organizational practices and workplace support systems have a more significant impact. Using these findings, the study suggests that organizations should have organized and long-term plans that would work towards improving employee engagement, creative performance, and employee well-being. In addition, the proposed study includes the implementation of the ENGAGE+ Sustainable Productivity Program (SPP) that combines engagement, learning, innovation, and well-being programs into a holistic organizational system. The program will aim at improving employee performance, reducing negative work behavior, and ensuring sustainability in the long-term productivity. Overall, the research provides valuable information to telecommunication companies, as well as other organizations, that aim to create a resilient, innovative, and high-performing workforce that can effectively adapt to changing work conditions.

papers.title: EFFECTS OF POLITICAL MEME EXPOSURE AMONG OUT-SCHOOL-YOUTH VOTERS IN NATIONAL ELECTION LEVEL
papers.abstract: This research aimed to assess the effects of political meme exposure on the voting behavior and political engagement of several registered out-of- school youth in Lipa City, Batangas. In the upcoming elections, all the voters must be vigilant in choosing the right candidate they want to vote for. A lot of misleading information is now available on different social media platforms that can mold and affect the behavior and engagement of a voter when he is exposed to different political meme content. This study uses a quantitative research approach and a descriptive research design to describe the effects of political memes exposure on the out-of- school youth voters in Lipa City, Batangas. To allow the researchers to have a deeper understanding of the topic. Three different sampling technique such as purposive sampling, quota sampling, and convenience sampling technique was also utilized when selecting their 150 respondents on eleven barangays in Lipa City, Batangas. A set of survey questionnaires were distributed, consisted of three parts. Most of the respondents were 18-24 years old, female, roman catholic, unemployed, junior high school graduate, and utilizing the Facebook platform to access the political memes on social media. With a four-point Likert scale (Strongly agree, Agree, Disagree, and Strongly Disagree) with corresponding skills of Very Great Extent, Great Extent, Low Extent, and Very Low Extent. The results gathered in SOP 2.1 mostly agree responses which largely equated to a great extent and the results gathered in SOP 2.2 mostly disagree responses which equated to a low extent level of understanding the effects of political memes level of understanding across the voting behavior and the political engagement of the respondents.

papers.title: Tagaytay Online Linkage (TOL): An Innovative Researchers Assistance for the City Government of Tagaytay
papers.abstract: The Tagaytay Online Linkage (TOL): An Innovative Researcher's Assistance for the City Government of Tagaytay was developed to improve the process of providing localized data and zoning certifications to researchers. The study aimed to transform the manual transaction process of the Office of the City Planning and Development Coordinator (OCPDC) into a web-based system that is more efficient, accessible, and convenient for users. The study utilized the Agile Scrum Methodology in developing the web application. The development process followed seven phases: Product Backlog and Refinement, Sprint Planning, Sprint Backlog and Development, Daily Scrum, Increment and Definition of Done, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective. After completing these phases, the system underwent release and implementation. The evaluation involved 325 respondents, consisting of 295 students, 23 instructors and IT professionals, and 7 clients. The web application was assessed using the ISO/IEC 25010 Software Quality Model, which includes Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Compatibility, Usability, Reliability, Security, Maintainability, and Portability. The findings revealed that the web application obtained an overall mean score of 4.77, interpreted as Excellent. Among the evaluated criteria, Portability received the highest mean score of 4.80, indicating that the system performs effectively across different devices, operating systems, and web browsers. The results also showed high ratings in the other quality characteristics, demonstrating that the application met the needs and expectations of its intended users. Based on the findings, it was concluded that the Tagaytay Online Linkage (TOL) web application successfully achieved its objectives and provided an effective digital solution for researcher assistance. The system improved access to localized data, streamlined request processing, and supported the digital transformation initiatives of the City Government of Tagaytay. The study further confirmed that the web application meets established software quality standards and is suitable for implementation and future enhancement.

papers.title: Proposed Integration of Skills-Based Certification in the Aircraft Maintenance Technology Program
papers.abstract: The Philippine aviation maintenance industry is experiencing heightened demand for technically competent aircraft maintenance personnel, driven by fleet expansion, the growing complexity of modern aircraft systems, and workforce transition as seasoned technicians approach retirement. These conditions place increasing pressure on Aviation Maintenance Technology (AMT) programs to produce graduates with not only foundational qualifications but also validated specialized competencies aligned with current maintenance practices. In the Philippines, AMT graduates typically enter the workforce with an academic diploma and pursue licensure through the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) Aircraft Maintenance Technician examination, which confirms entry-level competency but does not formally recognize specialization in high-skill technical domains. This study aimed to propose the integration of skills-based certification into the AMT program of the National Aviation Academy of the Philippines (NAAP) to strengthen alignment between outcome-based education and industry-required technical competencies. Specifically, the study assessed the perceived competency levels of AMT graduates, identified priority skill areas for certification, examined the relationship between competency perception and industry prioritization, and developed a proposed certification integration framework. A descriptive–developmental quantitative research design was employed using a structured survey questionnaire administered to 33 aviation industry practitioners. Data were analyzed using frequency distribution, weighted mean, ranking, and Spearman rank-order correlation. Findings revealed that AMT graduates were generally perceived to have low to very low competency in advanced diagnostics and troubleshooting, non-destructive testing, and sheet metal and structural repairs, the same areas rated high to very high in industry prioritization. A significant inverse relationship between perceived competency and industry prioritization was found in advanced diagnostics and sheet metal repairs at the 0.05 significance level. Based on these findings, a multi-pathway skills-based certification framework was developed, integrating institutional workshops, industry partnerships, and intergovernmental technical collaboration to strengthen specialized competency development and improve workforce readiness among AMT graduates.

papers.title: GridZero: An Offline Bluetooth Messaging Application and Emergency Response System for Barangay Sambong, Tagaytay City
papers.abstract: Communication is essential for both daily routines and emergency assistance, yet internet interruptions in Barangay Sambong, Tagaytay City, have caused persistent disruptions between residents and local authorities. These irregular outages hinder reporting and aid requests, prolonging response times and increasing risks for vulnerable communities. To address this challenge, this study introduces GridZero as an offline messaging and emergency alert platform designed to sustain communication without internet access. The hardware development of GridZero follows the Prototyping Model, enabling iterative construction and refinement of ESP32 and LoRa nodes. Initial prototypes are deployed and tested within the actual terrain of Barangay Sambong to evaluate signal range and system performance under real-world conditions. Feedback from these trials informs successive modifications, ensuring that both hardware reliability and the app interface are optimized for local communication needs. This approach allows continuous improvement while aligning the system design with the community's environmental and emergency response requirements. The hybrid network architecture extends communication beyond the 30‑meter Bluetooth limit of smartphones by integrating Wi‑Fi Direct mesh for device‑to‑device links and ESP‑NOW for relaying data across microcontrollers at 100–200‑meter intervals. Data packets converge at a centralized gateway equipped with an SX1262 transceiver, enabling transmission across a 3‑kilometer radius through dense obstacles. A localized mobile database supports offline caching and automatic forwarding upon connection restoration, ensuring resilient communication and efficient data handling. By offloading the network relay to affordable Wi-Fi microcontrollers and utilizing a single centralized LoRa gateway, the architecture aims to eliminate the prohibitive costs of deploying expensive long-range hardware across every household. Ultimately, this hybrid hardware-software approach seeks to provide an uninterrupted, reliable emergency coordination system during catastrophic cellular outages, offering a financially viable and life-saving blueprint for localized IoT mesh networks in disaster-prone communities.

papers.title: Business Intelligence and Data Analytics on Strategic Decision-making and Organizational Development: Evidence toward Organizational Sustainable Development Goals
papers.abstract: The increasing complexity of organizational environments has compelled institutions to adopt business intelligence (BI) and data analytics (DA) as strategic tools for informed decision-making and sustainable development. This study examined the extent to which business intelligence and data analytics contribute to strategic decision-making, sustainable organizational development, and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Specifically, it assessed the implementation of BI and DA practices, the effectiveness of strategic decision-making processes, and the level of sustainable organizational development among selected organizations. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, data were collected from 400 managers, supervisors, and employees through a researcher-developed questionnaire utilizing a four-point Likert scale. Findings revealed that BI and DA implementation (M \= 3.69), strategic decision-making (M \= 3.74), and sustainable organizational development (M \= 3.77) were all rated as Very High. Correlation analysis showed significant positive relationships between BI and DA implementation and strategic decision-making (r \= .842, p < .05) and sustainable organizational development (r \= .811, p < .05). The study concludes that organizations leveraging business intelligence and data analytics demonstrate stronger decision-making capabilities and greater progress toward achieving SDGs. A sustainable data-driven organizational development framework is proposed to guide organizations in maximizing analytics for sustainable growth.

papers.title: PRACTICE OF SKILLS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASE NURSES ENROLLED IN THE DOH NURSE CERTIFICATION PROGRAM
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Infection prevention and control (IPC) is a vital component of healthcare that requires a multidisciplinary approach, as highlighted by Turale et al. (2020). In the Philippines, this is guided by the Administrative Order No. 2016-0002 entitled, “National Policy on Infection Prevention and Control in Healthcare Facilities.” Methodology This descriptive-correlation study utilized currently working nurses at selected DOH-retained tertiary hospitals who have finished the DOH Nurse Certification Program. The “Compliance with Standard Precaution Scale (CSPS)” by Dr. Lam (2010) was used to gather data. Frequency and percentage distribution, original scoring of the questionnaire's author, weighted mean, Pearson's r (correlational) and paired t-test was the statistical treatment used. Findings Results revealed that most of the infectious disease nurse were 31 to 40 years old; female; rated themselves as having a sub-optimal compliance, and their nurse supervisors rated them as having optimal compliance with standard precaution scale; they both perceived high degree of practice of skills; only the domain Prevention of Cross Infection from Person to Person is significantly correlated with age and the only domain that has statistically significant difference when the perceptions of the nurses and their supervisors were compared; no significant correlation between sex and all the domains of the degree of practice of skills toward infection prevention and control; the nurse's perceived challenges as they attain the skills required by the DOH-NCP Program were: Tedious Studying; Time Constraints; Not Knowing What You Expect You Know; and Communication Barrier. Conclusion There is general agreement between nurses and supervisors regarding IPC skills; however, subtle perceptual gaps persist in some key areas like the PCIP2P. These findings highlighted the importance of establishing joint review protocols and reflective practice tools in clinical settings. Integrating feedback mechanisms into nursing evaluations could foster stronger alignment.

keynote.speaker: Prof. John Kristoffer Q. ANDRES
keynote.title: HABing a better future: Development of New tools for Harmful Algal Bloom mitigation
keynote.bio: John Kristoffer “JK” Andres is a marine biologist and PhD candidate in Integrative and Conservation Biology at the University of Central Florida, USA. His research focuses on harmful algal blooms (HABs) with an emphasis on detection, metabarcoding, qPCR, and mitigation strategies. Specifically, his doctoral research focuses on molecular approaches for HAB monitoring and ecological effects of clay treatments for red tide mitigation. He holds an M.S. in Marine Science from the University of the Philippines Diliman and a B.S. in Biology from the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila and has an extensive experience in plankton ecology, shellfish toxin dynamics, water-quality monitoring, and marine field research. His work has been presented at national and international scientific conferences and has won an award from one of those conferences.
keynote.abstract: Algal blooms are natural phenomena that occur globally and involve the rapid proliferation of single celled planktonic algae. Some bloom causing species can produce detrimental health effects and harm to the environment and these events are known as Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs). HAB occurrences are increasing in frequency and magnitude due to several factors such as climate change and anthropogenic impacts that have produced significant economic loss by affecting fisheries (fish kills, shellfish bed closures), tourism (beach closures), and human health (poisoning, respiratory problems, etc.). Along Florida's Gulf Coast, HABs caused by the marine dinoflagellate Karenia brevis, known as red tides, have led to the loss of millions of dollars in revenue to the state. Due to their economic and environmental impacts, research scientists and management agencies are focused on finding ways to detect and to track bloom events, for better understanding of bloom event dynamics and mitigating their impacts. My research has two central aims: 1) test the efficiency of clay application to mitigate K. brevis blooms and 2) develop molecular tools to detect HAB species as well as to track changes in the broader phytoplankton community during bloom events.

papers.title: Triboelectric Rain Energy Harvesting System for Emergency Tent Lighting During Typhoon Evacuations
papers.abstract: The Philippines experiences frequent, devastating typhoons, causing power grid failures that leave evacuation centers in total darkness. Conventional backup systems like diesel generators and solar panels are often hazardous, logistically challenging, or completely neutralized during severe storms. This study addresses the critical need for resilient off-grid power by engineering a Triboelectric Rain Energy Harvesting System to autonomously maintain emergency tent lighting. The optimized TENG panel utilizes a multi-layer architecture consisting of Aluminum as the electropositive electrode and superhydrophobic Fluorinated Ethylene Propylene (FEP) as the electronegative layer to maximize charge separation. To safely manage the high-impedance alternating current generated by raindrop impacts, the system employs an LTC3588 nano-power integrated circuit to rectify and buffer the harvested energy into a 0.047F supercapacitor, which is subsequently regulated by an HW-107 smart charging module into a 1200 mAh lithium-ion battery load. A quantitative-experimental approach was utilized to optimize performance, testing five distinct electrode patterns across three inclination angles (50°, 60°, and 70°). The prototype was subjected to a custom-built rain simulator calibrated to the PAGASA severe torrential rainfall classification (66.0 mm/hr). Empirical data confirmed that the Middle Electrode configuration at a 60-degree tilt is the most efficient, achieving an initial peak voltage of 49.30 V. The finalized full-scale system yielded a stabilized open-circuit voltage of 47.16 V, a short-circuit current of 388 µA, and a power density of 49.24 mW/m². During continuous torrential rain, the system executed burst-mode trickle charges generating 0.406 mAh per hour. This completely offsets the parasitic self-discharge of the battery, achieving a net positive gain of approximately 0.38 mAh per hour. Ultimately, the TENG Energy Harvester effectively functions as an autonomous standby maintainer, ensuring emergency lighting remains at full operational readiness indefinitely without sunlight or external fuels.

papers.title: Design and Development of Food Waste Conversion Machine for Sustainable Chicken Pellet Production
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the design and development of a Food Waste Conversion Machine for Sustainable Chicken Pellet Production as an innovative solution to address the increasing volume of food waste and the rising cost of commercial poultry feeds. The machine is designed to convert food waste materials, including rice residues, vegetable scraps, and protein leftovers, into nutritious and uniform chicken feed pellets. To improve efficiency and reduce production costs, the system integrates the processes of drying, mixing, grinding, and pelletizing into a single machine. Key components include a hopper, grinder, die plate, heating system, shaft assembly, bevel gears, and an ESP32-based monitoring and control system for process regulation and performance optimization. The machine was designed using computer-aided design (CAD) software and fabricated from locally available materials such as food-grade stainless steel, aluminum alloy, and standard mechanical components to ensure affordability, manufacturability, durability, and ease of maintenance. Performance evaluation focused on pellet quality, operational reliability, production capacity, and economic feasibility. The developed system was designed to meet target feed quality parameters, including a moisture content of 8–13%, crude protein of 18–23%, crude fat of 2–6%, crude fiber of 3–5%, and ash content of 4– 7%. Economic analysis showed a projected daily production capacity of 12–16 kg of chicken pellets and an estimated payback period of 131–227 days. Results indicate that the machine can provide a practical and sustainable approach to food waste management while offering a cost-effective alternative source of poultry feed. The study demonstrates the potential of integrating waste valorization and feed production technologies to support environmental sustainability, reduce feed costs, and promote circular economy practices in agricultural communities.
