papers.title: An Integrated Map-Based Assistive Navigation Device with Sensor-Fused YOLOv11n Obstacle Detection and Semi-Autonomous Steering for the Visually Impaired
papers.abstract: Visual impairment remains a significant barrier to safe and independent mobility, particularly in developing contexts where existing assistive technologies are often fragmented and limited. To address this, the study developed an integrated map-based assistive navigation device combining Google Maps–based routing, RGB camera and ultrasonic sensor fusion, YOLOv11n-based object detection, and semi-autonomous steering assistance, supported by multimodal audio and haptic feedback and a web-based caregiver application. A multi-stage methodology was employed, including a Design Validation Interview, a Quality Assessment Test (QAT) for system performance under controlled and real-world conditions, and user evaluation using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and Post-Study System Usability Questionnaire (PSSUQ). The YOLOv11n model achieved 63.84% precision, 49.38% recall, 55.69% F1-score, 50.96% mAP@0.50, and 36.82% mAP@0.50–0.95, demonstrating adequate real-time detection when supported by sensor fusion. The web-based application obtained a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 92.0 (Promoter), indicating very high caregiver satisfaction, while the device achieved an overall PSSUQ score of 1.91 (Strongly Agree) across system usefulness, information quality, and interface quality. Overall system performance, reliability, and safety were validated through QAT, confirming the effectiveness of the integrated system. The findings show that the device successfully integrates perception, navigation, and control into a unified assistive solution, enhancing user safety, confidence, and independent mobility.

papers.title: Microview Ai: Leveraging Large Vision-Language Models in an Augmentative Raspberry Pi-Based System for Automated Urine Microscopy Analysis
papers.abstract: Existing urinalysis methods fail to deliver the combined benefits of reliability, affordability, and transparency. Manual microscopy is slow and prone to human error, while commercial automated analyzers are prohibitively expensive for small-to-mid-scale laboratories. Furthermore, automated systems often operate as "black boxes," providing diagnostic results without clear, interpretable reasoning, which limits clinical trust. The study utilized a developmental-comparative experimentation framework. The researchers designed an affordable automated prototype utilizing a Raspberry Pi 4B, an Arduino-driven motorized stage, YOLOv11 for initial coarse-grained sediment detection, and the Gemini Vision-Language Model (VLM) for the final explainable audit of Red Blood Cells (RBCs) and White Blood Cells (WBCs). The system was evaluated against the manual microscopy consensus of two licensed Registered Medical Technologists (RMTs) using seven human urine samples of varying opacities. The evaluation proves the prototype successfully balances affordability with clinical reliability, yielding a positive Cost-effectiveness rating (Grand Mean: 3.75). This low-cost approach ensures transparency; experts confirmed the Explainable AI effectively justifies its decisions (Grand Mean: 4.00, Weighted Kappa \= .600). This transparent logic,is further reinforced by a flawless digital reporting module (Grand Mean: 3.92, Weighted Kappa \= .000). Because of this hardware-software synergy, the system reliably aligned with expert analysis, achieving an Overall Clinical Concordance Rate of 78.57% and a flawless 100% detection match in clear and hazy samples. However, performance boundaries were identified exclusively in highly turbid specimens, where dense optical debris exceeded the resolving capabilities of the affordable imaging hardware. MicroView AI successfully functions as a highly cost-effective and transparent decision-support tool for routine urinalysis. By generating natural language justifications for its image recognition, the VLM effectively bridges the "black box" gap, fostering professional trust. While highly effective for clear and hazy specimens, its diagnostic yield is currently constrained in high-noise environments by the physical limits of low-cost imaging hardware.

papers.title: Development of a LoRa-Based Diving System with Integrated Real-Time Health Monitoring and Depth Tracking for Small-Scale Shellfish Divers
papers.abstract: Small-scale shellfish aquaculture in Manila Bay supports small-scale fisherfolk with annual output of 5,752.11 metric tons (BFAR, 2022), but it relies on manual diving that exposes workers to physiological hazards. Unregulated hookah and freediving practices expose divers to carbon monoxide poisoning, decompression illness, and hypoxic blackout without real-time physiological oversights or automated alerts (BFAR,2022; Chin et al, 2016; Lindholm & Lungren, 2009). International data indicates up to 75 percent of artisanal divers experience decompression sickness or related injuries. Commercial dive monitors address these dangers but remain inaccessible and require digital literacy absent in fishing communities. This study developed a low-cost tethered system integrating a MAX30102 sensor for heart rate and SpO2 monitoring, LoRa communication, and a rule-based alert mechanism. The design utilizes PCA9615 differential I2C extenders over a Cat5e cable to eliminate the diver-side microcontroller. The control circuit operates a 12V relay with a high-level trigger to process signals at the surface boat node. The system includes a mechanical tether-length alarm that functions as a physical retrieval line for emergencies. Field testing achieved 100 percent LoRa packet delivery at 5.07 kilometers with latency below 500 milliseconds under high-tide conditions, with only two HR false positives attributable to motion artifacts. The mechanical tether alarm operated flawlessly as a fail-safe retrieval mechanism. Sensor accuracy reached ±3.52 percent for heart rate and ±2.56 percent for SpO2. Results indicate that the system provides a reliable and cost-effective solution for improving diver safety in resource-constrained environments.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Leo D. Manansala
keynote.title: When Everyone has AI, What Becomes the Competitive Advantage? Toward Sustainable and Inclusive AI Innovation
keynote.bio: Leo D. Manansala, PhD is a higher-education executive, management scholar, and researcher with more than two decades of experience in academic leadership, teaching, research, and institutional administration. He currently serves as Vice Dean of the College of Professional and Graduate Studies and concurrently leads the School of Governance, Public Service, and Corporate Leadership at De La Salle University–Dasmariñas, where he is also a faculty member in Business Management. Dr. Manansala's research interests span strategic management, digital transformation, business analytics, organizational development, human capital, ESG and sustainability, entrepreneurship, consumer behavior, and technology-mediated decision-making. His research has examined digital transformation and organizational innovation, financial and operational performance, human capital, ESG and sustainability, enterprise resilience, and the influence of social media and digital platforms on consumer behavior. He serves as Editor-in-Chief of the Lasallian Journal of Business and Tourism and as an Academic Editor for PLOS ONE. He also serves as a peer reviewer for various reputable international journals, in addition to his work as a research mentor, graduate research supervisor, and academic leader. His current research agenda increasingly focuses on the intersection of technology, sustainability, and human behavior, including AI-enabled transformation, sustainable consumption, digitalization and cultural tourism, sustainability disclosure, and technology's influence on consumer choices. Through his academic, research, and leadership work, Dr. Manansala is particularly interested in one overarching question: How can technological innovation be transformed into sustainable value for organizations, institutions, and communities?
keynote.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming ubiquitous across organizations, universities, businesses, and communities. As access to generative AI becomes increasingly democratized, a critical strategic question emerges: when everyone has AI, what becomes the competitive advantage? This keynote argues that AI itself will not remain the primary source of competitive advantage. Rather, the differentiating factor will be the ability of individuals and organizations to transform access to AI into meaningful, sustainable, and inclusive value. The central proposition is simple: AI is the enabler. Capability is the differentiator. Sustainable value is the test. Drawing from research on digital transformation, organizational innovation, human capital, ESG, digitalization, technology-mediated consumer behavior, and enterprise resilience, the presentation examines how technological capabilities interact with organizational conditions, institutional environments, human judgment, and societal outcomes. Evidence from research on generative AI productivity further illustrates both the potential of AI to enhance performance and the risks of relying on AI without sufficient human judgment and critical evaluation. The keynote proposes an AI Sustainability Test centered on a single question: Does AI strengthen human capability? Does it create sustainable economic value? Does it expand social opportunity? What are its environmental costs? And is it supported by responsible institutional governance? Ultimately, the challenge is no longer simply how to adopt AI, but how to use it wisely. For researchers, educators, business leaders, and policymakers, the imperative is to move beyond asking whether AI works toward asking when it works, for whom, at what cost, and toward what kind of future. The future competitive advantage may therefore belong not to those with the most AI, but to those who can use AI without losing purpose, inclusion, resilience, and humanity.

papers.title: Evidence-Based Deep Dive into Filipino Work Styles: Integrating Competency and Personality
papers.abstract: As organizations navigate increasingly volatile operational environments, workforce capabilities serve as critical determinants of institutional resilience and governance efficacy. Utilizing a large-scale empirical dataset (N \= 52,902), this study integrates profiles from the Profiles Competency Assessment (n \= 5,525) and the DISC Personality Profiler (n \= 47,377) to map the capability and behavioral landscape of the Philippine workforce. The empirical findings reveal robust proficiencies in adaptability, teamwork, integrity, and results orientation, contrasted against pronounced developmental constraints in communication, client-centric service delivery, strategic planning, stress management, and foundational leadership. Behavioral profiling indicates a dominant prevalence of Steadiness (S) and Compliance (C) traits. Synthesizing these dimensions, the study establishes five core strategic themes for targeted Organizational Development (OD): (1) balancing malasakit with operational clarity, (2) transitioning from structural endurance to psychological safety, (3) mitigating hierarchical hesitation, (4) shifting from reactive to analytical decision-making, and (5) engineering scalable institutional structures.

papers.title: Modeling Retirement Perspectives: Work Engagement and Financial Well‑Being in Public Employment
papers.abstract: IntroductionGovernments worldwide are reconsidering retirement policies in response to demographic shifts, increasing pension obligations, and changing labor market conditions. In the Philippines, proposals to lower the optional retirement age for government employees have generated discussions regarding employee readiness and retirement preferences. Previous studies suggest that work engagement and financial well-being are important factors influencing retirement decisions. This study examined how these factors affect government employees' perspectives on lowering the optional retirement age. MethodologyThe study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design involving 267 government employees. Quantitative data were collected using the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-9), the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Financial Well-Being Scale, and a researcher-developed measure of retirement perspective. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) was used to validate the latent constructs, while Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) examined the relationships among work engagement, financial well-being, and retirement perspective. Qualitative data were subsequently gathered and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis to provide deeper insights into participants' views regarding retirement reform. FindingsResults revealed that work engagement did not directly influence agreement with lowering the optional retirement age (β \= 0.019, p \= .244). However, work engagement significantly predicted financial well-being (β \= 0.630, p \= .004). Financial well-being, in turn, significantly influenced retirement perspective (β \= –0.012, p \= .004), indicating that employees with greater financial security were more likely to support earlier retirement. Moreover, financial well-being significantly mediated the relationship between work engagement and retirement perspective (indirect effect \= –0.009, p \= .042). Qualitative findings highlighted health concerns, pension sustainability, career mobility, and institutional inequities as key considerations in retirement reform discussions. ConclusionFinancial well-being plays a critical mediating role in shaping public employees' retirement perspectives. Retirement reform policies should therefore consider not only workforce engagement but also employees' financial preparedness and broader socio-economic realities.

papers.title: Utilization of Tax Incentives, BIR Service Quality, and Tax Sanctions on MSME Tax Compliance and Business Sustainability in Malolos City During the COVID-19 Pandemic
papers.abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a vital role in the Philippine economy, yet the COVID-19 crisis put their adaptability and long-term viability to the severest of tests. In this context, the study examined how tax incentives, tax penalties, and the quality of Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) services affect both tax compliance and ongoing sustainability among MSMEs operating in Malolos City. Using a cross-sectional quantitative design, researchers gathered survey data from 79 registered firms and analyzed the results with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings showed entrepreneurs' perceptions of how serious and likely tax penalties have emerged as the strongest positive driver of compliance behavior. This result echoed the work of Tohari et al. (2021), who also reported a substantial positive link between tax sanctions and overall compliance. Unexpectedly, MSMEs rated BIR service quality negatively related to compliance, while the take-up of available incentives has a weak effect, probably because owners remain poorly informed and find application processes overly complicated (Raquiza, 2021). The research showed that during the pandemic, MSMEs in severe financial distress found that meeting their tax obligations drained resources critical for day-to-day operations, leading to a statistically significant decline in overall business sustainability (Diaz, 2022). While tax incentives were not the primary engine of higher compliance, receiving even modest relief did improve sustainability by giving firms the temporary cash cushion they desperately needed (Manipol, 2025; Alera et al., 2022). In crisis moments, firms tend to follow rules out of sheer survival, meaning that punitive measures spur faster compliance than friendly assistance, yet that same compliance can further weaken fragile balance sheets. Given these dynamics, policymakers should craft tax systems that pair realistic enforcement with immediate, measurable support, protecting the long-term viability of MSMEs while encouraging the broader, ongoing social contract of tax payment.

papers.title: Entrepreneurial Inclinations of Maritime Students: Examining Skills, Attitudes, and Aspirations Toward Business Ventures
papers.abstract: This study examined the entrepreneurial inclinations of maritime students by assessing their entrepreneurial skills, attitudes, and aspirations toward business ventures. Anchored on the Theory of Planned Behavior, the study sought to determine how entrepreneurial competencies and perceptions influence maritime students' readiness to pursue entrepreneurship as an alternative or complementary career path. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 326 maritime students enrolled at John B. Lacson Colleges Foundation-Bacolod during the academic year 2025–2026. Respondents were selected using stratified random sampling and proportionate allocation. Data were gathered through a researcher-made questionnaire validated by experts and tested for reliability, yielding a Cronbach's alpha of .938, interpreted as excellent reliability. Statistical tools utilized included mean, standard deviation, frequency distribution, rank, Mann-Whitney U Test, Kruskal-Wallis Test, and Spearman's rho. Findings revealed that maritime students generally possessed high entrepreneurial skills and favorable attitudes toward entrepreneurship. Third-year students demonstrated the highest entrepreneurial competence, indicating that entrepreneurial skills improve as students advance academically. Significant differences were found in entrepreneurial skills and attitudes by year level, while no significant differences existed by program enrolled in. Results further revealed a significant relationship between entrepreneurial skills and attitudes toward entrepreneurship, suggesting that students with stronger entrepreneurial competencies also exhibit more positive entrepreneurial perspectives. Maritime environmental protection services emerged as the most preferred future business venture, reflecting students' growing interest in sustainability and green maritime initiatives. Digital exposure, leadership experience, and entrepreneurship education were identified as major factors influencing entrepreneurial development. The study concluded that maritime students possess strong entrepreneurial potential that can be further enhanced through institutional support, entrepreneurship programs, leadership training, and industry-based entrepreneurial exposure to prepare them for diversified career opportunities beyond traditional seafaring professions.

papers.title: Sustainable Recycling Network Optimization for Plastic Packaging Waste in the Philippines Using Linear Programming
papers.abstract: Plastic packaging waste management remains a major sustainability and operational challenge in the Philippines due to increasing waste generation, limited recycling infrastructure, and rising logistics costs. This study presents a linear programming–based optimization framework for sustainable recycling network allocation of plastic packaging waste under scenario-based operating conditions. A hypothetical but operationally realistic recycling network consisting of five collection zones and three recycling facilities was developed using literature-informed waste generation rates, facility capacities, and transportation cost parameters derived from publicly available waste management and plastics circularity reports in the Philippines. The optimization model minimized total transportation cost while satisfying waste supply and facility capacity constraints. Baseline results indicated that the existing recycling configuration was infeasible because total waste generation (92 tons/day) exceeded total recycling capacity (75 tons/day). Scenario analysis demonstrated that expanding recycling capacity by 25% produced the only feasible configuration and reduced transportation cost to PHP 381.75/day. Sensitivity analyses further showed that transportation costs increased linearly with logistics cost multipliers, whereas increasing recycling capacity improved allocation flexibility and reduced system-wide transportation expenditures. The findings highlight the importance of recycling infrastructure expansion, logistics optimization, and operational planning in achieving more sustainable and economically efficient plastic waste management systems in the Philippines. Overall, the study demonstrates that linear programming provides a useful decision-support tool for evaluating recycling network performance and supporting circular economy strategies for plastic packaging waste management.

keynote.speaker: Dr. Io Mones Jularbal
keynote.title: Heritage, identity, and Artificial Intelligence: Perspectives and issues from the Cordilleras
keynote.bio: An Igorot born and raised in Baguio City with ancestral roots from the Mountain Provinces. Dr. Jularbal received his PhD from the UPD Tri-College under its Philippine studies program. His research and published works include Cordilleran and highland public policy, Northern Local Language and literatures, as well as indigenous traditions and material culture. He is currently Dean of the College of Arts and Communication, University of the Philippines Baguio where he is also faculty of the department of language and literature and researcher for the cordillera studies center (CSC).
keynote.abstract: Currently, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a tool in bolstering representation capabilities of indigenous communities in the Cordillera has received much prominence and fashionability. From image generation to song and text composition etc., AI technology has taken indigenous representation to a wider audience with vast interactive capability, but despite all this, AI has proven itself to be revolutionary on a double-edged perspective, straddling a thin line between heritage preservation and misrepresentation. My keynote presentation will take into consideration the duality of AI as potential conservator and destroyer of cultural heritage and as such, posing ethical and technical issues, risks, and challenges. At present, both Indigenous representation and Artificial intelligence are rapidly evolving and to see the intersection between the two is indeed inevitable. The potential of AI in the promotion of Indigenous knowledge and heritage constructs also exists with the reality that such a promotion can lead to misinformation, misrepresentation, and eventual erosion of cultural and life ways for many indigenous communities.

papers.title: The ELEVATE Model: An Evidence-Based Institutional Model for Sustainable E-Waste Management
papers.abstract: The increasing generation of electronic waste (e-waste) presents significant environmental and public health concerns, particularly within engineering and technical education institutions where laboratory activities frequently produce discarded electronic components. This study assessed the level of awareness and the extent of proper e-waste handling and disposal practices among the students of the College of Engineering Technology during laboratory activities and developed an evidence-based institutional model for sustainable e-waste management. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, quantitative data were collected from 231 students through a validated survey, while qualitative insights were obtained through semi-structured interviews to explain the statistical findings. Results revealed that students demonstrated a high level of awareness regarding e-waste concepts, environmental impacts, policies, and disposal procedures (M \= 3.26), yet their actual implementation of proper e-waste handling and disposal practices was only moderate (M \= 2.49). No significant relationship was found between awareness and practice, indicating that knowledge alone does not guarantee responsible environmental behavior. Significant differences in practices were observed across year levels and academic specializations, highlighting the influence of laboratory exposure and experiential learning. Major challenges included inadequate training, insufficient collection facilities, lack of standard operating procedures, and weak institutional monitoring. Based on these findings, the ELEVATE Model was developed as a comprehensive institutional framework integrating Educate, Learn, Enforce, Volunteer, Associate, Track, and Enhance to bridge the awareness–practice gap through capacity building, policy implementation, stakeholder collaboration, monitoring, and continuous improvement. The model provides a sustainable roadmap for strengthening environmental stewardship and institutionalizing effective e-waste management practices in engineering and technical education institutions.

papers.title: Sludge Content as Digital Pedagogy: A Mixed-Methods Study of Attention Span and Learning Outcomes Among Generation Alpha Students
papers.abstract: This explanatory sequential mixed-methods study arrived at the conclusion of the content dubbed "sludge" being the TikTok-native multimedia that fuses narrated tutorials with images of completely unrelated activities (e.g., Subway Surfers), which serves as an intervention contrasting Mayer's coherence principle and Sweller's cognitive load theory, all in the context of the attention span issues of the Generation Alpha students. The study surveyed 61 respondents and conducted semi-structured interview with 18 participants and 1 teacher with 1 follow-up focus group discussion consisting of 6 participants within Generation Alpha BRafeNHS students at De La Salle Santiago Zobel which is aimed at assessing the impact on attention span through focus and shifting by using the validated Attention Control Scale (α \= .90), learning engagement, and outcomes (the result of formative collocations assessments) in comparison to the traditional instruction, which was steered by the three objectives and four hypotheses expecting significant differences in attention scores, quiz performance, observed behaviors (McNemar-tested), and correlations among the different measures. The research comprised of two major phases: Phase 1 implemented quasi-experimental pre/post-testing with paired t-tests, Pearson correlations, and observational checklists as the main statistical tools; Phase 2 conducted thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews for triangulation according to Creswell's design. The rationale behind the study is to determine whether cognitive overload facilitates cognitive processes or causes a bottleneck, thus giving a clue to multimedia strategy development in the case of the Philippine classrooms that are digital-native and need a balanced approach.

papers.title: Institutional Implementation of Language Soft Skills Micro-Credentialing of Wadhwani Skilling at City College of Calamba: Basis for a Strategic Plan on Micro-Credentialing Compliance
papers.abstract: This descriptive-correlational study assessed the implementation level and regulatory compliance of the Wadhwani Language Soft Skills Development (LSSD) micro-credentialing program at City College of Calamba. The research involved 383 respondents (368 students and 15 faculty/administrators) using an 85-item validated survey measuring implementation across five operational dimensions and compliance against CHED Memorandum Order No. 01, Series of 2025 standards. Findings revealed a significant implementation paradox: students perceived high- quality delivery (M \= 3.80) while faculty assessed it substantially lower (M \= 3.26), indicating that exceptional faculty effort was compensating for systemic gaps. Institutional compliance measured M \= 3.28 (Moderately Compliant), with particular weaknesses in digital credential portability. Correlational analysis revealed a statistically significant relationship between implementation quality and compliance (r \= 0.830, p < .001), validating that implementation improvements directly enhance regulatory compliance. Based on findings, a comprehensive 24-month Strategic Plan was developed encompassing nine integrated objectives: governance formalization, technical infrastructure enhancement, faculty compensation structures, curriculum integration, employer partnerships, student access programs, quality assurance mechanisms, financial diversification, and CHED registration. The plan allocates ₱5.6 million, projecting advancement to High-Operational implementation (4.40) and Mostly-to-Fully Compliant status (4.50). This research contributes evidence-based strategic guidance for Philippine local universities implementing external micro-credential programs and demonstrates alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals for quality education and decent work.

papers.title: Level off Student Knowledge Retention on the Developed Mobile Application as an Alternative Assessment Tool in Gas Turbine Engine Subject
papers.abstract: Gamified assessments are gaining popularity for their potential to enhance knowledge retention, yet their application remains underexplored in Aircraft Maintenance Technology programs at the National Aviation Academy of the Philippines. To address this gap, a mobile game application, Engine Knows, was developed to evaluate its effectiveness in improving student learning outcomes. This study analyzed knowledge retention levels through pre- and post-test results of control (CG) and experimental groups (EG), with significant differences between the two groups tested. A quasi-experimental design was employed, involving 100 second-year students each from selected four aviation schools, divided equally into CG and EG. A customized 30-item questionnaire on Gas Turbine Engine topics was pilot tested and validated through test-retest reliability. Both groups completed a pre-test to establish baseline knowledge. The EG then undertook a gamified post-test using a pictographic approach, while the CG completed a traditional pen-and-paper post-test. Statistical treatments included mean scores and paired t-tests, with scales and verbal interpretations used to assess knowledge retention levels. Pre-test results showed no significant difference between groups, with CG scoring a mean of 18.975 and EG 19.03, both at the average level (t \= -0.143, p \= 0.887). This indicated equivalent baseline knowledge. However, post-test findings revealed substantial improvement in the EG compared to the CG. The CG's mean score of 20.505 remained at the average level, while the EG achieved a mean score of 29.395, classified as high knowledge retention. The t-value of -32.600 and p-value of 0.000 confirmed a significant difference between groups. These results suggest that gamified assessment through Engine Knows positively influenced student knowledge retention, highlighting its potential as an effective educational tool in Gas Turbine Engine subject.

papers.title: The ELEVATE Model: An Evidence-Based Institutional Model for Sustainable E-Waste Management
papers.abstract: This study investigated the relationship between primary school learners' personality traits and their academic achievement to enhance classroom management of learner diversity through a proposed Strategic Intervention Management Program. Focusing on four core dimensions—perseverance, self-discipline, motivation, and critical thinking—the research explored how these traits influence learning outcomes and identified pedagogical opportunities emerging from the challenges teachers encounter when managing diverse student profiles. Employing a descriptive-correlational research design, the study sampled 335 public primary school teachers (Grades 1–6) across 35 schools in Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province, China, during the 2023–2024 academic year. Data were gathered via a validated survey questionnaire evaluating teachers' observations of student traits and classroom challenges, while concurrent academic records measured student performance. Both descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were applied to interpret the data. The findings revealed that teachers moderately observed the four targeted personality traits in their classrooms, and a majority of the learners achieved a Good level of academic performance. Crucially, inferential analysis demonstrated a statistically significant relationship between teachers' observance of these personality traits and students' academic achievement, underscoring their vital role in scholastic success. Key opportunities identified to optimize diversity management included engineering personalized instructional materials, deploying targeted student-engagement strategies, and adopting specialized assessment tools to monitor trait development. The study concludes that systematically recognizing and supporting diverse personality traits directly fosters superior academic outcomes. Further, the proposed Strategic Intervention Management Program offers a structured framework to elevate teaching competencies, cultivate inclusive classroom dynamics, and build responsive, academically supportive learning environments.

keynote.speaker: Prof. Larry V. PADILLA
keynote.title: Beyond the Surface: A Unitive Worldview Approach to Flood System Dynamics in Barangay Landayan, San Pedro City, Laguna
keynote.bio: Larry V. Padilla is an Associate Professor of the Biology Department, College of Science, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM). He previously served as the Director of the University Research Center, the Department Chair of the Biology Department and the College Secretary of the College of Science of this university. His research interests span from harmful algal bloom mitigation and ecology, aquatic ecology, environmental assessments and monitoring, natural products, sustainability science to chronobiology of organisms. He obtained his BSc in Biology degree from PLM and his MSc in Marine Science (maj. in Marine Biology) degree from The Marine Science Institute of the University of the Philippines (UP-MSI) in Diliman. He is currently pursuing a Doctorate degree in Sustainability from the University of the Philippines – Open University after taking some course work in PhD in Biology. Larry is an educator, a marine and environmental scientist, and a researcher. As a researcher, he was able to publish several research works in scientific journals indexed in Web of Science, Scopus, and ASEAN Citation index. He is an associate member of the National Research Council of the Philippines (NRCP) among other professional and technical organizations and was also part of the pioneering batch of the National Academy of Science and Technology (NAST)- Future Science Leaders. He was one of the three recipients of the Most Outstanding Faculty Award during PLM's 50th Golden Anniversary and the Nemenzo Award in one of the National Symposium in Marine Science. Prior to teaching in PLM, he also worked as an Environmental Scientist for AECOM, a multinational consultancy firm, and as a University Research Associate at the Marine Science Institute in UP Diliman. He has also joined oceanographic research cruises in the past that traversed the inner and eastern seas of the Philippines, was involved in several environmental consultancy works, and is also serving as a biology consultant tasked as an item validator and an item writer for national admission examinations.
keynote.abstract: Flooding in the Philippines is a systemic and persistent problem affecting communities. One area consistently experiencing its devastating impacts is Barangay Landayan, San Pedro City in Laguna, a lakeshore community. It has been reported that flood waters in several areas have not subsided for several months. The root cause/s of this wicked problem has not been definitively determined, prompting ineffective actions and measures to address the issue. This study sought to determine the causes of flooding in the area to identify potential solutions and adaptations using the Unitive Worldview Framework. Geospatial analyses of selected historical maps and images to trace changes in green spaces, ecosystems, land area, and waterways, as supported by secondary data, were performed using QGIS software. Two focused discussions (FGD) were also conducted to obtain crucial insights from key informants. Findings revealed that flooding may be attributed to encroachment of waters caused by lakeshore subsidence, wetland conversion to built-up areas, loss of green ecosystem, and obstruction of waterways. Moreover, FGDs revealed anthropocentric causes of flooding clustered into three themes: problematic multi-partite planning and execution, questionable strategic disaster mitigation investments, and failed urban resilience. This study revealed that flooding in Barangay Landayan is multi-causal and a complex problem that requires appropriate and holistic interventions, mitigation measures, and adaptations by the stakeholders, with some detailed in this paper.

papers.title: GaSolve: Development of IoT-Enabled LPG Leak Detection, Valve Auto Shut-Off System, and Weight Monitoring for Household Safety
papers.abstract: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is widely used in households but poses significant risks due to leaks and lack of integrated safety responses. Existing LPG conventional safety measures may not provide immediate detection and response during leak incidents. The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies offers opportunities to improve household safety through continuous monitoring, automated control mechanisms, and real-time user notifications, thereby reducing the risks associated with LPG-related accidents. This study developed GaSolve, an automated, IoT-enabled LPG safety system with three core functions: gas leak detection, automated valve shut-off, and weight monitoring. The system utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller, MQ-6 gas sensor, and a load cell with an HX711 amplifier to continuously detect gas concentration and measure tank weight. A high-torque servo motor controls a ball valve for automatic shut-off when unsafe gas levels (Warning Level: 1000+ ppm) are detected, and a mobile application provides real-time alerts and monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate high reliability and precision across all functions. For leak detection, the system achieved 100% success rates in correctly classifying In-Use (250–1000 ppm) and Warning (1000+ ppm) concentration levels, with an overall average success rate of 81.54% for Safe (0–250 ppm) conditions. The automated shut-off mechanism responded rapidly upon detecting a warning-level leak, achieving a 100% success rate and a highly consistent mean response time of 1.00 second, which is below the 5-second target. Furthermore, the load cell demonstrated a 100% measurement accuracy in determining the tank's tare, net, and gross weights, with the real-time display and monitoring response achieving an average accuracy of approximately 99.47%. Overall, the system enhances household LPG safety by providing reliable real-time monitoring and rapid automated emergency intervention, successfully satisfying the study's specific objectives.

papers.title: Design and Development of an On-Grid Integrated System with Pulverizing, Gravimetric Dosing, and Solar Thermal-Assisted Drying for Organic Hydroponic Nutrient Production in Alfonso, Cavite
papers.abstract: This study designed, developed, and evaluated an integrated system incorporating solar thermal-assisted drying, hammer mill pulverization, and automated gravimetric dosing preparation processes for the nutrient extraction of organic hydroponic nutrient supplements from cassava leaves, banana peels, papaya peels, and fish bones. The system was developed to provide a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to commercial NPK hydroponic nutrients while promoting agricultural waste valorization. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) were employed to optimize the thermal and structural performance of the system. CFD results demonstrated airflow velocities ranging from 0.058 to 0.700 m/s and temperature distributions between 20.05 °C and 75.02 °C, confirming efficient drying conditions. FEA revealed a maximum von Mises stress of 2.77 × 10⁷ N/m², a maximum deformation of 0.3225 mm, and a factor of safety of approximately 8, indicating structural reliability. The hybrid solar dryer successfully reduced the moisture content of the raw materials to below 12% under overall average temperature of 41.9 ° C. The hammer mill pulverizer achieved a throughput capacity of 22–26 kg/hr, while the gravimetric dosing system maintained high accuracy with an error range of only -2.00% to +1.00%. Laboratory analysis of the aqueous extract showed that the optimal 1:5 and 1:10 dilutions yielded mean pH values of 4.882 and 4.928 and mean electrical conductivity (EC) values of 1.422 and 0.822 mS/cm, respectively, indicating suitability for hydroponic nutrient preparation following pH adjustment.

papers.title: AGOS: Automated Graywater Operational System for Real-Time Monitoring and Reuse in Non-Potable Applications
papers.abstract: STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM: Urban water scarcity is worsening, yet large volumes of graywater remain discarded. At Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM), the absence of a recycling and automated monitoring system causes inefficient resource utilization. This study aimed to develop and evaluate AGOS, an IoT-integrated graywater system to treat, monitor, and reuse graywater for non-potable applications like irrigation and cleaning. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY: An experimental design utilizing Agile methodology was employed. A microcontroller-based prototype featuring a multi-stage filtration loop and UV-C disinfection was developed. ESP32-integrated sensors monitored turbidity, pH, and TDS. A purposive sampling technique facilitated a four-week pilot test at a residential setup and PLM's Gusaling Villegas. A mobile dashboard was evaluated via observation checklists, and sensor readings were validated against certified laboratory results. SUMMARY OF THE FINDINGS: Pilot testing revealed high sensor accuracy, with percentage errors well below the 5% tolerance limit. The filtration process significantly improved water quality, achieving an 85.34% reduction in turbidity and a 70.50% reduction in TDS. The mobile application passed all functionality tests, delivering zero-latency real-time monitoring and automated alerts. Over 28 days, the system successfully recovered 514.479 liters of treated graywater. CONCLUSION: The study successfully met its objectives. The AGOS prototype effectively treated graywater, restoring critical quality parameters to safe non-potable standards. The mobile application served as a highly reliable operational hub for data logging and real-time alerts. Ultimately, the decentralized system proved to be an operationally effective solution for institutional water conservation and reuse. RECOMMENDATION: To enhance the system, future researchers should expand water quality assessment by integrating sensors for a broader range of potential contaminants. Scaling the prototype for larger institutional deployment and direct integration into building distribution networks is advised. Additionally, conducting long-term durability testing and exploring renewable energy sources will maximize the system's operational sustainability and efficiency.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in BIM under ISO 19650
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Building Information Modeling (BIM) by extending conventional information management and automation capabilities throughout the building life cycle. This paper examines the integration of AI technologies within BIM processes through the framework of the ISO 19650 series, emphasizing their contribution to information management, project coordination, design optimization, construction planning, and asset operation. The study is based on an extensive review and comparative analysis of current scientific literature, international standards, and commercially available AI-enabled BIM applications. It identifies the principal AI methods applicable to BIM, including machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, generative design, and predictive analytics, and evaluates their relationship with BIM dimensions and the information management processes defined by ISO 19650. The analysis demonstrates that AI significantly enhances BIM by improving data processing, automating repetitive tasks, supporting informed decision-making, and increasing the efficiency and quality of project delivery. While AI applications are already widely used for design coordination, clash detection, cost estimation, scheduling, and document generation, their implementation remains fragmented and faces challenges related to interoperability, data quality, standardization, governance, and organizational adoption. The paper further discusses future opportunities for integrating AI into higher BIM dimensions and across the complete ISO 19650 information management framework. The findings suggest that ISO 19650 provides an appropriate organizational basis for the systematic implementation of AI in BIM environments, supporting the transition toward more intelligent, data-driven, and sustainable construction processes.

papers.title: Computational Study on Air Vorticity Distributions in Kitchen Rooms using k–ε Turbulence Model
papers.abstract: Indoor air pollutants are easily dispersed in the air and become trapped in turbulent airflow due to the formation of air vorticity. In confined spaces like the kitchen, vorticity formations are influenced by natural ventilation and physical obstructions that interfere with airflow. This is always a global health challenge linked to SDG 3, Health and Well-being, and has a direct impact on SDG 11, Sustainable Cities and Communities, regarding safe and healthy housing. This study aims to compare the air vorticity distributions in kitchen rooms using k–ε turbulence model, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method. The comparison focuses on the magnitude and location of vorticity shown in spatial and temporal distributions using descriptive comparative analysis. Results reveal that the number and size of vortical structures formed are influenced by the presence and position of the sink and refrigerator, which acted as barriers and stagnation points. In Case 1, many vortical structures formed, with pronounced vorticity magnitudes near the walls and between the sink corners and refrigerator. High vorticity magnitudes were observed at the door and window edges. In Case 2, a kitchen room without a window, fewer but larger vortical structures appeared due to the presence of barriers. A more uniform vorticity pattern was observed from 20.0 seconds to 60.0 seconds across most of the flow domain. These results highlight the relationship between airflow dynamics and vortical structures in the kitchen. This research provides ways for architectural designs that promote healthier indoor environments and sustainable urban living.

papers.title: Type M Electric Vehicles (EVs) As a Potential Alternative for a Cleaner and Sustainable Urban Transport System in the Philippines
papers.abstract: This study examined the factors influencing the slow acceptance of Type M electric vehicles (EVs) in Metro Manila and identified strategies to help accelerate its adoption within the context of sustainable transportation modernization in the Philippines, as grounded on diffusion and use of technology theories. It employed a quantitative cross-sectional research design using survey responses from 387 valid respondents composed of residents and transients in Metro Manila. Descriptive statistics, Spearman rho correlation, and multiple regression analyses were utilized to examine the relationships among seven (7) constructs. Findings revealed that although 79.63% of respondents expressed willingness to adopt Type M EVs, only 4.69% currently owned one, indicating a significant gap between favorable perception and actual adoption behavior. The slow acceptance of Type M EVs was primarily attributed to high vehicle acquisition cost, limited charging infrastructure, concerns regarding battery safety and reliability, uncertainty on resale value, and low consumer confidence toward relatively unfamiliar EV technology. Social influence, particularly from family members and relatives, significantly shaped behavioral intention, highlighting the collectivist nature of Filipino consumer behavior. The study concludes that acceptance of type M EVs as an alternative transport system for urban areas requires expanding charging infrastructure, strengthening non-fiscal incentives, improving public education and safety awareness campaigns, promoting family-oriented and community-based engagement, and encouraging local EV manufacturing to reduce purchase costs. Overall, EV adoption in Metro Manila is shaped not only by technological performance but also by economic, institutional, cultural, and social factors associated with sustainable urban mobility.

papers.title: Electrifying Mobility: Exploring the Electric Vehicle Transition of the Philippine Automotive Industry
papers.abstract: The recent conflict between the coalition of the United States and Israel against Iran has resulted in a sudden rise in oil prices to unprecedented heights. Gasoline and diesel breached the 100-peso mark due to growing insecurity surrounding oil-based fuels, following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Private car owners, as well as public utility vehicle operators and drivers, faced this crisis without adequate protection or the capacity to shoulder the massive increase in operating costs. This challenging scenario led to a sharp decline in motor vehicle operations, which disrupted the country's transportation system. The automotive market was also affected, with sales of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles declining. This situation reflects the broader problem of the oil regime—a resource structure heavily shaped by geopolitics and its finite nature. However, in the automotive sector, the limited supply of oil has also created opportunities for alternative engine technologies that have matured significantly over the past two decades. Despite the decline in ICE vehicle sales in the Philippines, overall automotive consumption has not faltered. Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained market share in recent years and are now experiencing massive demand due to the increasing volatility of fuel prices. This research explores this phenomenon through an analytical critique of the neoliberal political-economic model applied in the Philippines. By examining the steady rise in EV consumption, the paper discusses the potential for the country to align its industrial capacity with the growth of the EV sector. As a result of rising oil prices, the nation and its government have already begun transitioning toward a possible EV boom. Overall, this research connects the issues of the oil regime with the Philippines' industrial potential in pivoting toward electrification.

papers.title: Regulatory Capture and the 69% Premium: Institutional Failure in the Philippine Sugar Industry – Implications for Responsible Governance
papers.abstract: Introduction. Sustainable economies depend on governance systems that allocate resources equitably and remain open to innovation. The Philippine sugar industry challenges this ideal: despite ranking among the world's top producers, Filipino consumers pay prices averaging 69 percent above world market levels. This paper argues that the premium is not a market failure but a designed outcome, the product of self-reinforcing institutional mechanisms that entrench rent extraction while systematically excluding the most vulnerable stakeholders from reform. Methodology. This study employs institutional analysis grounded in primary and secondary sources. Primary sources include Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) Sugar Orders from 2021-2026, monthly price data, supply-demand reports, Executive Order No. 18 (1986), and Republic Acts 809 and 10659. The analysis proceeds through historical tracing, documentary analysis of SRA allocation and pricing data, and structural inference where direct evidence is constrained by the opacity the system itself produces. An event study design measures millgate price movements across three-month windows before and after major Sugar Orders. Findings. The paper introduces the Triple Lock framework: regulatory capture (planters and millers control the SRA board while consumers hold no seats); path dependency (the quedan system persists despite five consecutive years of zero A-sugar allocation); and an innovation tax (the fixed 70/30 milling split under RA 809 suppresses extraction rates to 78 percent against Australia's 92 percent). Costs fall concretely on consumers paying PHP 102 per kilogram, small bakeries reformulating products or closing, smallholder planters incurring negative farm returns, seasonal workers earning below minimum wage, and children in sugar households exhibiting stunted growth. Conclusion. Reform is sequenced, not optional. SRA board restructuring must precede cane purchase reform and import liberalization, as a captured regulator will administratively neutralize both. Resilient, inclusive economies are built not merely through policy change, but through dismantling the institutional machinery that makes extraction structurally rational.

papers.title: Social Security in the Informal Economy: Barriers to SSS Participation and Retirement Preparedness Among Women in Sari-Sari Store Businesses
papers.abstract: Despite the Social Security System's (SSS) mandate to provide long-term financial security, informal workers continue to face substantial barriers to social security coverage and participation. This study examined how the everyday economic circumstances of women engaged in sari-sari store businesses influence their participation in the SSS. A qualitative multiple case study design was employed, utilizing pakikipagkuwentuhan, an indigenous method grounded in informal sharing of stories, among five women aged 49–57 who were involved in managing sari-sari stores in Barangay San Jose, Navotas City. The data were analyzed through cross-case analysis to identify recurring themes and significant variations across participants' experiences. The findings revealed that participants perceived retirement as an uncertain process shaped primarily by their financial preparedness, family obligations, and the continued need to work for their livelihood. Their participation in the SSS was constrained by limited income, insufficient time and information, and intergenerational obligations, resulting in irregular or minimal contributions. Although participants recognized the value of SSS benefits, they prioritized meeting their families' immediate needs and investing in property over participation in formal retirement systems. These findings underscore gaps in social protection coverage and highlight the need for more inclusive and context-specific social security policies that account for the lived experiences of women in the informal economy.

keynote.speaker: Dr. David Paul RAMOS
keynote.title: Simulating the Future: An Outcomes-based and Sustainable Approach to Preparing Future-Ready Nurses
keynote.bio: Dr. David Paul R. Ramos is an Associate Professor III and former Dean of the College of Nursing at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila. He holds a Doctor of Philosophy in Nursing Education, a Master's in Nursing Education from the University of the Philippines Manila, and a Master of Arts in Nursing major in Nursing Administration. A registered nurse with clinical experience in perioperative nursing, he has devoted more than two decades to nursing practice, education, research, and academic leadership. Dr. Ramos has authored and co-authored studies on nursing education, academic motivation, organizational commitment, exercise dependence, and data privacy. His scholarly work has been presented at national and international conferences, including the Sigma Nursing International Nursing Research Congress in Seattle, Washington. He is an Associate Member of the National Research Council of the Philippines and previously served as a Board Director of the Philippine Nurses Association–NCR Zone 1 and Vice President of the Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing–Phi Gamma Chapter. His professional interests include simulation-based nursing education, perioperative nursing, curriculum development, evidence-based teaching, research, and educational innovation. Through his work, he continues to advocate for transformative learning experiences that prepare future nurses to provide safe, competent, compassionate, and responsive care.
keynote.abstract: Preparing future-ready nurses requires educational approaches that can address limited clinical placements, resource constraints, and the increasing complexity of healthcare practice. This plenary presentation examines simulation-based nursing education as an outcomes-based, innovative, and sustainable strategy for strengthening clinical readiness and preparing nurses to contribute to resilient and inclusive communities. This presentation describes the integration of a structured, low-fidelity perioperative simulation module into third-year Adult Health Nursing. Guided by Bondy's Clinical Performance Path Model, the module was designed to support students' progression from assisted toward supervised clinical performance. It combined prebriefing, skills stations, role-based operating-room scenarios, structured debriefing, and competency-based evaluation. Learners managed simulated situations involving breaks in sterile technique, incorrect surgical counts, intraoperative bleeding, patient-safety risks, prioritization, and interdisciplinary communication. Pilot qualitative validation based on student narratives indicated that participants exposed to simulation perceived stronger clinical understanding, confidence, procedural skills, communication, teamwork, and ability to connect theory with practice. Narratives from students without simulation exposure reflected greater dependence on lectures, return demonstrations, observation, and clinical-instructor guidance, together with continuing difficulty applying knowledge in realistic situations. These findings support the curricular value of structured simulation while remaining limited to students' reported experiences rather than controlled measures of effectiveness. Such applications must remain ethical, transparent, culturally responsive, and educator-guided. By enabling safe repetition, reducing exclusive dependence on scarce clinical placements, and permitting locally developed, resource-conscious learning experiences, simulation can advance sustainability and educational inclusion.

papers.title: Building Resilient Communities Through Inclusive Health Innovation: Perceived Roles of Physical Therapists in Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
papers.abstract: Introduction: The Philippines is among the world's highest-risk countries and it is facing a huge challenge in terms of innovation in its Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) systems. Physical therapists (PTs), who are experts in movement and rehabilitation, are still mostly left out from local disaster management teams. This paper explores the potential solution to such a gap through the evaluation of the perceived readiness and roles of PTs in the four phases of DRRM in the City of Manila. Methods: This study utilized a descriptive cross-sectional quantitative research design. A validated questionnaire on DRRM was administered to 83 respondents, however, only 50 PT respondents were included in the study. Frequency, mean, and standard deviation were used to analyze the quantitative data of the study. Findings: Majority of the participants (96%) were very positive about further training in DRRM and 72% of them were confident in their ability to be able to render professional PT during disaster situations. There was a very high level of agreement among participants on their roles in recovery, evacuation planning for healthcare facilities and preparedness, response, and evacuation planning for vulnerable populations. Even with this preparedness, only 24% of them have taken part in disasters by volunteering, suggesting a systemic disconnect between the capacity of PTs and institutional inclusion. Conclusion: Formal DRRM integration of PTs, especially for the elderly, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups is both an evidence-based and doable measure to create the resilient, inclusive, and future-ready communities that are in line with the Sendai Framework and Sustainable Development Goals 3 and 11. AI-based DRRM training programs and digital deployment tools should be the subject of the future study to understand their role in extending this integration to other disaster-prone cities in the Philippines.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Early Breast Cancer Detection: A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Approach to Benign and Malignant Mammogram Classification
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, highlighting the importance of early and accurate detection. Mammography is widely recognized as the primary imaging modality for breast cancer screening; however, image interpretation can be time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated the potential of deep learning techniques to assist radiologists by automating image analysis and improving diagnostic efficiency. This study developed and evaluated a deep learning-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the binary classification of mammographic images into benign and malignant categories. The dataset comprised publicly available mammograms containing both benign and malignant cases. Images were preprocessed and augmented prior to model training using a custom CNN architecture consisting of four convolutional layers, max-pooling operations, and fully connected classification layers. Model performance was assessed using multiple evaluation metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, balanced accuracy, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Cohen's Kappa, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC). The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 91.18%, sensitivity of 95.83%, specificity of 81.75%, precision of 91.42%, F1-score of 93.57%, balanced accuracy of 88.79%, MCC of 0.7977, Cohen's Kappa of 0.7955, and an AUC of 0.976. To enhance interpretability, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to visualize image regions contributing to classification decisions. The resulting heatmaps demonstrated that the CNN focused on anatomically relevant breast tissue structures rather than background regions, providing evidence of clinically meaningful feature extraction. These findings indicate that deep learning-based CNN models can serve as effective decision-support tools for early breast cancer detection and may contribute to improving screening efficiency and diagnostic confidence in mammographic analysis.
